Not part of the fix, just cosmetic if the fork moves.
- Actually load-bearing in `src/`: `src/api/routes/update_check.py:21` (`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/javastraat/meshpoint/main/src/version.py` — the real "Check for updates" version fetch) and `src/api/update/install_status.py:219` (same `raw.githubusercontent.com/javastraat/meshpoint/` pattern, used during install-status/progress tracking). These two are the ones an override would actually need to redirect.
- `src/remote/executors.py:19` (`GITHUB_REPO = "https://github.com/javastraat/meshpoint.git"`) is DEAD CODE right now — grepped the whole file and every importer (`upstream_client.py` only imports the `execute_*` functions, not this constant); `execute_apply_update()` (line 91) runs `git pull origin main`, relying on whatever remote `origin` is already configured in `.git/config` at clone time, never reading this constant. Either wire it in as part of this feature or remove it as unused.
- Unrelated, don't touch: `serial_config_routes.py`/`meshcore_config_routes.py` hit `api.github.com/repos/{meshtastic/firmware,meshcore-dev/MeshCore}/releases/latest` for THIRD-PARTY firmware version checks, not our own repo.

User's proposed design: keep a hardcoded default (current `javastraat/meshpoint`), but if a base-URL key is present in `local.yaml`, use that instead — so a user running their own fork can redirect self-update/version-check without a code change. Needs: (1) a new config field (e.g. under `update_check:` in `AppConfig`/`default.yaml`, something like `repo_base_url` or `github_repo`, defaulting to the current hardcoded value), (2) `update_check.py:21` and `install_status.py:219` both switch from a hardcoded f-string/literal to reading this config value, (3) decide whether to also wire `executors.py`'s currently-dead `GITHUB_REPO` into the same config value (for consistency) or drop it, (4) since `git pull origin main` in `execute_apply_update` relies on the git remote itself (not this constant), an override wouldn't change the actual `git pull` source unless the remote is also repointed — worth clarifying with the user whether the override is meant to affect just the update-CHECK (version string fetch) or the actual `git pull` too, since those are two different mechanisms today. Not started — revisit when picked back up.

**DONE 2026-07-16: full API endpoint auth audit + SDR start/stop/tune admin-gate fix.** User asked "are all api endpoints protected for viewer and admin" — spawned an Explore agent to enumerate every `@router.*` decorator across all ~32 `src/api/routes/*.py` files plus `server.py`, cross-referenced against the three auth deps in `src/api/auth/dependencies.py` (`require_auth`=any session, `require_admin`=admin only, `optional_auth`=never rejects). Structural finding: `server.py:435` builds `protected = [Depends(require_auth)]` and applies it via `app.include_router(..., dependencies=protected)` to 34 routers at once, so "no per-route Depends" in those files is NOT a gap — it's viewer-open by the router-level floor, with `Depends(require_admin)` layered on top per-route for actual write/action endpoints. 9 route files are included WITHOUT that blanket dependency (`auth_routes, metrics_routes, identity_routes, auth_config_routes, public_radar_routes, terminal_routes, update_routes, backup_routes, dangerous_routes`) — manually verified every route in all 9 individually (this is where a missing `Depends` would mean a FULLY public route, worse than the router-floor case) and all check out: admin-only where expected (`update_routes` all 10 admin, `backup_routes` all 3 admin, `dangerous_routes` both admin, `auth_config_routes` all 3 admin, `terminal_routes`'s 2 HTTP routes admin + its `/ws` websocket does a manual `claims.role != ROLE_ADMIN` check before accepting the PTY), and the few genuinely-open ones are intentional (`/api/auth/setup`+`/login`+`/logout` pre-auth by necessity, `/api/identity` uses `optional_auth` with a strict field allowlist so `/login` can render pre-session, `/api/public/recent_rx` deliberately scrubbed+rate-limited).

**Only real gap found: SDR `start`/`stop`/`tune` actions were viewer-reachable, not admin-only** — `dab_routes.py` (`POST /tune`, `/stop`), `rtl433_routes.py` (`POST /start`, `/stop`), `listener_routes.py` (`POST /tune`, `/stop`), and all 3 `pager_routes.py` sub-routers (P2000/pagers/POCSAG `POST /start`, `/stop`) had zero per-route `Depends`, relying only on the router-level `require_auth` floor — inconsistent with every other state-changing endpoint in the app (`messages.send`, `update.apply`, `backup.restore`, etc.) which all require admin. FIXED: added `_claims: SessionClaims = Depends(require_admin)` to all 8 action routes (imports added: `from src.api.auth.dependencies import require_admin` + `from src.api.auth.jwt_session import SessionClaims`, matching the exact pattern already used in `backup_routes.py`/`update_routes.py`). Read-only `GET /status` and `GET /stream`/`/stream/{sid}` on the same listeners deliberately left viewer-open (no state change). **DONE 2026-07-16: configurable self-update repo, derived from `origin` instead of hardcoded — supersedes the "IDEA, NOT YET BUILT" entry above.** User asked where `github.com/javastraat/meshpoint` lives in the code (wanted to eventually redirect self-update to their own fork); when shown the real `/opt/meshpoint/.git/config` (`[remote "origin"] url = https://github.com/javastraat/meshpoint.git`), user proposed deriving the repo from that instead of adding a new config key — "if i clone it and use it it will point to my git automatically". Agreed and built it.

New `src/remote/repo_source.py`: `resolve_owner_repo()` reads `.git/config` directly via `configparser` (repo root from the existing `src/backup/paths.py::resolve_meshpoint_root()` — `MESHPOINT_DIR` env var or cwd, already used elsewhere for the same Pi-vs-Mac-checkout portability problem; deliberately NOT a `git remote get-url` subprocess, so it sidesteps the dubious-ownership/safe.directory check entirely). Parses both `https://github.com/owner/repo.git` and `git@github.com:owner/repo.git` remote forms; only trusts the parse when the host is actually `github.com` (raw.githubusercontent.com has no equivalent for other hosts). Falls back to **`KMX415/meshpoint`** (the upstream project user specified, not `javastraat` — the fallback should point at the canonical project, not any one fork's maintainer) on any failure: no origin, unreadable config, non-GitHub host, missing `.git` entirely. Result cached module-level for the process lifetime (git remote doesn't change without a restart, same reasoning as `update_check.py`'s existing 300s version-check cache). `github_raw_url(branch, path)` helper builds the raw.githubusercontent.com URL from the resolved repo.

Wired into the two previously load-bearing hardcoded spots: `update_check.py:21`'s `_VERSION_URL` and `install_status.py:219`'s `fetch_remote_version_sync()` both now call `github_raw_url(...)`. Per user's explicit "7. just delete" — `executors.py:19`'s dead `GITHUB_REPO` constant (never read anywhere, confirmed by grep) removed outright, no replacement needed since `execute_apply_update()`'s `git pull origin main` already reads the real git remote directly.

Confirmed with the user that this doesn't touch branch **selection** at all — the Stable/Custom channel picker and its `custom_branch` value flow untouched; this only prepends the repo name onto whatever branch text was already resolved.

Follow-up same session (user: "will it populate the branches automatically... i know KMX415/meshpoint has branches"): new `GET /api/update/branches` (`update_routes.py`, admin-gated like every other route in that router) fetches `api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches` for the install's own **resolved** repo (not hardcoded to KMX415 — follows the same origin-derived owner/repo as everything else this session), sorted main/master-first then alphabetically, cached 5 minutes — mirrors `serial_config_routes.py`'s existing firmware-release-check fetch/cache pattern exactly (stdlib `urllib.request`, `Accept: application/vnd.github+json`, timeout=10, bare `except Exception` → `None` → cached `"Could not reach GitHub"` error, no shared helper per this repo's established small-helper-duplication convention).

**DONE 2026-07-20: ADS-B air traffic tab (dump1090).** User asked for a new RTL-SDR tool: `dump1090` (MalcolmRobb/dump1090 fork) for 1090ES aircraft tracking, installed by `scripts/install.sh` and exposed as a new Listener tab.

Install.sh (section 10, between rtl_433 and welle.io — all later sections renumbered 11→25): clones and builds from source since upstream has no apt package. **Root cause found live on the Pi**: first build attempt failed at the link step with "multiple definition of `Modes`/`tDF`" — this 2016-era codebase declares its globals in `dump1090.h` without `extern` (old-style tentative definitions), which GCC 10+ breaks by defaulting to `-fno-common`. Fixed with `make EXTRACFLAGS=-fcommon` (a variable the Makefile already threads into every compile rule). Also: upstream's Makefile has no `install` target at all, so binaries are copied to `/usr/local/bin` by hand (`install -m 755 dump1090 view1090 ...`) after the build.

Backend/frontend built to match the existing RTL-SDR tab architecture (rtl433/DAB+ patterns, see `src/audio/sdr_registry.py` for the shared dongle-exclusivity design): new `src/audio/adsb_listener.py` (`AdsbListener`, owner name `"adsb"`) spawns `dump1090 --net --net-http-port 8081` (port chosen to avoid the dashboard's own 8080 and DAB+'s 7979) and polls dump1090's own embedded webserver's `/data.json` every 2s — modeled on `DabListener`'s `/mux.json` polling rather than `Rtl433Listener`'s stdout-JSON-per-line parsing, since dump1090's HTTP endpoint already returns a clean full snapshot of currently-tracked aircraft (hex, flight, squawk, altitude, speed, track, lat/lon, messages, seen) with no CSV/stdout parsing needed. Deliberate UX deviation from the rtl433/pager tabs' append-only message log: ADS-B renders as a table keyed by ICAO hex that updates in place (a successful poll wholesale-replaces the table so aircraft that left range disappear; a failed poll leaves the previous table showing) — matches how dump1090's own bundled map view and every other ADS-B UI presents this data, judged more useful than literally mirroring rtl433's flowing log. New `src/api/routes/adsb_routes.py` (`GET/POST /api/adsb/*`, same start/stop/status shape as rtl433/dab routes), wired into `src/api/server.py` (import, global, lifespan init/shutdown, router include). Frontend: new `frontend/js/adsb_panel.js` (`AdsbPanel`, reuses `PagerPanel`'s `.pager-status`/`.pager-actions`/`.pager-count` CSS classes for a consistent status-header look, custom `.adsb-table` styles added to `listener.css`), wired into `frontend/js/listener_panel.js` as an eighth tab positioned right after RTL433 and before DAB+ Config in the tabbar (tab button, content div, panel instantiate/mount, `_showActiveTab`/`_switchTab`/`hide()` branches, and the `dongle_owner` busy-label maps in both `listener_panel.js` and `pager_panel.js`'s shared `_DONGLE_OWNER_LABELS`).

Verified: `bash -n` on install.sh; Python `ast.parse` on the two new backend files plus `server.py`; a stubbed-logic script exercising `AdsbListener`'s `/data.json`→status transform (flight-name trimming, `validposition`/`validtrack` nulling, seen-ascending sort) against a fake dump1090 payload — output shape confirmed correct; `node --check` on all three touched/new JS files; `ChangelogParser.parse_file()` confirmed the new CHANGELOG bullet still parses.

Its `public_html/planeObject.js` (dump1090's own bundled Google-Maps web UI) has a `funcGetIcon()` that builds a rotated `google.maps.Symbol` plane icon colored by squawk (7500 hijack, 7600 radio failure, 7700 general emergency = distinct colors, "seen > 15" = stale/dimmed) — borrowed the IDEA (rotate-by-track, the same 3 squawk colors, the same 15s staleness threshold) but not the code itself, since it's tied to the Google Maps API which this app doesn't use; the actual marker here is a small inline SVG arrow (feather-icons style, matching the sidebar's own stroke-based icon language at `frontend/index.html`'s `.sidebar__icon` svgs) rotated via CSS `transform`.

**New feature, same conversation: ADS-B flight-detail modal on row click.** User: "can you open a modal and show info about the flight, have a look in dump1090 how they did it to get flight data etc, plane foto they did alot of lookup data i think". Spawned an agent to check the actual bundled dump1090 web UI first rather than assume — finding: this dump1090 fork (upstream MalcolmRobb, the old FlightAware-derived C decoder, not dump1090-fa/tar1090/readsb) does **none** of that. No photo API, no registration/type/manufacturer database (bundled or remote), no route lookup anywhere in `planeObject.js`/`script.js` — `funcGetIcon()` only builds a generic squawk/altitude-colored marker, and the only enrichment-adjacent thing is `script.js` building three plain `<a href>` outbound links (fr24.com, flightstats.com, flightaware.com) from the flight number for a human to click manually. So "how dump1090 did it" turned out to be "they didn't" — had to source real lookups elsewhere.

Chose two free, no-API-key public services also used by other open-source dump1090-derived web UIs (tar1090 etc): **hexdb.io** (`/api/v1/aircraft/{hex}` for registration/type/manufacturer/operator, `/api/v1/route/icao/{callsign}` for origin-destination ICAO route, `/api/v1/airport/icao/{icao}` to resolve those codes to friendly names) and **planespotters.net** (`/pub/photos/hex/{hex}` for a real photo + photographer credit). Both called directly from the browser via `fetch` — no new backend endpoint, since these are public CORS-enabled read APIs, same as how tar1090-style tools do it client-side. **Did not guess the response schemas** — used `WebFetch` to hit all four live endpoints first and confirm exact field names before writing any parsing code (this mattered: fields are non-obvious/non-guessable — `RegisteredOwners`, `ICAOTypeCode`, `OperatorFlagCode`, route as a single hyphenated `"EDDF-EGLL"` string not separate origin/destination fields, `thumbnail_large.src`/`.size.{width,height}`, `photographer`).

New `frontend/js/adsb_flight_modal.js` (`AdsbFlightModal`, singleton, reuses the `.pdm-overlay`/`.pdm-modal` shell and `PacketDetailModal`'s `_buildLayer`/`_row` pattern). Shows an always-available "Flight" layer built purely from the already-in-hand row data (hex, squawk, altitude, speed, track, position, messages, seen — no fetch needed), plus three independent best-effort layers (Aircraft, Route, Photo) that start as "looking up…" and get replaced in place as each of the three fetches resolves — one failing/404ing (common for GA/military/older aircraft not in either database) never blocks the other two, rendered as a plain "not found"/"no photo found", not an error state. `adsb_panel.js` wired up: rows gained `data-adsb-hex` + `.adsb-table__row` (cursor pointer, hover highlight — new CSS in `listener.css`), a single delegated click listener on the tbody (`_onRowClick`) looks the clicked hex up in `this._aircraft` (now cached every `_render()`, previously only used transiently) and calls `window.AdsbFlightModal.show(aircraft, metric)`.

Verification: since this has zero backend/Python surface (pure frontend + external API calls) and no live antenna session this turn, built a minimal custom DOM+fetch stub in Node (no jsdom available on this Mac) that `eval()`s the real `adsb_flight_modal.js` source against **mocked responses matching the exact live-confirmed API shapes** — confirmed correct rendering for the happy path (real Lufthansa D-AILI/A319 test data: registration/type/manufacturer/operator, Frankfurt→Heathrow route with both airport names resolved, photo + photographer + planespotters link all appear correctly) AND every fallback path (unknown hex → "not found in hexdb.io", blank callsign → "no callsign", empty photo array → "no photo found"). `node --check` clean on all touched/new JS. `ChangelogParser.parse_file()` still parses (26 sections) after the new bullet. README's ADS-B bullet extended to mention the flight-detail modal and both lookup services. **LIVE-VERIFIED on the Pi, same conversation**: user screenshot of a real click-through — AFR99ZC (F-HBLI, an Air France HOP Embraer EMB-190) resolved registration/type/manufacturer/operator, the EHAM→LFPG (Schiphol→Paris CDG) route with both airport names, and a real photo of the airframe, all from the Pi's own network. "verified lookup very cool." Feature fully closed, external API reachability from the Pi confirmed.

**Follow-up, same conversation: map marker click opens the same modal.** User: "when clicking on the mp on a plane can you open the same modal as clicking on a row?" — `adsb_map_modal.js`'s marker gained a `click` handler (`marker.on('click', ...)`) alongside its existing hover tooltip, calling the same `window.AdsbFlightModal.show(a, metric)` the table row uses. Caught one real correctness issue before it shipped: since the flight modal can now stack on top of the map modal, both bind their own `keydown` Escape-close listener to `document` — without a fix, one Escape press would fire both listeners and close both modals at once instead of just stepping back one layer. Fixed with `e.stopImmediatePropagation()` in `AdsbFlightModal._onKeyDown` before its own `close()` (listeners on the identical event target fire in registration order regardless of plain `stopPropagation`; only `stopImmediatePropagation` prevents a later-registered sibling listener on the same node from running). `node --check` clean on both touched files.

**Second follow-up, same conversation: broken photo image handled gracefully.** User pasted a real click-through (CES772, hex 780f3e, China Eastern 777 B-7365) where registration/type/operator/route/photo-credit all resolved correctly but the actual `<img>` came up as a broken-image glyph (just the `alt="Aircraft photo"` text showing) -- the hotlinked planespotters.net thumbnail (`t.plnspttrs.net`, a BunnyCDN-fronted domain separate from `api.planespotters.net`) failed to load in-browser even though the metadata fetch succeeded. Checked the CDN directly with `curl -I` (with/without a referer, different user-agents) — no hotlink protection found, so this reads as a one-off transient failure rather than a systemic block, but added a proper fallback regardless since a bare broken-image icon is bad UX either way. Rewrote the photo block (`adsb_flight_modal.js`) from an HTML-string `insertAdjacentHTML` row into a real DOM-built `_photoRow()` (new `_replaceLayer`/row-type support for `{el}` alongside the existing `{html}`/`{key,val}` shapes) specifically so an `error` listener could be attached to the `<img>` — on failure it swaps the image out for "Photo failed to load in this browser -- view on planespotters.net" (still a working link, since the JSON metadata with `photo.link` was already confirmed present). User immediately followed up with a second real click-through (a later aircraft, CES772 again after a refresh or a different aircraft — China Eastern 777) showing the photo rendering correctly: "looks great sofar" — confirms the original failure was transient, and the new fallback path is in place for if it recurs. `node --check` clean.

**Third follow-up, same conversation: flight trails.** User asked "how hard woould it be to have trails on the planes" (exploratory) — answered honestly: easy, no backend change needed, positions already stream every 2s poll; main tradeoff is trails only persist while the modal stays open (state resets on close since Leaflet gets torn down/rebuilt fresh each `show()`). User: "yes sounds good so we see where they go :)" — built it. `adsb_map_modal.js` gained `this._trails` (a `Map<hex, [lat,lon][]>`, cleared in `close()`), a `_updateTrail(a)` helper (dedupes an unchanged position so a grounded/lost-fix aircraft doesn't pile up redundant points at one spot, caps at 60 points ~2 minutes at the 2s poll rate via `shift()`), and pruning in `_render()` keyed off the FULL aircraft snapshot (not just the positioned subset, so a contact that briefly drops its GPS fix mid-flight isn't wiped). Each trail draws as an `L.polyline` in the SAME color as that aircraft's own marker — pulled the squawk-color/staleness logic out of `_icon()` into a shared `_color(a)` so marker and trail can never disagree. Drawn under the marker each render (trails first, then markers, same `clearLayers()`-then-rebuild pattern as before). Verified with a scripted Leaflet stub (fake `L.polyline`/`L.marker` recording every call, no real Leaflet/browser needed) rather than assuming the logic was right: a moving aircraft's trail grows and a polyline draws once it has 2+ points; a stationary one dedupes to exactly 1 point and draws nothing; an aircraft removed from the snapshot has its trail entry deleted entirely; 100 simulated moving polls confirmed the 60-point cap actually holds (never grows past it, correctly shifts out the oldest). `node --check` clean. Not yet Pi-verified live — next step if wanted is opening the map on the Pi with several real aircraft moving and confirming the trails visually track their actual flight paths.

**LIVE-VERIFIED, same conversation**: user screenshots of trails working over Amsterdam/Schiphol approach paths (curved descent tracks clearly visible), "nice :)".

**Fourth follow-up, same conversation: stale contacts now drop off the map, not just dim.** User noticed gray (stale) planes accumulating and asked "when will they drop of the map? i dont want a map full og gray planes (last position)". Rather than assume, read the actual dump1090 C source (`dump1090/interactive.c`, `interactiveRemoveStaleAircrafts()` at line 533): a contact is only purged from the linked list (and thus from `/data.json`, since `aircraftsToJson()` in `net_io.c` just walks that list with zero TTL filtering of its own) after `MODES_INTERACTIVE_DELETE_TTL` = 300s/5min of total silence (`now - a->seen`). The existing "seen > 15s → gray" rule is purely our own frontend's early dimming cue (borrowed loosely from dump1090's OWN separate `MODES_INTERACTIVE_DISPLAY_TTL` = 60s, used at `interactive.c:449` to decide whether ITS OWN interactive display keeps showing a contact) and never removed anything — so a stale ghost could legitimately sit at its last known lat/lon for up to 5 minutes before this fix.

Fix: the MAP (not the Aircraft table, which still lists everything dump1090 reports, stale or not — a deliberate scope choice, table = full log, map = "where things actually are") now filters a contact out of `placed` once `seen > MAP_STALE_HIDE_SECONDS` (60, chosen to literally match dump1090's own `MODES_INTERACTIVE_DISPLAY_TTL` rather than an arbitrary pick — "our map hides what dump1090's own display would already stop showing"). Its trail also gets reset the moment it's hidden (new prune pass in `_render()`, separate from the existing full-snapshot-departure prune) so a contact that later reappears (came back into range, decoded again) starts a brand-new trail instead of drawing one long false "teleport" line straight across however long it was gone.

Verified with the same scripted `L`-stub approach as the trails feature: an aircraft that accumulated a real 5-point trail while moving vanishes entirely from the map (0 markers) the instant its `seen` crosses 60, its trail entry is confirmed deleted while hidden, and a later reappearance at a distant position correctly starts fresh (1-point trail, no polyline, no jump-line). `node --check` clean.

## DAPNET (POCSAG companion) capture source + Networks page (2026-07-29)

**Full feature, following the config-page-only prep from earlier the same day.** User confirmed naming: keep the Listener tab's existing RTL-SDR passive decoder as "POCSAG" (untouched — too entrenched: `kind="pocsag"` baked into `/api/pocsag/*` routes, `_KINDS["pocsag"]`, ~15 doc mentions), name the NEW bidirectional companion feature "DAPNET" instead (zero existing references, and more accurate — POCSAG is just the modulation, DAPNET is the specific real network this board talks to).

**Architecture, modeled on LoRaWAN** (the closest existing one-way-receive, no-conversations protocol) but with a genuinely different low-level source:
- `Protocol.DAPNET` + `PacketType.DAPNET_ALPHA/NUMERIC/TONE/ACTIVATION` added to `src/models/packet.py`.
- `src/decode/dapnet_event_adapter.py` (`adapt_event`) — parses `{"capcode","function","type","text"}` JSON lines from `extra/pocsag_companion`'s serial protocol into a `Packet`. No RF signal (the board reports none over JSON) — `Packet.signal` stays `None` deliberately, matching how `meshcore_event_adapter.py` handles payloads with no rssi/snr.
- `src/capture/dapnet_source.py` (`DapnetSerialSource`) — genuinely new pattern in this codebase: raw pyserial `readline()` in a background thread (blocking call, mirrors `src/hal/gps_reader.py`'s fallback path) bridged into `asyncio.Queue` via `loop.call_soon_threadsafe`. Neither `serial_source.py` (meshtastic-python's own pubsub-based `SerialInterface`) nor `meshcore_usb_source.py` (the `meshcore` library's own event subscription) were reusable templates since DAPNET has no equivalent higher-level library — this is plain JSON-over-serial with no framing library at all. `name` property follows the `dapnet_<label>`/bare `dapnet` convention shared with serial/meshcore_usb.
- Wired into `coordinator.py._process_capture` (`raw.capture_source.startswith("dapnet")` branch, mirroring the existing `meshcore_usb` special-case) and `_update_node` (early-return, no nodes-table row — same as LoRaWAN's own "just bump a counter that's actually a no-op since there's no row" branch).
- `src/main.py`/`src/api/server.py` both gained `_add_dapnet_source()` (one `DapnetSerialSource` per `config.capture.pocsag_serial` entry), dispatched on `source_name == "pocsag_serial"` in both files' capture-source loops (exact mirror of the serial/meshcore_usb dispatch pattern already there).
- `src/api/routes/dapnet_routes.py` — `GET /api/dapnet/{capcodes,packets,stats}` + CSV exports, same shape as `lorawan_routes.py` but keyed on `capcode` (not `dev_eui`), no RF columns. Registered in `server.py` (import, `include_router`, `init_routes(coord.packet_repo, ...)`).

**Two-tier capcode filtering — the trickiest design decision this session**, driven by three successive user clarifications that initially seemed contradictory until the third one resolved it:
1. First ask: "blacklist 4512,4520,224,208,216,200 ... dont write them to the db and a ignorelist to dont show them in the screen 4512,4520" — read initially as one unified list (ambiguous).
2. Final, unambiguous clarification: **"blacklist doesnt write and ignore doesnt show, so we can see the time stamps 206 208 etc but its not written en 4520 4521 are not shown not written"** — this is what got built:
   - `DapnetConfig.blacklist_capcodes` (`src/config.py`, default `[200, 208, 216, 224]` — DAPNET's own real confirmed housekeeping/time-sync beacon capcodes) → **shown live, never stored**. `coordinator.py._process_capture` calls `_notify_callbacks(packet)` (the same call that broadcasts every packet over the dashboard WebSocket) but skips `_store_packet`/`_relay`/`_publish_mqtt`/`_record_stats` entirely.
   - `DapnetConfig.ignore_capcodes` (default `[4512, 4520]`) → **neither shown nor stored**, dropped immediately, not even counted as a stray frame (it decoded fine, it's just unwanted).
   - Classification lives in a new `PipelineCoordinator._dapnet_capcode_tier(packet)` helper, checked right after decode/before storage.
3. **Frontend consequence**: since blacklisted pages never reach the DB, a pure 15s-poll page (like LoRaWAN's) would never show them despite the backend broadcasting them live. `frontend/js/dapnet_panel.js` therefore ALSO subscribes directly to `window.concentratorWS.on('packet', ...)` (the same feed the main dashboard packet log uses) and merges live-only rows into its packets list; each poll cycle keeps any live-only row not yet superseded by a real DB row and drops the rest. A blacklisted page's on-screen appearance is thus genuinely transient (by design — it was never persisted, so nothing survives to reconstruct it after the next poll). Reused `frontend/css/lorawan.css`'s existing `lw-*` classes wholesale (no new CSS) since they're generic table/tab/stat-card styling, not LoRaWAN-branded.

**New sidebar-hiding pattern, first use in this codebase**: `sidebar/sidebar_controller.js` gained `_applySourceGating()` (called from `bind()`, alongside the existing role-based `_applyIdentity()`) — fetches `/api/config` itself (no shared config object existed at sidebar-boot time; confirmed via research that `app.js`'s boot sequence never fetches `/api/config` before the sidebar renders) and toggles `[data-requires-source]` elements' visibility based on `capture.sources`. The DAPNET `<li>` in `index.html` carries `data-requires-source="pocsag_serial"` — independent of the existing `data-requires-section` (role/permissions) mechanism. Trade-off accepted: this only re-evaluates on page load/bind, not reactively after a config save — enabling the checkbox and expecting the sidebar link to appear without a reload isn't wired up (matches the existing "restart needed to fully apply" convention for capture-source config elsewhere).

**Configuration → POCSAG page** gained a second card, "DAPNET capcode filters" (two comma-separated capcode inputs, blacklist + ignore), backed by new `PUT /api/config/dapnet` (applies immediately, no restart — the coordinator reads `config.dapnet` fresh on every packet, unlike the USB-device-list PUTs which need a service restart to reconnect anything).

**Verification** (Mac has no fastapi/aiosqlite/pycryptodome venv, per this file's standing constraint — stubbed `sys.modules` for `aiosqlite`/`Crypto.Cipher.AES` this time too, a new addition to the established stubbing technique since `coordinator.py` imports `CryptoService` which imports pycryptodome):
- `node --check` clean on all touched/new JS (`app.js`, `dapnet_panel.js`, `pocsag_serial_card.js`, `sidebar_controller.js`, `meshcore_card.js`, `serial_card.js`).
- `ast.parse` clean on all touched/new Python (11 files).

- **Full `PipelineCoordinator._process_capture()` exercised end-to-end** against a `__new__`-constructed instance with `_store_packet`/`_notify_callbacks`/`_relay`/`_publish_mqtt`/`_record_stats`/`_stray_frames` all replaced with call-recording fakes: confirmed normal capcode → all 5 downstream calls fire; blacklisted capcode → only `_notify_callbacks` fires; ignored capcode → nothing fires, not even stray-frame recording; a non-JSON line → only stray-frame recording fires. This is the load-bearing test for the whole two-tier feature.

- `_add_dapnet_source` (both `main.py` and confirmed-present-once in `server.py`) exercised against a fake `CaptureCoordinator` — confirmed one `DapnetSerialSource` per configured device, correct `name` (`dapnet_heltec`).

## DAPNET polish round: icon, text truncation, scroll, log formatting, status/topbar chip (2026-07-29, same day)

Four small bugs found from user screenshots/logs after the DAPNET feature above, fixed in sequence:
1. **Sidebar icon looked like a briefcase** (rounded rect + arc handle) — swapped for an actual pager glyph (body/screen/three-button-row/antenna stub) in `index.html`.
2. **Long page text truncated mid-sentence.** Root cause: DAPNET's tables reused LoRaWAN's `.lw-table` CSS (`table-layout: fixed` + forced single-line ellipsis), sized for short DevEUI/RSSI columns, and the borrowed column classes (`col-fport` 60px, `col-dev` 130px) squeezed the free-text column. Fixed with new `.lw-table--dapnet-packets`/`.lw-table--dapnet-capcodes` CSS (`table-layout: auto`, wrapping text column via a new `lw-text` cell class) in `lorawan.css`.
3. **DAPNET page wasn't scrollable** — its `data-section="dapnet"` was missing from the CSS selector list that opts specific pages out of the shared `.section`'s `overflow: hidden` (LoRaWAN/Meshtastic/MeshCore were already listed, DAPNET was never added when the page was built).
4. **`meshpoint logs` showed a fake "perfect signal" bar for every DAPNET line** (`rssi 0.0 ▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓`) — `print_packet()` defaulted a missing `signal` object to `rssi=0.0`, which clamps to the *best* end of the RSSI bar's -120..-50 scale. DAPNET genuinely has no signal data (`Packet.signal` stays `None` by design). Fixed: `--`/empty bar when `packet.signal` is `None`, real values otherwise. Same fix pass added a `_payload_summary()` case for `dapnet_alpha/numeric/tone/activation` — previously DAPNET was the only protocol with no quoted-text summary at the end of its log line.

**New feature, same day: companion status query + topbar chip.** User: "can you make the companion spit out some data freq etc... and if activated show a topbar widget" — scoped down in discussion first: frequency/baud are already static/known Meshpoint-side (no need to query them), the one genuinely dynamic fact worth a round-trip is the **operator callsign** (set via the companion's own web UI, invisible to Meshpoint otherwise). Recommended and built a one-shot (not periodic) request/response query rather than continuous telemetry, to avoid adding chatter on the same serial line real page JSON already flows over.

- **Firmware** (`extra/pocsag_companion.ino`): new `BOARD_NAME_STR` macro (`"ttgo"`/`"heltec"`, reused by the boot banner too) right after the board-select `#if` guard; `handleSerialJsonLine()` now checks `doc["cmd"] == "status"` FIRST and calls a new `sendStatusReply()` (`{"type":"status","board":...,"callsign":...,"freq":439.9875}`) rather than falling into the send-a-page path. Compile-verified on BOTH board targets via the established temp-copy-and-restore workflow (`cp` to `/tmp`, flip the `#define`, `arduino-cli compile --fqbn esp32:esp32:ttgo-lora32`/`heltec_wifi_lora_32_V3`, restore from `/tmp` backup) — file left on `BOARD_HELTEC_WIFI_LORA32_V3` (the user's own active board). **User OTA-reflashed the companion themselves** (their own action, not something this session did).
- **`src/capture/dapnet_source.py`** rewritten: `_read_loop()` now writes `{"cmd":"status"}\n` once at the very top before entering its read loop; `_looks_like_json()` (bool pre-filter) refactored into `_parse_json_line()` (returns the parsed dict or `None`, avoiding a redundant second `json.loads` the old design would have needed to inspect `type`). Any line whose parsed dict has `"type":"status"` is cached into `self._status` (`board`/`callsign`/`freq`) and NOT enqueued as a page — a status reply has no `"capcode"` key anyway, so even without this explicit check `dapnet_event_adapter.adapt_event()` would have silently rejected it (harmlessly landing as a stray frame instead) — the explicit check just avoids that noise. New `connected`/`status` properties, same shape as Serial/MeshCore's own cached-radio-info pattern.
- **Backend status plumbing**: new `_find_dapnet_sources()` in `server.py` (mirrors `_find_serial_sources`), passed into `config_routes.init_routes(..., dapnet_sources=...)`. New `_dapnet_status_entry(src)` in `config_routes.py` building `{"name","connected","board","callsign","frequency_mhz"}`, fed into a **new top-level `payload["dapnet_status"]`** array in `GET /api/config`. **Deliberately a different key from the existing `payload["dapnet"]`** (the saved blacklist/ignore-capcode config from `config_enrichment.py`) — reusing that key would have been silently overwritten since `config_enrichment.enrich_config_payload()` runs after and unconditionally reassigns `base["dapnet"]`. Same naming-collision trap as the earlier `payload["serial"]` (live status) vs `payload["capture"]["serial"]` (saved config) distinction already documented in this file.
- **Frontend**: new `frontend/topbar/topbar_dapnet_chip.js` (`TopbarDapnetChip`), a near-verbatim copy of `TopbarSerialChip`'s structure/CSS reuse (`.topbar-serial*` classes wholesale, zero new CSS) with DAPNET's own fields swapped in (callsign instead of node ID, board name instead of modem preset). **CI lint failure investigated and fixed, same day — pre-existing/environmental, not caused by the DAPNET work.** PR #345 ("DAPNET page wasn't scrollable" — a CSS-only change) failed `ruff check src/ tests/` in CI with "Found 903 errors". Root cause confirmed by installing ruff locally and bisecting versions: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` installs ruff unpinned (`pip install -r requirements.txt ruff ...`), so CI always gets whichever version is newest at run time. Bisected exactly: **ruff 0.15.1 and everything before it passes this repo with zero config and zero errors; 0.16.0 broadened the default lint rule set** (adds `UP045` "`Optional[X]` → `X | None`" among others) and immediately surfaces ~905 pre-existing style hits repo-wide — this would have broken the next PR regardless of what it touched, purely from ruff cutting a new release. Confirmed this session's own new files (`dapnet_source.py`, `dapnet_event_adapter.py`, `dapnet_routes.py`) only contribute 12 of the 905, and only because they matched the codebase's own established `Optional[...]` convention (same style already used everywhere, e.g. `meshcore_event_adapter.py`) — not a new inconsistency introduced.

User was given the choice (pin version / add a ruff config to ignore the new rules / do a full repo-wide autofix now / leave it) and picked **pin the version** — smallest, safest option, doesn't touch any source files or address the underlying `Optional[X]` style debt. Fixed: `ci.yml`'s install step now pins `"ruff==0.15.1"` with an inline comment explaining why and what to do on a deliberate future bump (fix or explicitly ignore whatever the new version newly flags, rather than let it drift again). **If ruff needs bumping again later, expect UP045 (and whatever else 0.16+ adds by default) to surface across most of `src/`/`tests/` at once — that's expected fallout of the version bump, not a new bug, unless this memory note is stale by then.**

**Remote-settable DAPNET callsign — BUILT 2026-07-30** (the item directly above, picked up as "let's start with" from the worklist). User confirmed the deferred scope unchanged: "we want a serial command to set the callsign thru serial in our pocsag companion, so a user can connect it and set the callsign to get tx enabled."

- **Firmware** (`extra/pocsag_companion.ino`): new `handleSetCallsignCommand()`, dispatched from `handleSerialJsonLine()` on `cmd == "set_callsign"` (alongside the existing `cmd == "status"` branch) — exact same validation cascade as the on-device web dashboard's `/api/callsign` POST handler (empty check, `CALLSIGN_MAX_LEN`, `N0CALL` placeholder rejection, `isValidCallsign()`'s digit requirement), same `prefs.putString("callsign", cs)` NVS persistence, always replies exactly once (`{"type":"set_callsign_result","ok":true,"callsign":cs}` or `{"ok":false,"error":...}`). **Real compile bug hit and fixed**: `prefs` (the global `Preferences` object) is declared much later in the file, right before `getCallsign()`/`setCallsign()` — Arduino's auto-prototype generator only ever covers *functions*, never global variable ordering, so the new function calling `prefs.putString(...)` from earlier in the file hit a hard `'prefs' was not declared in this scope` compile error. Fixed with `extern Preferences prefs;` added to the file's existing "Forward declarations" block (which until now only ever held function prototypes for the *other* known Arduino auto-prototyping gap — functions defined after the web dashboard's raw HTML string literal — this is a related but distinct gap, now documented as such in that block's own comment). Compile-verified on BOTH board targets via the same temp-copy-and-restore workflow as every other multi-board change this project makes, file restored to `BOARD_HELTEC_WIFI_LORA32_V3` afterward. **Not yet reflashed to real hardware this round** — user will need to OTA-flash again before this specific command works against the real companion (the earlier `{"cmd":"status"}` addition IS already flashed from the prior round).
- **`src/capture/dapnet_source.py`**: gained real request/response plumbing, since until now the wire protocol was fire-and-forget only (the one-shot status query never awaited a specific reply, just cached whatever arrived). New `send_command(command, expect_type, timeout=5.0) -> Optional[dict]`: creates an `asyncio.Future`, stashes `(expect_type, future)` as the one-at-a-time pending request (the wire protocol has no request-id — this mirrors the same "one companion, one line, replies come back in order" assumption the original status query already relied on), pushes the JSON command onto a new stdlib `queue.Queue` (NOT `asyncio.Queue` — this queue is drained by the background reader thread, not the event loop), and awaits the future with a timeout. `_read_loop()` now calls a new `_flush_command_queue()` once per pass (writes any queued outgoing commands — worst-case latency to actually go out is one read timeout, 1s, since it's checked right before each blocking `readline()` call) and, on receiving a line whose parsed `"type"` matches the currently-pending `expect_type`, resolves the future via `_resolve_pending()` (uses `loop.call_soon_threadsafe` to call `future.set_result()` on the event-loop thread, since a `Future` must only be touched from its own loop's thread — this is the standard, correct cross-thread-to-asyncio bridging pattern, not a shortcut). New `note_new_callsign(cs)` updates the cached `status` dict immediately after a successful save, so the topbar chip / config-page readout don't have to wait for another status query (which only ever fires once, at connect).
- **New `src/api/routes/dapnet_config_routes.py`** (mounted `/api/config/dapnet/*` — deliberately a different router than `system_config_routes.py`'s bare `PUT /api/config/dapnet`, which saves the blacklist/ignore lists; `/api/config/dapnet/callsign` is a distinct path, no collision, exact same split as `serial_config_routes.py`/`meshcore_config_routes.py` owning per-device identity actions separately from the bulk device-list PUT). `_resolve_dapnet_source(label)` mirrors `_resolve_serial_source`'s naming convention exactly. `PUT /callsign` resolves the source, calls `send_command(...)`, and translates the result into ordinary FastAPI `HTTPException`s (503 not-connected-or-timeout, 400 device-rejected-with-the-real-reason) rather than a custom `{ok,error}` body — matches this codebase's existing HTTP-error convention rather than the device's own wire-protocol shape, and means the frontend's shared `api.put()` wrapper (which already toasts `err.detail` on any non-2xx response) needed zero new error-handling code. Registered in `server.py` (`_find_dapnet_sources(coord)` already existed from the earlier topbar-chip work, reused here unchanged).
- **Frontend** (`pocsag_serial_card.js`): new `_callsignEditHtml(live)` (only rendered when `live.connected` — no serial link to send anything over otherwise) adds a "Set callsign" input + button + status line to each connected device's row, right after the existing read-only readout tiles. `_saveCallsign()` PUTs to the new endpoint, clears the input and shows the confirmed (server-uppercased) callsign on success, generic "Save failed." on any error (real reason already surfaced via the shared toast).

Route logic (`dapnet_config_routes.update_dapnet_callsign`) exercised directly via minimal hand-rolled `fastapi`/`pydantic` stubs (same technique established earlier this session) covering all 4 branches: success (200 + cache update), device rejection (400 + real error message), timeout (503), and no-matching-source (503).

**Periodic status poll (TX count/uptime), 2026-07-30 — same day, following the "dig into it, tell me first" design review.** User agreed with the recommended split (static fields first, dynamic fields behind a real poll design) and asked to make the interval user-configurable, default 60s, global not per-device (matches how blacklist/ignore capcodes are already global, not per-companion).

- **Firmware**: `sendStatusReply()` gained `tx_count`/`last_tx_ok`/`uptime_ms` (reusing the already-tracked `txCount`/`lastTxOk` globals + `millis()`). Same forward-reference compile bug as the callsign feature hit again — `txCount`/`lastTxOk` are declared later in the file than `sendStatusReply()` — fixed with two more `extern` lines in the same "Forward declarations" block (`extern int txCount; extern bool lastTxOk;`), extending that block's own comment to note it now covers this too. Compile-verified on both boards via the usual workflow, restored to Heltec.
- **`src/config.py`**: new `DapnetConfig.status_poll_interval_s: int = 60`.
- **`src/capture/dapnet_source.py`** — the substantial change: constructor gained `status_poll_interval_s`; new `_status_poll_loop()` background asyncio task (started in `start()`, cancelled in `stop()`) calls `send_command({"cmd":"status"}, "status", timeout=5.0)` every interval -- reuses the EXISTING request/response plumbing from the callsign feature rather than inventing a new channel, keeping the "never an unsolicited device push" design goal intact (Meshpoint decides the cadence, still request/response). **Real bug caught and fixed while wiring this up**: `_read_loop()`'s `type=="status"` branch always did `continue` immediately after caching, without ever checking whether a pending `send_command()` call was actually waiting for a `"status"` reply -- meaning the periodic poll's `await self.send_command(...)` would have silently timed out on EVERY cycle despite the companion replying correctly, since its future was never resolved. Fixed by checking `if self._pending_expect_type == "status": self._resolve_pending(data)` inside that same branch, before the `continue`. **Second real bug, more serious, caught by reasoning through the new periodic-caller before it ever ran**: `send_command()`'s single-slot `_pending_expect_type`/`_pending_future` fields have zero protection against two concurrent callers -- previously harmless (status fired once at boot, callsign-set was rare and user-paced), but a 60s recurring timer WILL eventually overlap with a manual "Set Callsign" click, and the second caller would silently clobber the first's pending state, stranding it until its own timeout even though the companion answers both correctly, in order. Fixed with `self._command_lock = asyncio.Lock()` wrapping the whole body of `send_command()`, serializing concurrent callers instead of racing.
- **Config plumbing**: `main.py`/`server.py`'s two `_add_dapnet_source()` functions now pass `status_poll_interval_s=config.dapnet.status_poll_interval_s` into the constructor. `config_routes.py`'s `_dapnet_status_entry` gained `tx_count`/`last_tx_ok`/`uptime_ms`. `system_config_routes.py`'s `DapnetUpdate`/`update_dapnet` gained the new field (`Field(60, ge=10, le=3600)`) -- **and a real "which fields need a restart" distinction**: the two capcode lists still apply live (coordinator re-reads config per packet) but `status_poll_interval_s` is read once at `DapnetSerialSource` construction, so the route now computes `restart_required` by comparing the incoming value against the CURRENT config value before overwriting it, rather than the previous unconditional `False`. `config_enrichment.py`'s `base["dapnet"]` gained the field too.
- **Frontend** (`pocsag_serial_card.js`): "DAPNET capcode filters" card renamed "DAPNET settings" (no longer just capcode filters) with a new "Status poll interval (seconds)" number input (10-3600), save button now shows a restart-needed message when the interval actually changed (reads `result.restart_required` from the PUT response). Three new readout tiles per device: TX Count, Last TX (`Never`/`OK`/`Failed` based on `tx_count`/`last_tx_ok`), Uptime (`_fmtUptime()`, d/h/m/s formatting, documents the ~49.7-day `millis()` wraparound caveat inline).

**Verification**: `.ino` compiles clean on both boards. `node --check`/`ast.parse` clean on all touched files. Config round-trip confirmed (default 60, override via local.yaml). **The two bugs above were both caught by a real behavioral test BEFORE assuming the fix worked**: a fake serial harness with a 1s poll interval confirmed the periodic poll's reply actually resolves the pending future (previously would have silently timed out every cycle) and correctly updates `.status` with fresh `tx_count`/`uptime_ms`; a second test fired 5 concurrent `send_command()` calls via `asyncio.gather` and confirmed all 5 resolve correctly with the lock in place (this is exactly the scenario that would have silently corrupted/stranded requests without it). Route-level test confirmed `restart_required` is `False` when the interval is unchanged and `True` when it changes, plus Pydantic's `ge=10`/`le=3600` validation rejecting an out-of-range value. `_dapnet_status_entry` re-verified via AST-extraction to include the 3 new fields. `tests/test_html_assets.py` 7/7, changelog still parses (26 sections).

**Not yet Pi-flashed/live-tested** — needs another OTA reflash (firmware) plus a service restart (to pick up the new config field and Python-side poll loop) before this is live on real hardware.

**Web dashboard password settable from Configuration → POCSAG, 2026-07-30 (same day).** User: "we now have the default itoldyoualready, maybe we can make it so we can set it thru the config, just like the callsign?" — built as a genuine security-sensitive sibling to the callsign feature, deliberately handled MORE carefully in several respects since a password isn't public information the way a ham callsign is.

- **Firmware**: `WEB_PASSWORD` was previously a `secrets.h` compile-time-only `#define`, compared directly in `checkAuth()` — no runtime override existed at all (unlike callsign, which already had NVS-backed `getCallsign()`/`setCallsign()` before this session). Converted to a proper runtime value: new `String webPassword = WEB_PASSWORD;` (compile-time default until overridden) + `getWebPassword()`/`setWebPassword()` (mutex-guarded, mirroring `getCallsign`/`setCallsign` exactly), loaded from NVS at boot (`setWebPassword(prefs.getString("web_password", WEB_PASSWORD));`, right after the equivalent callsign line) with fallback to the compile-time default if never set. `checkAuth()` now compares against `getWebPassword()` instead of the raw macro. New `handleSetWebPasswordCommand()` (dispatched on `cmd == "set_web_password"`) validates only non-empty (deliberately NOT trimmed/uppercased like callsign — a password's exact characters, including case, are the point) and persists via `prefs.putString("web_password", pw)`.
- **Three deliberate asymmetries vs. the callsign feature, all security-motivated**:
  1. The companion's reply (`{"type":"set_web_password_result","ok":true}`) never includes the password value, unlike callsign's confirmation which echoes `cs` back — nothing about a password should appear in a JSON reply.
  2. `checkSerialInput()`'s own verbatim command-echo logging (`Serial.print("[serial] received line: ...")`, which prints EVERY other incoming command in full, including capcode sends and the set_callsign command) now specifically checks for `set_web_password` and logs a redacted placeholder instead — otherwise the password would appear in cleartext in the device's own serial console output regardless of anything done on the Meshpoint side.
  3. `dapnet_config_routes.py`'s new `PUT /api/config/dapnet/web-password` never caches, persists, or logs the value anywhere on the Meshpoint side (no `local.yaml` entry -- there's no config field for it at all, no status-cache update the way `note_new_callsign()` does, no audit-log `params` entry) — pure relay, by design. The route's own docstring calls this out explicitly as the deliberate difference from the callsign endpoint right next to it.
- Existing "Clear Settings" button (`/api/clear-settings`) updated to also reset the in-memory `webPassword` back to the `secrets.h` default alongside callsign/screen-timeout, since `prefs.clear()` now wipes a THIRD NVS key (`web_password`) that needs the same in-memory reset treatment the other two already got.
- **Frontend** (`pocsag_serial_card.js`): new `_webPasswordEditHtml()`/`_saveWebPassword()` mirroring the callsign edit control's structure, but `type="password"` (not `text`), `autocomplete="new-password"`, and the input is cleared immediately on send (success or failure) rather than only on success — nothing sensitive lingers in the DOM. No `_api.refresh()` call on success either (unlike callsign) since there's genuinely nothing to re-render.

Heltec (ESP32-S3, much larger partition) unaffected.

**Immediately after this, user asked a bigger strategic design question** (before this feature was even finished): should WiFi SSID/password and OTA password also become remotely settable, enabling a "flash once with blank secrets.h, configure everything else through Meshpoint" onboarding flow, plus folding a WiFi reset into the same reset button? Answered as a design review (per this session's "tell me first" pattern) rather than building immediately:
- **WiFi SSID/password**: recommended as genuinely valuable (removes the "must hand-edit secrets.h before every single flash" friction) and architecturally sound (USB serial is independent of WiFi state -- a companion with blank/wrong WiFi credentials is still fully reachable over serial for RX/TX and any {"cmd":...} commands). Recommended persist-to-NVS + require-a-reboot-to-apply (reusing the companion's own existing `/api/reboot`/`rebootRequested` mechanism) rather than attempting a live WiFi reconnect while RX keeps running -- safer, avoids unverified timing interactions with the radio.
- **OTA password**: same buildable pattern as web password, explicitly deprioritized as "yes, trivial, later" rather than bundled into the same pass.
- **Flash headroom flagged prominently**: TTGO is now at 95% -- WiFi+OTA-password support would add more code and could plausibly push it over the edge to a hard compile failure on that board specifically (Heltec, ESP32-S3, has ample headroom and is unaffected). Not a blocker, but must be watched closely, build-and-check-percentage after each addition, starting with Heltec.
- **Not yet decided by the user**: whether a future WiFi reset should fold into the SAME reset_credentials command/button or be a separate, more clearly-labeled destructive action (since a WiFi reset, unlike a callsign/password reset, actually takes the companion off the network until reconfigured -- a materially bigger consequence). Awaiting user's answer before building anything WiFi-related.

- **Fixed a real UX bug caught by the user first**: the reset-credentials button was still using a raw `window.confirm()` (the native, unstyled browser dialog, screenshot showed it looking out of place against the dark dashboard theme) -- every OTHER destructive action in this codebase (Settings → System, backup restore, channel/callsign deletes) already goes through a shared themed modal, `window.confirmModal({label, description}) -> Promise<boolean>` (`frontend/js/terminal/dangerous_modal.js`, CSS in `terminal.css`). Swapped the reset button over to it -- this card was the one remaining holdout. No new component needed, this modal was already loaded globally on every page (single script tag in `index.html`, not gated to Settings).
- **Firmware**: `WIFI_SSID`/`WIFI_PASSWORD` (previously `secrets.h` compile-time-only, used directly in `setupWifiNtpOta()`'s `WiFi.begin()` call and its "are credentials configured at all" check) converted to NVS-backed runtime values (`wifiSsid`/`wifiPass` globals + `getWifiSsid()`/`getWifiPassword()`/`setWifiCredentials()`, same mutex-guarded pattern as callsign/webPassword), loaded from NVS at boot with fallback to the `secrets.h` defaults, right alongside the existing callsign/webPassword NVS loads in `setup()`. `setupWifiNtpOta()` itself now reads via the getters, not the raw macros. New `handleSetWifiCommand()` (`cmd == "set_wifi"`) validates only non-empty SSID (empty password is explicitly valid -- open networks exist), persists via `prefs.putString`, replies with the SSID echoed back (not sensitive) but never the password. New `handleRebootCommand()` (`cmd == "reboot"`) reuses the EXACT existing `rebootRequested`/`rebootRequestedAt` delayed-restart mechanism the web dashboard's `/api/reboot` already uses (reply sent first, `loop()` calls `ESP.restart()` `REBOOT_DELAY_MS` later) -- letting Meshpoint trigger a reboot without needing the companion's own web UI at all, which is the whole point (bad WiFi credentials could make that web UI unreachable too, but USB serial keeps working regardless of WiFi state). `checkSerialInput()`'s redaction check extended to cover `set_wifi` lines too (carries the password in cleartext, same reasoning as `set_web_password`).
- **Two more forward-reference `extern` additions** to the same "Forward declarations" block (now the THIRD round of this exact pattern this session -- `prefs` for callsign, `txCount`/`lastTxOk` for the status poll, now `rebootRequested`/`rebootRequestedAt` for the serial reboot command): `handleRebootCommand()` sits near the other command handlers, well before where `rebootRequested`/`rebootRequestedAt` are actually declared (right before the web dashboard's own `/api/reboot` handler, much further down the file).
- **`src/api/routes/dapnet_config_routes.py`**: new `PUT /wifi` (mirrors the web-password route's "never cache/log/echo the secret" discipline exactly, only the SSID comes back in the response) and `POST /reboot` (separate action-trigger endpoint). The reboot route's own docstring flags an honest, real uncertainty: whether `DapnetSerialSource`'s connection survives the companion's reboot depends on whether the board's USB-UART bridge chip stays enumerated through an ESP32 reset (likely, given both current boards use one) or the board re-enumerates via native USB (would need a full Meshpoint service restart to reconnect, since this source has no reconnect loop -- same documented limitation `SerialCaptureSource` already has). Not yet resolved either way on real hardware.
- **Frontend**: new `_wifiEditHtml()`/`_saveWifi()`/`_rebootCompanion()` in `pocsag_serial_card.js` -- its own SSID+password field pair (password field cleared on send regardless of outcome, same discipline as the web-password control), a confirm-modal step BEFORE sending (since this genuinely disrupts connectivity, unlike callsign/password), and on a successful save, a SECOND confirm-modal offering "reboot now?" that chains into the new reboot endpoint if accepted -- explicitly warns the user in that second dialog's text that Meshpoint's own connection might need a service restart afterward, matching the backend's own documented uncertainty rather than overpromising a seamless reconnect.

Heltec (ESP32-S3) unaffected, still comfortably under its much larger partition. This is now genuinely close to the point where further TTGO-side additions to this file may need to trim something else first -- worth raising proactively before adding the still-pending OTA password feature.

**DAPNET From/To semantics fixed -- backwards since the adapter was first written, 2026-07-30 (same day).** User caught this via a packet-detail screenshot on the main Dashboard: a time-sync beacon showed "From: 200 (200), To: broadcast (broadcast)" and the mixed-protocol feed table rendered the real capcode/broadcast strings mangled through Meshtastic-style hex-ID formatting (`2041152` -> `!1152`, `broadcast` -> `!cast`). First fix attempt (a protocol-aware `_fmtId()` that kept the existing From/To data as-is) was rejected -- user pointed out the *direction* itself was backwards: DAPNET has no real sender, a page is broadcast over RF and addressed **to** a capcode, not from one. Exact quote: "its more from broadcast to 200 in this example, so its more the from and to need to be switched and the the too fully shown, this is for dapnet only."

Root cause: `src/decode/dapnet_event_adapter.py`'s `adapt_event()` set `source_id=str(capcode)` / `destination_id="broadcast"` -- the reverse of the real direction.

**Fix (data-model level, not just display)**:
- `dapnet_event_adapter.py`: swapped to `source_id="broadcast"`, `destination_id=str(capcode)`.
- `src/api/routes/dapnet_routes.py`: every capcode-roster query (`/capcodes`, `/packets`, `/stats`, both CSV exports) switched from grouping/filtering/reading `source_id` to `destination_id` for the capcode value; `/packets`' response now also exposes the raw `source_id` (always `"broadcast"`) alongside `capcode`.
- `src/storage/packet_repository.py`: `delete_dapnet_capcodes()` (the capcode-filter purge feature from the prior day's work) now filters `DELETE ... WHERE destination_id IN (...)` instead of `source_id` -- this was a real latent bug, since after the adapter swap the old `source_id`-based purge would never match anything (source_id is always the literal `"broadcast"` now).
- `frontend/js/dapnet_panel.js`: `_onWsPacket()`'s live-WebSocket capcode mapping (`capcode: packet.source_id`) switched to `packet.destination_id`.
- `frontend/js/simple_packet_feed.js`: `_fmtId(id, protocol)` gained a `protocol === 'dapnet'` branch that shows the id verbatim as plain text (no `!`-prefix hex truncation, no `"broadcast"` collapsed into `!cast`) -- this is the display-layer companion fix, now correct because the underlying source/destination values are also correct.
- `tests/test_packet_repository_dapnet_purge.py`: fixture helper `_insert_dapnet()` updated to build packets with the new (correct) `source_id="broadcast"`/`destination_id=capcode` shape; would otherwise silently test against data no longer representative of what the real adapter produces.
- `scripts/clear_dapnet_packets.py`: stale docstring comment referencing `source_id` for capcode corrected to `destination_id` (the script's own delete logic was already protocol-only and unaffected by the swap).

**Existing DB rows are NOT migrated** -- old-semantics rows (`source_id`=capcode, `destination_id`="broadcast") stored before this fix stay as-is. Recommended (not yet run) that the user execute `scripts/clear_dapnet_packets.py --apply` on the Pi once, right after deploying this fix, to clear out the old-semantics history rather than build a fragile automatic migration for what's a fairly small/disposable packet log.

**Verification (Mac, stub-based per this repo's testing constraints)**: `ast.parse` clean on all three touched `.py` files; `node --check` clean on both touched `.js` files; `adapt_event()` exercised directly against the exact JSON from the user's screenshot (capcode 200, "alpha" type) -- confirms `source_id="broadcast"`/`destination_id="200"`; `dapnet_routes.py`'s `/packets` and `/capcodes` handlers exercised end-to-end against a stubbed `fastapi`+fake DB row shaped like real storage, confirming `capcode` in the response now correctly reflects `destination_id`; `tests/test_html_assets.py` 7/7; changelog re-parses (26 sections) after the new bullet. **Not yet Pi-tested against a real captured page** -- `coordinator.py` was checked and confirmed unaffected (its DAPNET capcode-tier check and node-update path both read `decoded_payload.get("capcode")` directly, never `source_id`/`destination_id`), and `message_name_resolver.py`'s `source_id`-based broadcast-sender lookup was checked and confirmed scoped to the (unrelated) Meshtastic messages table, not DAPNET packets.

**Arduino-cli/ESP32 flash toolchain built into install.sh + proven live end-to-end, 2026-07-30 (same day).** Goal: a future Networks > DAPNET "flash firmware" button that builds+uploads `extra/pocsag_companion/pocsag_companion.ino` to a connected board straight from the dashboard, no Arduino IDE. User asked for the steps to test this manually first via the Pi CLI before committing to install.sh.

- **install.sh gained a new idempotent section 13** ("Install arduino-cli + ESP32 toolchain"): installs `arduino-cli` (official installer, `BINDIR` pointed at `/opt/arduino-cli/bin`), a self-contained config at `/opt/arduino-cli/arduino-cli.yaml` (`directories.data/user/downloads` all under `/opt/arduino-cli`, `board_manager.additional_urls` set to the ESP32 index), the `esp32:esp32@3.3.10` core, and the sketch's own libraries (Adafruit GFX 1.12.6, Adafruit SSD1306 2.5.17, RadioLib 7.7.1, ArduinoJson 7.4.3, Async TCP, ESP Async WebServer 3.12.0) -- then `chown -R meshpoint:meshpoint` the whole tree. Deliberately NOT under any user's `~/.arduino15`: the systemd service that will actually invoke this at runtime runs as `meshpoint`, a `--no-create-home` system account with no real `$HOME`. Sections 13-25 renumbered to 14-26 to make room. Also added `curl` to the section-1 apt package list (needed for the arduino-cli installer, nothing else in the script depended on it before).
- **Comment deliberately generalized after user pushback**: the toolchain itself (arduino-cli + esp32 core, which bundles `esptool`) is NOT POCSAG-specific -- it's usable later for flashing prebuilt Meshtastic/MeshCore firmware `.bin` releases via `esptool` directly too. Only the specific *libraries* installed are scoped to the `pocsag_companion` sketch (an Arduino-sketch build, unlike Meshtastic/MeshCore's PlatformIO-built official releases).
- **Real bug found and fixed during live testing**: `meshpoint` has no real `$HOME` (`--no-create-home`), so `arduino-cli compile` failed with `Cannot create build cache directory: mkdir /home/meshpoint: permission denied` -- arduino-cli's build *cache* (distinct from `--build-path`, no `--config-file` key of its own) always resolves via Go's `os.UserCacheDir()` (`$XDG_CACHE_HOME`, else `$HOME/.cache`), and `su`/service login still populates `$HOME` from the passwd entry even though the directory was never created and `/home` isn't writable by `meshpoint`. Fixed with `Environment=XDG_CACHE_HOME=/opt/arduino-cli/cache` added to `meshpoint.service`, plus pre-creating that dir in install.sh's section 13.
- **LIVE-VERIFIED, full loop, 2026-07-30**: as the actual `meshpoint` user (via the dashboard's own web Terminal, confirmed to be a child process of the running `meshpoint.service`, `User=meshpoint` in the unit file) --
  1. `arduino-cli compile --fqbn esp32:esp32:heltec_wifi_lora_32_V3 /opt/meshpoint/extra/pocsag_companion` succeeded cleanly (1,210,495 bytes / 36%, matching the Mac's own compile-check to within a few bytes).
  2. `arduino-cli upload -p /dev/ttyUSB2 ...` succeeded (esptool v5.3.0, ESP32-S3 detected, full flash write + hash verify, hard reset via RTS) -- **no `sudo` needed at all**, confirming `meshpoint`'s existing `dialout` group membership + directory ownership is sufficient (proven further by the fact DAPNET capture already reads this same port live in production as this same user).
  3. Board rebooted with the new firmware and the OLED's 180-degree rotation (see below) was visually confirmed flipped on the real device.
- **Gotchas hit and resolved along the way** (all now folded into the design, nothing outstanding): (a) `pi` user testing `sudo arduino-cli compile` hung/failed because plain `sudo` resets `$HOME` to `/root`, losing `pi`'s installed core/libraries -- resolved by moving everything to the shared, meshpoint-owned `/opt/arduino-cli` instead of relying on any one user's home; (b) a hand-written test script (`make-pocsag_companion.sh`) had a stray Windows-batch `pause` (harmless no-op in bash) and a leftover `sudo` on the upload line copied from earlier `pi`-user-context advice -- `meshpoint` has NO password at all (system account, matches `config/sudoers-meshpoint`'s own comment), so that `sudo` could never succeed and needed removing, not a new sudoers entry; (c) `/dev/ttyUSB1` (the port shown in Configuration → POCSAG) disappeared entirely (`ENOENT`, not "busy") after a replug/reset shifted enumeration -- board came back as `/dev/ttyUSB2`; confirms `/dev/ttyUSB*` numbers aren't stable across resets/replugs the way `/dev/serial/by-path/...` symlinks are (Configuration's own device list already uses by-path for exactly this reason) -- **a real future flash-button feature should resolve the by-path symlink at flash time, not hardcode a ttyUSBN**.
- **Also fixed while in the file**: `pocsag_companion.ino` OLED was mounted upside-down on this Heltec V3 -- added `display.setRotation(2)` right after `display.begin()` (Adafruit_GFX: 0=normal, 2=180°). Compile-verified on both TTGO (1,254,072 bytes/95%, +12 bytes negligible) and Heltec (1,210,527 bytes) on the Mac before the live flash above. Live-verified: display now renders right-side-up on the real board.

**Not yet built**: the actual Networks > DAPNET "flash firmware" dashboard button/route -- this session only proved the underlying toolchain and permission model work end-to-end from the CLI/web-Terminal. Next step when picked back up: a backend route that shells out to `arduino-cli`/`esptool` (with `XDG_CACHE_HOME` + `--config-file` already sorted by this work) resolving the target port via `/dev/serial/by-path/` rather than a raw device number, plus UI to trigger it and stream progress.

**Confirmed live, 2026-07-30 (same day, right after the flash toolchain test above): `DapnetSerialSource` does NOT auto-reconnect after a companion reflash/reboot.** This was flagged as an open, untested risk in the WiFi/reboot feature's own docstring earlier this session ("whether Meshpoint's own serial connection survives the companion's reboot... would need a Meshpoint service restart to reconnect, since DapnetSerialSource has no reconnect loop") -- now confirmed true in practice: after flashing the Heltec V3 companion (which reset it and re-enumerated its USB port, same session as the ttyUSB1->ttyUSB2 jump above), the "POCSAG companions" card's readout tiles went blank/stale until the user manually ran `sudo systemctl restart meshpoint`. Not yet fixed -- candidate for later: a reconnect loop that detects the drop and re-resolves the configured `/dev/serial/by-path/...` symlink rather than requiring a manual restart, useful both for the flash-button feature (section above) and plain unplug/replug resilience.

**"Companion firmware" Compile/Flash card built on Configuration → POCSAG, 2026-07-30 (same day, right after the arduino-cli toolchain was proven live from the CLI).** Turns the manual `arduino-cli compile`/`upload` commands just tested by hand into a real dashboard feature. User's original ask: a card between "POCSAG companions" and "DAPNET settings" with Compile + Flash buttons, port taken from the configured companion (ask which one only if multiple are configured), streamed compile output shown somewhere but collapsible/hidden by default. Also specifically asked for the board list to be a pulldown auto-populated by reading the `.ino`'s own board defines, rather than hardcoded, since "we can build ttgo and heltec for now."

**Backend** (`src/api/routes/pocsag_firmware_routes.py`, new file):
- `GET /api/pocsag/firmware/targets` -- scans `pocsag_companion.ino` for every `#define BOARD_*`/`//#define BOARD_*` line (regex `_BOARD_DEFINE_RE`, scoped to the `BOARD_` prefix so it never touches the sketch's many other unrelated `#define`s) and cross-references against `_KNOWN_BOARDS` (macro -> label/fqbn -- the one piece that can't be auto-derived, since a board's FQBN isn't spelled out in the source). A third board added to the sketch later shows up in the pulldown automatically; still needs one line added to `_KNOWN_BOARDS` before it's actually buildable.
- `POST /api/pocsag/firmware/compile/stream` -- `_select_board_define(macro)` rewrites the sketch's two toggle lines (uncomment target, comment every other known macro) before running `arduino-cli --config-file /opt/arduino-cli/arduino-cli.yaml compile --fqbn <fqbn> <sketch_dir>` via `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec`, streamed line-by-line as NDJSON through `_stream_subprocess()` (new small helper, same wire shape as `src/api/update/streaming.py`'s `stream_update()` -- `{"type":"started","cmd":[...]}`, `{"type":"line","stream":"stdout"|"stderr","text":...}` per line, final `{"type":"result","result":{"returncode":...,"success":...}}`, the nested `"result"` key deliberately matching `UpdateStreamClient.postNdjson`'s own expected shape so the same frontend client class works unmodified).
- `POST /api/pocsag/firmware/flash/stream` -- resolves the target port SERVER-SIDE from `config.capture.pocsag_serial` by label (never trusts a raw path from the browser), then -- new safety behavior, not just a straight upload -- if that device's `DapnetSerialSource` is currently connected, calls `await source.stop()` before flashing (esptool needs exclusive access to reset+write the board) and `await source.start()` after a 3s settle delay, reporting whether it actually reconnected. This directly closes the gap hit earlier the same day (reflashing left DAPNET capture dead until a manual `systemctl restart meshpoint`) for flashes done through this new feature specifically -- flashes done by hand outside Meshpoint still hit that gap, unchanged.
- Wired into `src/api/server.py`: import, `app.include_router(pocsag_firmware_routes.router, dependencies=protected)`, `pocsag_firmware_routes.init_routes(config=config, dapnet_sources=_find_dapnet_sources(coord))`.

**Frontend** (`frontend/js/configuration/pocsag_serial_card.js`, extended, no new file -- matches the existing one-class/multiple-cards pattern already used for "POCSAG companions"/"DAPNET settings"): new `<article class="cfg-card">` inserted between the two existing ones. Board `<select>` populated on mount from `/targets`; device `<select>` populated in `render()` from the same `config.capture.pocsag_serial` list the existing device rows already use, hidden entirely when 0 or 1 devices are configured (skips the picker when there's nothing to choose between, per the user's own suggestion). Compile has a `window.confirmModal` guard on Flash only (compile is non-destructive; flash briefly interrupts capture and writes real flash). Both actions share `_runFirmwareStream()`, calling `window.UpdateStreamClient.postNdjson()` (same NDJSON client Settings → Updates already uses, reused as-is -- no new client class needed) into a `<pre class="cfg-firmware-output">` panel, hidden by default with a "Show/Hide output" toggle button; auto-reveals itself on failure. New CSS `.cfg-firmware-output` in `configuration.css`, matching `settings.css`'s `.update-progress__terminal-body` look (same monospace dark panel) but standalone rather than nested in a bigger terminal wrapper.

**Design decision, explicitly discussed with the user first**: the sketch's board target is a source-level `#define`, not an `arduino-cli` build flag -- there's no way to say "compile for TTGO" without editing the file first. Went with the pragmatic fix (`_select_board_define` sed-toggles the two lines server-side before every compile) rather than the cleaner refactor (board selected via a `--build-property` instead of mutating source), per the user's explicit "for now" framing. **This means every Compile run mutates the checked-out `pocsag_companion.ino` on disk** (leaves it in whichever board's state was last compiled) -- expected/by design, not a bug, matching exactly what was done by hand earlier this session; worth remembering if `git status` ever shows this file dirty on the Pi.

**Verification (Mac, stub-based per this repo's testing constraints)**: `ast.parse` clean; `node --check` clean; board-discovery/select-define round-tripped against the REAL `.ino` file (select TTGO -> select Heltec back -> byte-identical to git HEAD, confirmed via `git status --short` staying clean); both streaming routes exercised end-to-end with stubbed `fastapi`/`pydantic`/audit/auth and a fake subprocess command (`true`)/fake `DapnetSerialSource`, confirming: the NDJSON event shape, the stop-before/start-after behavior around a connected source, and the 400 rejection for an unconfigured device label; `tests/test_html_assets.py` 7/7; changelog re-parses (26 sections). **LIVE-VERIFIED through the actual browser UI, same day**: Compile ran against the real Heltec V3 (Sketch uses 1,210,511 bytes/36%). Two bugs found and fixed from this first live click-through:
- Compile's arduino-cli invocation was missing `-v` -- the whole ~10s+ build produced zero output until the final size summary, making the panel look frozen the entire time despite working correctly. Added `-v` to the compile command.
- The "Companion to flash" picker showed up even with only one companion configured (should auto-select and stay hidden) -- `.cfg-field`'s own `display: flex` was silently beating the browser's `[hidden] { display: none }` rule, same bug class as the earlier LoRaWAN search-box fix (`.lw-search-wrap[hidden]`). Fixed with an explicit `.cfg-field[hidden] { display: none; }` override in configuration.css.

Flash then verified fully working end-to-end for real: released `/dev/serial/by-path/...-usb-0:1.3:1.0-port0` (the STABLE by-path entry, not a raw ttyUSBN -- confirms the earlier renumbering concern doesn't apply here since the configured device already uses by-path), ran esptool's full write+verify+reset, waited 3s, and `dapnet_heltec reconnected` on the same by-path port automatically -- no manual `systemctl restart meshpoint` needed. This closes the loop on the "flash leaves capture dead" gap for any flash done through this new button specifically.
