**Real bug fixed: 17s Messages-page load traced to a missing index, not DB size, 2026-08-02 (same session).** User asked about the DB "getting bigger" (12MB) and whether to move to MySQL, then added the real concrete symptom mid-investigation: reloading Messages pinned 1 of 4 CPU cores at 100% while memory stayed flat at 230MB. That CPU signature (not I/O wait, not memory pressure) was the key clue steering the diagnosis away from "DB too big" and toward "expensive unindexed computation."

Two parallel research subagents confirmed: (1) DB size/MySQL was a red herring -- caps unchanged since the July investigation (1M packets/100K telemetry), single-writer/single-connection architecture confirmed (no evidence of real multi-writer contention), and MySQL would have been a genuine regression since Backup/Restore hard-depends on SQLite's own hot-backup API (`src/backup/archive_builder.py:159-171`, `sqlite3.Connection.backup()`) with no MySQL equivalent. (2) The real cause: `node_repository.py`'s `get_capture_sources_for_broadcasts()` (used by the Messages page's `_enrich_conversations()`) joins `messages` to `packets` on `packet_id`/`protocol` -- but `packets` had indexes on `timestamp`/`source_id`/`protocol`/`packet_type` only, **never `packet_id`**, confirmed via `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` on the live DB showing a full unindexed `SCAN p` per matched message row. Separately, the whole app runs every read and write through one shared SQLite connection with no WAL (`journal_mode=delete`, `synchronous=FULL` confirmed on the live file) -- explaining why it was only "sometimes" slow: a Messages read could land right behind the hourly bulk packet-retention DELETE (up to the 1,000,000-row cap) or a burst of live capture writes, and rollback-journal mode blocks readers during any write.

**Fix** (`src/storage/database.py`): added `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_packets_packet_id ON packets(packet_id, protocol)` to `SCHEMA_SQL` (idempotent, applies automatically to the existing live DB on next connect via the already-existing `executescript(SCHEMA_SQL)` call -- no separate migration needed, unlike the column-add migrations which need the `_run_migrations()` guard pattern since `ALTER TABLE` isn't naturally idempotent). Added `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` + `PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL` right after opening the connection in `connect()` -- WAL is a durable property of the DB file (set once, persists across restarts), synchronous is per-connection (set every time); NORMAL is the standard safe pairing with WAL for this kind of workload (capture/monitoring log, not a financial ledger -- worst case on a hard power loss is losing the last uncommitted write, never corruption).

**Verified for real, not just syntax-checked**: `aiosqlite` isn't installed on the Mac (confirmed, matches this repo's standing limitation) so `tests/test_database_migration.py` can't run locally (ImportError, pre-existing CI-only limitation, not something this change broke -- confirmed the test doesn't assert index names/counts either, so no conflict). Instead, extracted the real `SCHEMA_SQL` string from the actual file via regex and ran it through Python's stdlib `sqlite3` (a real SQLite engine, just not the async wrapper) against an in-memory DB: confirmed the new index actually gets created, and ran the EXACT join query from `node_repository.py` through `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` -- confirmed it now reads `SEARCH p USING INDEX idx_packets_packet_id (packet_id=? AND protocol=?)` instead of the full scan the investigation found on the live database. This is a genuine before/after proof the fix resolves the diagnosed root cause, not just a hopeful index add. `ast.parse` clean. Changelog bullet added under the existing "Dashboard and storage" section, `v0.7.9`, re-parses at 27 sections.

**Not yet live-tested for the actual 17s->fast timing improvement** -- next step when picked back up: deploy to the Pi, reload Messages, confirm the CPU spike is gone and the load feels fast. WAL mode will also create `-wal`/`-shm` files alongside `concentrator.db` on first connect after this deploys -- worth knowing so an unexpected new file next to the DB isn't mistaken for something else.

**Pager channel decision corrected twice, then finalized: ch9/FSK, not ch5-7, 2026-08-02 (same session, still pure planning, nothing built).** Picking up the pager plan where it left off (concentrator channel + sync word first, per user's own build order: "first a freq to receive, then a page where we see it and then send stuff to it"). Real register-level investigation into `extra/sx1302_hal` (the patched libloragw source this fork maintains) overturned the earlier "Option A" plan and corrected two of my own mistaken claims along the way -- worth reading in full since the final answer is the opposite of where this started today.

**Finding 1 -- ch5-7 can't get an independent sync word after all.** Traced the actual register map (`extra/sx1302_hal/libloragw/inc/loragw_reg.h`): all 8 multi-SF channels (ch0-ch7) share ONE sync-word register pair (`SX1302_REG_RX_TOP_FRAME_SYNCH0/1_SF7TO12_PEAK1/2_POS`, registers 578/579) -- there's no per-channel version, confirming `_configure_board()`'s own comment ("`lorawan_public=True` programs ch0-ch7 multi-SF... at lgw_start()") means literally ALL of them, not each independently. The only other independently-configurable slot is the service channel's (`SX1302_REG_RX_TOP_LORA_SERVICE_FSK_FRAME_SYNCH0/1_PEAK1/2_POS`, 932/933) -- already Meshtastic's `0x2B`. So exactly two sync-word slots exist total on this chip, both already spoken for; a new channel on ch5-7 would be stuck sharing LoRaWAN's `0x34`. This invalidated the "extend `set_syncword()` to ch5-7" plan from the previous planning session -- not because it's hard, but because the hardware genuinely has no third slot.

**Finding 2 -- my own first answer about ch9 was WRONG, corrected after deeper digging.** When the user asked "what about channel 9 then" as the fallback, I initially (wrongly) concluded ch8 (Meshtastic's service channel) and ch9 (FSK) share the same physical demodulator based on both living under a combined `LORA_SERVICE_FSK` register-name prefix -- i.e. that activating FSK would disable Meshtastic reception. User asked to verify before accepting that. Correctly walked it back after reading the *actual* HAL implementation, not just register names: `lgw_rxif_setconf()` (`loragw_hal.c:602-695`) shows ch8 and ch9 write to **separate** config state (`CONTEXT_LORA_SERVICE` vs a wholly separate `CONTEXT_FSK` struct, the latter with its **own independent `sync_word`/`sync_word_size`**), each with its own per-index `enable`/`freq_hz` slot in `CONTEXT_IF_CHAIN[]`. Confirmed further via the hardware capability table itself (`loragw_sx1302.c:85-95`, `LGW_IFMODEM_CONFIG` -- the code's own comment calls this "hardware modem capabilities... available IF chains and modems on the hardware", listing `IF_LORA_STD` and `IF_FSK_STD` as two of ten parallel fixed entries, not a mode switch) and via the packet-decode path (`loragw_sx1302.c:1938-2101`, which reads whichever `if_chain` a given received packet actually arrived on and branches to LoRa vs FSK decode per-packet -- only possible if both demodulators can be actively receiving in the same poll). No exclusivity check, comment, or shared-resource gate found anywhere. **Conclusion: ch8 and ch9 are genuinely independent, simultaneously-operable hardware, each with its own sync word** -- activating FSK does NOT touch Meshtastic.

**Final decision: the pager uses ch9/FSK**, reverting to close to the user's actual first-ever idea from earlier in this same session ("i thought about our pocsag companion what we have now but direct on the concentrator on a lora freq" -- their words, right at the start of this whole pager thread) -- except now correctly understood as FSK *modulation* on genuinely isolated hardware with its own real sync word, not necessarily the POCSAG *protocol* specifically (still explicitly not-POCSAG per the user's earlier "no not pocsag realy using the most out of the concentrator" clarification -- the pager can use its own simple custom framing over FSK, distinct from DAPNET's actual on-air protocol). This supersedes the ch5-7 plan and its shared-LoRaWAN-syncword fallback entirely.

**What this actually commits to building, scoped but not started**: `src/hal/sx1302_wrapper.py` has **zero FSK support today** -- `MOD_LORA` is the only modulation constant defined anywhere in `src/hal/` (re-confirmed, matches an earlier finding from the original concentrator-idle-capacity investigation). Needed: (1) an RX config method for if_chain 9 (bandwidth/datarate/sync word), mirroring `_configure_if_channels()`'s existing pattern but for the FSK path; (2) a `MOD_FSK` constant + FSK packet construction in `send()` for TX -- the `LgwPktTxS` struct already has an `f_dev` (frequency deviation) field sitting unused, so this was anticipated but never finished; (3) deciding the actual over-the-air framing for the pager itself (sync word value, payload shape for the canned-message IDs) -- the user's own protocol, not POCSAG's.

**Status: still pure planning, decision now final and stable** (channel choice took a full round-trip today -- ch5-7 -> rejected -> ch9 -> wrongly rejected -> corrected -> accepted). Next real step when picked back up: build the RX-config side of the Python wrapper first, per the user's own stated build order (receive before send, dashboard page after that).

**Pager project: first real code, FSK RX config added to the HAL wrapper, 2026-08-02 (same session, right after the ch9 decision).** First implementation step of the pager plan, per the user's own build order (concentrator channel/sync-word first). Scoped deliberately narrow: this is the concentrator-side RX *capability*, not the full pipeline -- no capture source class, no coordinator wiring, no chosen frequency/sync-word for real operation yet, no dashboard page. Those are separate next steps once this foundation is confirmed solid.

**`src/hal/sx1302_wrapper.py` changes**:
- New constants: `MOD_FSK = 0x20` (matches `extra/sx1302_hal/libloragw/inc/loragw_hal.h:65` exactly), `FSK_IF_CHAIN = 9`, `FSK_DATARATE_MIN/MAX = 500/250_000` (matches `loragw_hal.h:86-87`'s `DR_FSK_MIN`/`DR_FSK_MAX`), `FSK_DEFAULT_BANDWIDTH = BW_125KHZ` (FSK reuses the same BW_125/250/500KHZ constants as LoRa -- `loragw_hal.h:67-68`'s own comment: "values available for the 'bandwidth' parameters (LoRa & FSK)"), `FSK_DEFAULT_DATARATE = 4_800` (a starting default, not yet tuned against real hardware).
- New `configure_fsk_channel(rf_chain, rf_chain_freq_hz, frequency_hz, sync_word, sync_word_size=2, datarate=4800, bandwidth=BW_125KHZ)` method -- populates the *same* `LgwConfRxifS` ctypes struct already used for LoRa channels (confirmed its Python mirror in `sx1302_types.py` already has the `sync_word`/`sync_word_size` fields, byte-for-byte matching the real `struct lgw_conf_rxif_s` in `loragw_hal.h:195-207` -- no struct changes needed, just a new caller) and calls `lgw_rxif_setconf(9, conf)`, the same generic HAL function already used for every other channel. Computes the IF offset the same way `_configure_if_channels()` does for the main LoRa plan (`frequency_hz - rf_chain_freq_hz`). Deliberately a standalone method, not folded into `ConcentratorChannelPlan`/`_configure_if_channels()` -- ch9 is independent hardware serving a different project with its own framing, not part of the Meshtastic/LoRaWAN plan those methods manage. Raises `ValueError` for an out-of-range datarate, `RuntimeError` if the HAL call itself fails -- matching this file's existing error-handling conventions elsewhere.
- `ConcentratorPacket` gained a `modulation: str = "lora"` field (defaulted, so the one existing construction call site didn't need touching structurally beyond adding the new kwarg) and `receive()` now sets it from `pkt.modulation == MOD_FSK` -- necessary because `pkt.datarate` is the *same* underlying C field for both modulations (a real spreading factor 5-12 for LoRa, or the raw FSK bitrate in bps for FSK, per `loragw_hal.h`) -- without checking `.modulation`, a consumer would have no way to know `spreading_factor` doesn't mean SF for an FSK packet.

**Verification, done for real since there's no aiosqlite/hardware dependency in this file** (confirmed `sx1302_wrapper.py` imports cleanly standalone on the Mac): (1) constants checked against the actual values found in `extra/sx1302_hal`'s real header during the investigation, not just internal self-consistency; (2) `configure_fsk_channel()` exercised against a fake `lgw_rxif_setconf` capturing every struct field written -- confirmed correct IF-offset math (869.4625 MHz target against a 869.525 MHz RF1 anchor -> -62500 Hz, matching the two precomputed frequencies already sitting in this codebase's `meshtastic_eu868_default()` plan for this exact sub-band), confirmed sync word/size/datarate/bandwidth all land in the struct correctly, confirmed the out-of-range-datarate `ValueError` and HAL-failure `RuntimeError` paths both fire correctly; (3) `receive()` exercised against a fake `lgw_receive` returning ONE simulated LoRa packet (ch2) and ONE simulated FSK packet (ch9) in the *same* poll -- exactly the "both demods active simultaneously" scenario the whole ch8/ch9-independence investigation was about -- confirmed both come back correctly tagged (`modulation="lora"`/`"fsk"`) with the LoRa packet's `spreading_factor` staying a real SF (7) and the FSK packet's staying the raw bps value (2400), not misinterpreted. The pre-existing `tests/test_sx1302_wrapper.py` suite (11 tests) still passes unchanged, confirming no regression to the LoRa-only paths this file already handled. `ast`/import-level checks clean.

**Changelog**: one honest bullet added under "Hardware page and band spectrum" (`v0.7.9`), explicitly labeled "(internal, not yet reachable from the dashboard)" -- real new capability in the codebase, but zero user-visible effect yet, no chosen frequency/sync-word wired to anything real. Re-parses at 27 sections.

**Not yet decided/built, explicitly next**: the pager's actual sync word value (needs to be genuinely arbitrary/distinct, not yet chosen), which of RF0/RF1 and which exact frequency within 869.4-869.65 MHz to commit to for real (869.4625 MHz was only used as a verification example, matching the two frequencies `meshtastic_eu868_default()` already precomputed for this sub-band, not yet confirmed as the final pick), a real capture-source class analogous to `DapnetSerialSource`/`SerialCaptureSource` to actually consume `receive()`'s new FSK-tagged packets into the rest of the app, TX support (mirroring this same RX work for `send()`), and only after all of that, the dashboard page. This session's piece was purely "can the concentrator receive FSK at all, correctly, without breaking the LoRa channels already running" -- confirmed yes, on paper; still needs a real hardware test once wired to an actual running coordinator.

**Pager project: frequency and sync word chosen, 2026-08-03 (new session, still pure decision -- no code changed).** User asked what I'd pick for both, then pasted a Google search result confirming the Dutch ETSI sub-band P rules (869.40-869.65 MHz, 500mW/27dBm ERP, 10% duty cycle) as the constraint to satisfy -- matches what was already understood from the earlier `concentrator_config.py` investigation, no new info there, but the TTN RX2-downlink detail (869.525 MHz specifically) was a useful concrete reason to steer away from that exact frequency.

**Frequency: 869.4625 MHz, on RF1** (anchor 869.525 MHz -> IF offset -62,500 Hz). Not a new number -- it's one of the two frequencies `meshtastic_eu868_default()` already precomputes for this sub-band (the other being 869.5875 MHz), and the same value already used as the verification example when `configure_fsk_channel()` was tested last session. Sits inside 869.40-869.65 MHz, and 62.5 kHz clear of 869.525 MHz -- deliberately avoiding that exact frequency since the Google answer flagged it as TTN's real-world RX2 downlink channel, and this concentrator's own Meshtastic ch8 already sits exactly there; the pager shouldn't stack a second signal on that specific frequency.

**Sync word: 0xF72D91, 3 bytes.** Checked the real HAL header this session to confirm the field shape before recommending anything (`extra/sx1302_hal/libloragw/inc/loragw_hal.h:201-202`): `sync_word` is `uint64_t`, `sync_word_size` is in bytes with no hardware-enforced minimum/maximum noted -- so size is a free choice, not a constraint. Picked 3 bytes over the wrapper's own 2-byte default (`configure_fsk_channel()`'s `sync_word_size=2` default from last session) because FSK sync detection is a raw bit-pattern correlation (unlike LoRa's chirp correlation, which tolerates a 1-byte sync word fine) -- a longer word lowers the false-sync-lock rate against other ambient FSK traffic sharing the 869.4-869.65 sub-band. Value itself is arbitrary but deliberately distinct from both sync words already live on this concentrator (LoRaWAN public `0x34` on ch0-7, this fork's Meshtastic `0x2B` on ch8) for clarity in captures, though there's no actual collision risk either way since ch9 is an independent demodulator.

**Explicitly noted for later, not applicable yet**: the 10% duty cycle / 500mW ERP ceiling from the regulation is a TX-side constraint -- irrelevant to the RX config work done so far, will matter once the Heltec V3 TX firmware is built (duty-cycle bookkeeping, power-amp capability check per the Google answer's own warning that many SX1276-class chips cap at 14-20dBm without a PA).

**Status: decision recorded, nothing wired yet.** Still needed per the existing build order: a capture-source class to consume FSK packets via `receive()` using this frequency/sync word, coordinator wiring to actually call `configure_fsk_channel(rf_chain=1, rf_chain_freq_hz=869_525_000, frequency_hz=869_462_500, sync_word=0xF72D91, sync_word_size=3, ...)` at startup, TX support, and the dashboard page -- none of that touched this session.

**Pager project: capture-source wiring + sync word revision, 2026-08-03 (same session as the freq/sync-word decision above).** After picking the frequency/sync word, user said "go ahead" on building the capture-source class per the established build order. Real architectural finding along the way: a genuinely separate `CaptureSource` subclass polling the same hardware independently isn't possible -- there's only one `SX1302Wrapper`/one physical SPI device, and `receive()` already drains BOTH LoRa and FSK packets from one HAL call per poll. So this wired directly into the existing `ConcentratorCaptureSource` rather than adding a new class, tagging FSK packets distinctly rather than running a second poll loop.

**Traced the decode pipeline first** (via research agent) to find the right integration point: `PipelineCoordinator._process_capture()` (`src/coordinator.py`) dispatches by `raw.capture_source` string prefix (`meshcore_usb`, `dapnet`) BEFORE falling through to `PacketRouter.decode()`'s protocol_hint if/elif chain -- and critically, anything that reaches `PacketRouter` with no real decoder match falls through to a Meshtastic/MeshCore *trial-decode* fallback, which would silently swallow foreign FSK frames into the in-memory-only `StrayFrameLog` (never persisted) rather than storing them. This meant the pager packets needed their own `capture_source` prefix routed BEFORE the router, mirroring how DAPNET already avoids it.

**Changes:**
- `src/models/packet.py`: added `Protocol.PAGER` and `PacketType.PAGER_RAW` (explicitly documented as a placeholder -- no real OTA framing exists yet since there's no Heltec V3 firmware).
- `src/decode/pager_event_adapter.py` (new, mirrors `dapnet_event_adapter.py`): `adapt_event(raw_payload, signal)` wraps raw bytes as an undecoded `Packet` (`encrypted_payload=raw_payload`, `decoded_payload=None`, `decrypted=False`) -- unlike DAPNET's adapter, this one DOES keep `signal` (real RSSI/SNR from the concentrator itself, not a serial companion with no RF visibility).
- `src/coordinator.py`: new `elif raw.capture_source.startswith("pager")` branch (between the existing dapnet branch and the router fallback) plus a `_adapt_pager` staticmethod, exact mirror of the dapnet pattern.
- `src/capture/concentrator_source.py`: new constants `PAGER_FSK_FREQUENCY_HZ = 869_462_500`, `PAGER_FSK_SYNC_WORD = 0x946437`, `PAGER_FSK_SYNC_WORD_SIZE = 3`, `PAGER_FSK_RF_CHAIN = 1` (RF1, same chain as Meshtastic's ch8, since 869.4625 MHz is already within RF1's tuning window -- no second RF chain/retune needed). New `pager_enabled: bool = False` constructor param; `start()` calls `self._wrapper.configure_fsk_channel(...)` right after `configure(self._channel_plan)` (matching the wrapper's own docstring: call before `start()`) only when the flag is on. `packets()` now checks `pkt.modulation == "fsk"` first and yields those with `capture_source="pager"`/`protocol_hint=Protocol.PAGER` instead of falling into the existing Meshtastic/LoRaWAN frequency-based branch.
- `src/config.py`: `RadioConfig.pager_enabled: bool = False` -- picked up automatically by the existing generic YAML merge (`_apply_yaml`/`_merge_dataclass`), no special-casing needed, confirmed by checking how `sx1261_spi_path` (a same-shaped existing flag) is handled.
- `src/main.py`: `_add_concentrator_source` now passes `pager_enabled=config.radio.pager_enabled` through.
- `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`: documented the new `radio.pager_enabled` key in both the Radio section and the flat full-config reference near the bottom.
- `docs/CHANGELOG.md`: updated (not duplicated) the existing "Concentrator FSK support" bullet from last step to reflect it's now wired to real capture, still opt-in/off by default, still no dashboard page. Re-parses at 27 sections.

**Sync word revised from 0xF72D91 to 0x946437 mid-session.** User pasted a list of joke 3-byte sync word ideas (a Google-style "funny hex words" list) and asked to pick one. Rather than accepting on humor alone, checked each candidate's actual RF suitability (longest run of identical consecutive bits, and repeating sub-patterns -- both raise false-sync-lock risk against ambient noise) via a quick Python script. Findings: `0xC0FFEE` has an 11-bit run of 1s (bad), `0xAAAA00`/`0xBEE900`/`0xBEEF00` have 8-9 bit runs (`0xAAAA` also alternates exactly like a typical radio preamble -- risks false-triggering mid-preamble), `0x911911` repeats its own sub-pattern (secondary autocorrelation peak). `0x946437` ("PAGER" in hex leetspeak) has a max run of 4 bits, no repeating structure, balanced 11/24 ones -- objectively as sound as the original arbitrary `0xF72D91` pick, and actually readable in a hex dump. Went with `0x946437`.

**Verified for real** (no aiosqlite/Crypto on the Mac, stubbed both per the standing convention -- `sys.modules['aiosqlite']`/`sys.modules['Crypto.Cipher']` as bare fakes, matching how `test_database_migration.py`'s limitation is already handled): (1) `pager_event_adapter.adapt_event()` exercised directly -- confirms `Protocol.PAGER`/`PacketType.PAGER_RAW`/`encrypted_payload`/real `signal` all land correctly, and empty payload returns `None`; (2) `PipelineCoordinator._adapt_pager` (a staticmethod, callable without constructing the full coordinator) exercised directly -- confirms the dispatch branch produces the same correct Packet; (3) `ConcentratorCaptureSource.start()` exercised against a fully mocked `SX1302Wrapper` -- confirms `configure_fsk_channel()` gets called with exactly the right kwargs (`rf_chain=1, rf_chain_freq_hz=869525000, frequency_hz=869462500, sync_word=0x946437, sync_word_size=3`) when `pager_enabled=True`, and confirms it's NOT called at all when `pager_enabled=False` (the default) -- proving zero behavior change for the existing live deployment unless this flag is explicitly opted into; (4) `packets()` exercised with one simulated LoRa packet and one simulated FSK packet returned from the same `receive()` call (the exact "both demods active in one poll" scenario the whole ch8/ch9-independence investigation was about) -- confirms the LoRa packet still gets `capture_source="concentrator"`/`Protocol.MESHTASTIC` unchanged, and the FSK packet correctly gets `capture_source="pager"`/`Protocol.PAGER`.

**Status: real code, tested, still nothing on the Pi.** `pager_enabled` defaults to `false`, so this is fully inert on the current live deployment until explicitly turned on in `config/local.yaml`. Once turned on and deployed, a page arriving on 869.4625 MHz with sync word `0x946437` would now show up as a real row in the packets table (protocol `pager`, undecoded bytes) -- but there's still no Heltec V3 firmware anywhere to actually transmit one, no TX support in the wrapper, and no dashboard page. Next steps, in order: TX support (mirroring this RX work for `send()`), the Heltec V3 firmware itself (this is genuinely new hardware work, not just software), then a dashboard Pager page, then finally deciding a real over-the-air framing so `pager_event_adapter.py` can do more than store raw bytes.

**Real bug found via live testing: pager_enabled had zero effect on the actual running service, 2026-08-03 (same session, right after the capture-source wiring above).** User set `pager_enabled: true` in `/opt/meshpoint/config/local.yaml`, restarted, and the boot log showed a completely clean startup -- but no `FSK channel (ch9) configured` line anywhere, still `Concentrator configured with 9 IF channels` (not 10), still `concentrator (8-ch SX1302)` in the startup banner. No exception, no warning, nothing -- which was itself the key clue, since a real failure inside `configure_fsk_channel()` would have crashed the whole `CaptureCoordinator.start()` (nothing catches exceptions from an individual source's `start()` there).

**Diagnosis went through several ruled-out hypotheses before finding the real one, each confirmed/ruled out with an actual command on the Pi rather than assumed:**
1. Stale deploy? `git log --oneline -5` on the Pi showed `HEAD` was exactly the commit that added this feature. Ruled out.
2. Wrong `local.yaml` (git checkout at `~/Software/meshpoint` vs the actual runtime tree at `/opt/meshpoint`, confirmed as two separate directories on this Pi)? Checked `/opt/meshpoint/config/local.yaml` directly -- `pager_enabled: true` was right there at the correct path. Ruled out.
3. Deployed code missing the feature? Grepped `pager_enabled`/`configure_fsk_channel`/`PAGER_FSK` in `/opt/meshpoint/src/capture/concentrator_source.py` and `/opt/meshpoint/src/main.py` directly -- all present, matching the source exactly. Ruled out.

**The real bug**: `src/api/server.py` has its OWN separate, hand-duplicated `_add_concentrator_source()` (line 598) -- a near-exact copy of the one in `src/main.py`, used by the actual FastAPI dashboard service (`create_app()`), completely independent from `main.py`'s copy (which only backs the CLI-only `run_standalone()` path -- confirmed the user's log is genuinely the FastAPI/Uvicorn path, never `run_standalone()`, by the `"Uvicorn running..."`/`server:`-prefixed log lines vs. the `"Standalone mode"` line `run_standalone()` would have printed instead). When `pager_enabled` was wired into `main.py`'s copy earlier this session, `server.py`'s copy -- the one actually running in production -- was never touched, so `ConcentratorCaptureSource` got constructed there without the flag at all, silently defaulting to `False` regardless of what `local.yaml` said. This is a real gap in "grep before declaring a fix done" applied to Python, not just the CSS-class lesson recorded elsewhere: **`main.py` and `server.py` maintain independent, hand-copied `_add_*_source()` functions for every capture source** (`_add_serial_source`, `_add_dapnet_source`, `_add_concentrator_source`, `_add_meshcore_usb_source` all appear to exist in both files) -- any future change to how a capture source gets constructed needs to touch BOTH copies, or grep for the function name across the whole repo first to confirm which copies exist, since only `server.py`'s copy is what real deployments actually run.

**Fix**: added `pager_enabled=config.radio.pager_enabled` to `server.py`'s `_add_concentrator_source()` (line ~608), matching `main.py`'s copy exactly. `ast.parse` clean. Changelog bullet amended (not duplicated) to note the fix inline with the original feature bullet, since this landed in the same still-unshipped/opt-in feature before it ever really worked. Re-parses at 27 sections.

**Not yet re-verified live** -- next step when picked back up: the user needs to pull this fix onto the Pi (via the dashboard's own git-pull update mechanism, confirmed as the actual deploy path: "git pull directly in /opt/meshpoint via the update web interface") and restart once more; this time the `FSK channel (ch9) configured: 869462500 Hz...` log line should actually appear. A full `install.sh` rerun was already tried during this investigation and did NOT surface the bug (expected -- reinstalling doesn't fix a genuine code gap, it would have deployed the exact same broken `server.py` either way), which is itself useful confirmation the deploy mechanism isn't the problem, only this specific missing line of code was.

**Pager `pager_enabled` mystery deepens: every layer verified correct in isolation, still no FSK channel in three restarts, 2026-08-03 (same session, continuing from the server.py duplicate-wiring fix above).** After fixing the `server.py`/`main.py` duplicate-wiring bug and confirming the fix reached the Pi (git log, direct file grep), THREE separate restarts (14:25, 14:29-30, each preceded by fresh verification) still showed zero `FSK channel (ch9) configured` log line, still `Concentrator configured with 9 IF channels` (not 10), no exceptions, no warnings, completely clean startup through to normal operation every time.

**Methodically ruled out, each with a real command run ON the Pi, not assumed:**
- Duplicate top-level `radio:` key in `local.yaml` (which would make YAML silently keep only the last block, discarding `pager_enabled` if it were the earlier one) -- `grep -n "^[a-z_]*:"` showed exactly one `radio:` section (line 26).
- Stale/shadowed module import (e.g. a `pip install` from `install.sh` having copied `src/` into the venv's site-packages, shadowing the live checkout) -- ran `python -c "from src.capture import concentrator_source; print(concentrator_source.__file__)"` as the actual `meshpoint` service user from `/opt/meshpoint`: confirmed `/opt/meshpoint/src/capture/concentrator_source.py` (the real file), confirmed `hasattr(..., 'PAGER_FSK_FREQUENCY_HZ')` True, confirmed `inspect.getsource(ConcentratorCaptureSource.start)` contains the `configure_fsk_channel` call.
- `load_config()` itself not resolving the flag -- ran it directly, same user/cwd/env (`CONCENTRATOR_CONFIG=/opt/meshpoint/config/local.yaml`) as the real systemd unit: `c.radio.pager_enabled` printed `True`.
- An exception being silently swallowed somewhere between `ConcentratorCaptureSource.start()` and app startup -- traced the whole await chain (`CaptureCoordinator.start()` -> `PipelineCoordinator.start()`'s unguarded `await self._capture.start()` -> `lifespan()`'s unguarded `await pipeline.start()`) and confirmed nothing catches it at any level; a real failure here would produce "Application startup failed. Exiting." from uvicorn, never seen.

**Every proxy check passed, yet the real behavior still doesn't match.** Added one direct diagnostic log line at the very top of `ConcentratorCaptureSource.start()`: `logger.info("Concentrator start() entered (pager_enabled=%s)", self._pager_enabled)` -- this will show, inside the actual live process on the actual next restart, whether `self._pager_enabled` genuinely holds `True` or `False` at the moment it matters, closing the gap between "every indirect check says this should work" and "it doesn't." `ast.parse` clean.

If it prints `False`, the bug is between construction (`server.py`'s `_add_concentrator_source`) and this print, which would be very hard to explain given the source confirmed correct -- would need to re-examine whether `server.py` truly reaches `_add_concentrator_source` via `_build_pipeline` on THIS deployment vs. some other registration path.

**Real root cause found: a THIRD, monkey-patched copy of concentrator startup, 2026-08-03 (same session, resolving the pager_enabled mystery above).** After exhausting every other explanation (config file correct, `load_config()` resolves `True` live, module import resolves to the right file, no exception possible, no duplicate YAML key, `__pycache__` cleared and still no diagnostic line) the diagnostic `logger.info("Concentrator start() entered...")` added at the very top of `ConcentratorCaptureSource.start()` STILL never printed across two more restarts, even confirmed present in the deployed file via direct grep. That was the real tell: `start()` itself was never being called at all.

**Found via re-reading `server.py`'s own suspicious duplicate log lines** ("TX gain LUT configured" appearing under both `sx1302_wrapper:` and `server:` prefixes in every boot log) -- traced to `_inject_tx_gain_into_source()` (`src/api/server.py:1061`), called from `lifespan()` only `if config.transmit.enabled` (true on this deployment, confirmed by the dashboard's own "TX ENABLED: On" reading seen in an earlier screenshot). Its docstring explains why it exists: `lgw_txgain_setconf` must be called between `lgw_configure` and `lgw_start`, and rather than stop/restart the already-running concentrator to inject it later, this function **replaces `conc_source.start` with a hand-written closure** (`_start_with_tx_gain`) that reimplements the ENTIRE startup sequence (`load`, `reset`, `configure`, `configure_tx_gain`, `start`, `set_syncword`, `set_tx_syncword`) inline -- completely bypassing the real `ConcentratorCaptureSource.start()` method (and therefore every FSK-wiring change made to it this session) on any deployment with TX enabled. This is a THIRD independent copy of "how to start the concentrator," on top of the `main.py`/`server.py` duplicate `_add_concentrator_source()` functions found earlier the same session -- the same underlying lesson (grep before declaring a fix done applies just as much to Python control flow as to CSS classes) but one level sneakier, since this isn't a second function definition, it's a runtime method replacement that doesn't show up by grepping for `_add_concentrator_source` or even `ConcentratorCaptureSource.start` at all.

**Fix**: added the same `if conc_source._pager_enabled: conc_source._wrapper.configure_fsk_channel(...)` block into `_start_with_tx_gain()`, positioned the same way (after `configure()`/`configure_tx_gain()`, before `start()`), with the four `PAGER_FSK_*` constants imported from `concentrator_source.py` inside the closure (matching this file's existing deferred-import convention).

**Verified without importing `server.py`** (no fastapi on the Mac, and this file's import graph is far too large to stub) **by extracting the real function via `ast.parse`/`ast.walk` (grabbing the actual `_inject_tx_gain_into_source`/`_find_concentrator_source` FunctionDef nodes from the real file) and `exec`-ing just those into an isolated namespace** -- genuinely testing the exact deployed code, not a re-typed copy. Confirmed: with a fake concentrator source (`_pager_enabled=True`), calling the patched `start()` calls `configure_fsk_channel` with the exact right kwargs AND still calls `wrapper.start()` afterward (no regression to the TX gain feature this function exists for); with `_pager_enabled=False`, `configure_fsk_channel` is correctly never called while `wrapper.start()` still runs normally (confirming zero behavior change for every other TX-enabled deployment without the pager flag on).

**Status: fix committed, not yet live-verified** -- this was an unusually long live-debugging arc (COUNT: roughly 8 restart-and-inspect round trips) that methodically eliminated config, YAML, module resolution, and bytecode-cache explanations before finding the real one, which was architectural (a third hidden code path) rather than a simple typo. Next step: pull + restart once more on the Pi; this time both the diagnostic `Concentrator start() entered (pager_enabled=True)` line AND the following `FSK channel (ch9) configured: 869462500 Hz...` line should finally appear, since the patched `start()` now runs the same FSK logic (though it does NOT include the diagnostic print itself, since that's only in the original method -- worth noting if that specific line still doesn't show, its ABSENCE is now expected and fine, only the `FSK channel (ch9) configured` line actually matters as proof).

**Pager frequency/sync word made user-editable, with a hardware-aware guard rail, 2026-08-03 (same session, right after making ch9 visible on the Hardware page).** User asked whether the pager's freq/sync-word should go in the config, then specifically asked for advice on how much to expose given how tightly the frequency choice is tied to the concentrator's actual hardware -- a good instinct that shaped the final scope.

**Decision, made with the user's explicit input:** expose frequency + sync word + sync word size as editable; deliberately do NOT expose `pager_rf_chain`. Reasoning worked out together: the frequency validator has to stay bounded to the ETSI EU868 "sub-band P" window (869.40-869.65 MHz), and that window only makes physical sense on RF1 in this deployment (RF0 is anchored ~1.2 MHz away at 868.3 MHz for LoRaWAN) -- letting a user pick RF0 here would just produce a huge, hardware-rejected IF offset with no valid reason to ever do it. `pager_rf_chain` stays a real `RadioConfig` field (so a genuine channel re-plan is still possible by hand-editing `local.yaml`), just not surfaced as a UI trap. User's own follow-up ("guard the freq to only use the correct offset freq") pushed this further: rather than only bounding frequency to a fixed absolute range, the save route now rebuilds the actual current channel plan (same `ConcentratorChannelPlan.from_radio_config()` call `_concentrator_status()` already makes) and checks the requested frequency is within `_PAGER_MAX_IF_OFFSET_HZ` (1 MHz, chosen to comfortably cover sub-band P's real +-125kHz span from RF1's anchor while still catching a wrong pick) of whichever RF chain's *actual* anchor -- this catches not just typos but a real latent gap: nothing previously stopped `pager_enabled` from being turned on under a non-EU868 region, where RF1's anchor would be somewhere else entirely (confirmed by testing: US915's RF1 anchor at 907.4 MHz correctly gets rejected for the EU868-only pager frequency, with a clear error naming the actual offset and region).

**Changes:**
- `src/config.py`: `RadioConfig` gained `pager_frequency_mhz`/`pager_sync_word`/`pager_sync_word_size` (all now the source of truth, defaults unchanged from the hardcoded constants chosen earlier) and `pager_rf_chain` (kept, YAML-only, not routed through any update model).
- `src/capture/concentrator_source.py`: `__init__` now derives `self._pager_frequency_hz`/`_pager_sync_word`/`_pager_sync_word_size`/`_pager_rf_chain` from `radio_config` when supplied (falling back to the original module constants otherwise, e.g. direct test construction). New `pager_rf_anchor_hz` property picks `radio_1_freq_hz` vs `radio_0_freq_hz` based on `_pager_rf_chain` -- added specifically so `server.py`'s separate monkey-patched copy could share the exact same logic instead of re-deriving it.
- `src/api/server.py`: `_inject_tx_gain_into_source`'s `_start_with_tx_gain` closure no longer imports the old fixed `PAGER_FSK_*` constants -- reads `conc_source._pager_*`/`conc_source.pager_rf_anchor_hz` instead, so both of this feature's two startup-code-paths (the real `start()` and this monkey-patched replacement, per the earlier 3-copies debugging saga) now stay in sync automatically through the same instance state rather than needing manual updates in two places every time a pager config field changes.
- `src/api/routes/config_routes.py`'s `_concentrator_status()`: ch9's display row now reads `radio.pager_*` directly instead of the old fixed constants, so the Hardware page reflects whatever's actually configured.
- `src/api/routes/system_config_routes.py`: new `RadioPagerUpdate` Pydantic model + `PUT /api/config/radio/pager` route, modeled directly on the existing `radio/advanced` route's pattern (always `restart_required=True`, `save_section_to_yaml("radio", updates)`). Validates sync_word actually fits within sync_word_size bytes, and validates frequency against the live-rebuilt plan's RF-chain anchor as described above.
- `src/api/routes/config_enrichment.py`: new `base["radio_pager"]` block (mirrors the existing `radio_advanced` block) feeding the new frontend card.
- `frontend/js/configuration/radio_pager_card.js` (new): mirrors `radio_advanced_card.js`'s structure closely. One thing caught before it shipped: initially used `cfg-field--inline` for the enable checkbox by copying a pattern from `meshcore_card.js` -- grepped the actual CSS first (per the standing "grep shared classes before declaring a fix done" lesson) and found the real established convention for checkbox rows is `cfg-field--toggle` (used in `hardware_card.js`), not `--inline` (which is for horizontal text-field layouts) -- fixed before the card was ever tested, not after.
- `frontend/js/configuration/configuration_panel.js` + `frontend/index.html`: new card mounted alongside `radio-advanced` under Configuration -> Radio, script tag added.

**Verified for real, in the order things were built:**
1. Extracted the actual `update_radio_pager` FunctionDef via `ast`/exec (no pydantic/fastapi on the Mac) and ran it against fake config objects: confirmed basic single-field update, the sync-word/sync-word-size byte-fit rejection (0xFFFFFFFF doesn't fit in 2 bytes -> 400), a full multi-field update, and the no-op case (empty update -> `saved: False`) all produce exactly the right `updates`/`saved()` calls.
2. After adding the RF-chain-anchor frequency guard, re-ran the extracted function again: a frequency near the real RF1 anchor saves fine, 869.65 MHz (at the edge of sub-band P, ~125kHz from anchor, well within the 1MHz guard) still saves fine, and the same pager frequency under a simulated US915 config (RF1 anchor 907.4 MHz) now correctly raises 400 with a message naming the actual MHz offset and region -- proving the new guard catches a real class of misconfiguration, not just a typo'd number.
3. Re-ran the `ConcentratorCaptureSource.start()` test (from the earlier session) with an actual `RadioConfig` object carrying non-default pager values -- confirmed `configure_fsk_channel()` is called with exactly those config-driven values, not the old hardcoded ones.
4. Re-ran the `server.py` monkey-patched-closure test (via the same `ast`-extraction technique from the earlier debugging session) with a fake conc_source exposing `pager_rf_anchor_hz` -- confirmed it also now reads instance state correctly, proving both copies stay in sync through shared state rather than duplicated logic.
5. Rendered the real `radio_pager_card.js` under plain Node with DOM stubs -- confirmed `mount()` produces no "rf-chain" element (successfully removed) and `render()` runs without error against a realistic `radio_pager` payload shape.

**Status: done, not yet deployed/looked at live.** Next restart + a save from Configuration -> Radio (Pager) should show up in `local.yaml` under `radio:` and take effect on the following restart (everything here is restart-only, same as `radio/advanced`).

**Pager project: TX support added to the HAL wrapper, 2026-08-03 (same session, right after making frequency/sync word editable).** User asked for TX support next, per the build order established since the start of this project (RX first, TX second, firmware/dashboard after). Scoped the same way RX was originally scoped: wrapper capability only, nothing wired to a coordinator/route/dashboard yet.

**Real HAL source read before writing any code** (`extra/sx1302_hal/libloragw/src/loragw_hal.c`), same discipline as every other step this session -- two findings shaped the implementation:
1. **TX is only physically enabled on RF chain 0 on this hardware.** `_configure_rf_chains()` in `sx1302_wrapper.py` already sets `conf.tx_enable = (rf_chain == 0)` -- confirmed this isn't a rule specific to Meshtastic by checking `tx_service.py`'s existing native TX path (`_build_hal_packet()`), which hardcodes `tx_pkt.rf_chain = 0` even though Meshtastic's own channel (869.525 MHz) is RF1's anchor. This means `send_fsk_packet()` must ALSO always use `rf_chain=0` for TX, completely independent of `pager_rf_chain` (which only matters for RX/IF-chain association) -- the RF chain field on a TX packet selects which physical PA path fires, not a frequency restriction (RF0's synthesizer can tune to whatever frequency is requested in `freq_hz`, including near RF1's nominal IF range).
2. **FSK TX reuses the RX-side sync word automatically -- no separate TX sync-word call needed** (unlike LoRa, which needed the whole `set_tx_syncword()` patch because the stock HAL only knew two hardcoded LoRaWAN sync words). Confirmed by reading `lgw_send()`'s C implementation directly: `sx1302_send(..., &CONTEXT_FSK, pkt_data)` at `loragw_hal.c:1435` passes the SAME `CONTEXT_FSK` struct that `configure_fsk_channel()` populates via `lgw_rxif_setconf(FSK_IF_CHAIN, ...)` -- meaning as long as the pager channel was configured for RX (i.e. `pager_enabled` at startup), TX automatically uses the same sync word with zero extra plumbing. `send_fsk_packet()`'s docstring calls this out explicitly since it's a genuinely different pattern from `set_tx_syncword()` and easy to wrongly assume needs a matching TX-side sync-word setter.
3. Also read the HAL's own FSK TX validation (`loragw_hal.c:1394-1406`) to match its exact bounds rather than guessing: `f_dev` must be 1-200 (kHz), datarate must satisfy `IS_FSK_DR` (500-250,000, matching the existing `FSK_DATARATE_MIN/MAX` constants from the RX side), payload capped at 255 bytes. Also confirmed `bandwidth` on a TX packet is documented "LoRa only" (`loragw_hal.h`) -- left unset/zero for FSK, matching what the HAL's own validation actually checks (it never looks at `bandwidth` for `MOD_FSK`).

**New code** (`src/hal/sx1302_wrapper.py`): `FSK_DEFAULT_FDEV_KHZ = 25` (a conservative, not-yet-measured starting point for a few-kbps GFSK link, documented as such -- there's no real firmware to tune it against yet). `send_fsk_packet(payload, frequency_hz, rf_power_dbm, datarate=FSK_DEFAULT_DATARATE, f_dev_khz=FSK_DEFAULT_FDEV_KHZ, preamble=0, no_crc=False) -> int` builds an `LgwPktTxS` (same struct/pattern as `tx_service.py`'s existing Meshtastic TX packet builder) with `modulation=MOD_FSK`, `rf_chain=0`, validates datarate/f_dev/payload-size up front (raises `ValueError` with a clear message rather than letting a bad value reach `lgw_send()`'s own C-side rejection), then calls the already-generic `self.send(tx_pkt)` -- no changes needed to `send()` itself, it never assumed a modulation.

**Verified for real**: constructed a fake `_lib` capturing the exact `ctypes.byref()`-wrapped struct passed to `lgw_send`, confirmed every field lands correctly (`freq_hz`, `modulation=MOD_FSK`, `rf_chain=0`, `tx_mode=TX_MODE_IMMEDIATE`, `datarate`, `f_dev`, `no_crc`/`no_header`, and the payload bytes round-tripping exactly). Exercised all three `ValueError` paths (datarate too low, f_dev out of range, payload >255 bytes) and confirmed the pre-existing "not started" `RuntimeError` guard (already in `send()`) still fires correctly when called through `send_fsk_packet()`. Re-ran the full pre-existing `tests/test_sx1302_wrapper.py` suite (11 tests) -- all still pass, confirming zero regression to the LoRa RX/CRC-filtering paths this file already handled.

**Status: wrapper capability only, same deliberate scoping as the original RX step.** Nothing calls `send_fsk_packet()` yet -- no coordinator wiring, no dashboard "send a test page" button, and critically still no Heltec V3 firmware anywhere to actually receive a transmitted frame. Next steps, in order, per the original build plan: the Heltec V3 firmware itself (genuine new hardware/embedded work, not something this session can do), then a dashboard Pager page (send + receive UI), and only after both of those exist, a real over-the-air framing decision so `pager_event_adapter.py` can decode more than raw bytes.

**Pager project: full dashboard page built (Inbox/Outbox/New Message), 2026-08-03 (same session, right after TX support landed).** User proposed this next step explicitly ("dashboard in networks guarded by Enable pager channel... same idea sort of as the dapnet page, but Inbox/Outbox/New Message tabs"), confirmed to proceed, and separately clarified the ACK question raised earlier ("we can say send, and then when a ack comes back we can even ack it in the display... thats for later") -- this shaped the Outbox schema (a `status` field, not a boolean, so a future real ACK is a new status value, not a migration).

**Research done first, via a background agent, before writing any code** -- mapped the DAPNET page's exact structure (tabs, storage, sidebar/topbar registration, how to reach the live concentrator instance) so the new page mirrors established patterns instead of inventing new ones. Two important findings that changed the plan:
1. **Naming collision**: `window.PagerPanel` / `frontend/js/pager_panel.js` already exists -- the unrelated, pre-existing RTL-SDR P2000/Pagers/POCSAG listener tab (under Listener), nothing to do with the concentrator. Also **`src/api/routes/pager_routes.py` already exists** for that same RTL-SDR feature (`/api/p2000`, `/api/pagers`, `/api/pocsag`) -- caught by the Write tool itself refusing to overwrite an unread file. Used distinct names throughout: class `PagerDashboardPanel` (not `PagerPanel`), file `frontend/js/pager_dashboard_panel.js`, backend file `src/api/routes/emergency_pager_routes.py` (not `pager_routes.py`), route prefix `/api/pager` (singular -- free, doesn't collide with the existing plural `/api/pagers`).
2. **A real gap in the RX adapter**: `packets` table has no `encrypted_payload` column at all (checked `packet_repository.py`'s `insert()` directly) -- last session's `pager_event_adapter.py` stored raw bytes there, which meant every received "pager" packet was actually being persisted with `decoded_payload=NULL`, completely unreadable. Fixed as part of this step, exactly matching the plain-UTF8-placeholder-text convention already agreed with the user: `adapt_event()` now does `raw_payload.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")` and stores `decoded_payload={"text": ...}`, `decrypted=True` (matching DAPNET's own "decoded, not really encrypted" semantics).

**DAPNET patterns confirmed and mirrored exactly**: pages live in the `packets` table only (no `messages` table row) -- DAPNET's own routes bypass `PacketRepository`'s typed methods entirely and hand-write raw SQL (`WHERE protocol = 'dapnet'`) directly against `_packet_repo._db.fetch_all()`; the new `emergency_pager_routes.py` does the same (`WHERE protocol = 'pager' AND capture_source = ?`). One genuine asymmetry from DAPNET, worth remembering: DAPNET has no real Outbox tab because its serial companion echoes a successful send back into the normal receive feed automatically (same reasoning as receiving your own over-the-air transmission) -- `send_fsk_packet()` has no such loopback (direct synchronous HAL call, no serial round-trip), so the send route must explicitly `packet_repo.insert()` its own outbound row, tagged `capture_source="pager_tx"` (vs the real RX tag `"pager"") so Inbox/Outbox stay genuinely separate queries. Reaching the live `ConcentratorCaptureSource` instance reuses the existing `_find_concentrator_source(coord)` helper in `server.py` (already used twice for exactly this kind of need -- `_inject_tx_gain_into_source` and the dangerous-registry restart handler) -- resolved once at startup and handed into `emergency_pager_routes.init_routes(...)`, same convention as every other route module needing a live source.

**Send route's honesty contract** (mirroring DAPNET's `/send` status-code shape but adjusted for what's actually true): `400` for empty text or a `ValueError` from `send_fsk_packet` (bad params), `503` if no concentrator source or `pager_enabled` is off, `502` if the HAL returns a non-zero code, `{"sent": True}` on success. Explicitly does NOT claim device receipt anywhere -- docstring and the frontend's New Message tab both say plainly that "sent" only means the concentrator hardware accepted the transmission, matching the user's own framing of the ACK question as future work, not something to overclaim now.

**Sidebar/topbar gating needed a small new mechanism**: DAPNET's existing `data-requires-source="pocsag_serial"` (`sidebar_controller.js`'s `_applySourceGating()`) only checks membership in `config.capture.sources` -- doesn't fit a plain boolean flag (the pager isn't a capture source, it's a channel on the existing concentrator source). Added a sibling `data-requires-config="radio_pager.pager_enabled"` attribute + a dotted-path resolver in the same method (reusing the same already-fetched `GET /api/config` response, no extra network round-trip) -- verified the traversal logic handles a missing top-level key and a null intermediate value without throwing. The topbar chip (`TopbarPagerChip`) is much simpler than DAPNET's per-device chip: a single badge, purely config-driven (no live companion round-trip to track), fed directly from the same `cfg.radio_pager` block the sidebar gating also uses.

**Pager project: first pager_client firmware written, compile-verified, 2026-08-03 (same session, right after the dashboard page and TX support landed).** User: "now come the fun part... build a pager_client now a heltec v3 so we can send messages and receive messages from the just build emergency pager" -- with an explicit scoping decision: "for now hardcode the freq and syncword right into the ino code maybe we can get it later from the local.yaml" (floated the sync-from-config idea, settled on hardcoding for v1).

**Found `extra/pager_client/` already existed as an empty directory** (created earlier this session, presumably in anticipation) -- the natural home for the new sketch, `pager_client.ino`.

**Reused hard-won ground truth from `extra/pocsag_companion/pocsag_companion.ino`'s own Heltec V3 pin map** (its own comments cite the ESP32 core's board file + Meshtastic's `heltec_v3` variant.h as ground truth, plus two real live-hardware bugs already fixed there) rather than re-deriving: SPI SCK=9/MISO=11/MOSI=10/CS=8, radio RST=12/BUSY=13/DIO1=14 (`SX1262 radio = new Module(CS, DIO1, RST, BUSY)`), OLED SDA=17/SCL=18/its own dedicated RST=21 (NOT shared with the radio's RST -- a real bug in an earlier pocsag_companion draft), VEXT=GPIO36 (active LOW power switch for the OLED rail, must be driven low before `Wire.begin()`/`display.begin()` or the screen stays dark even though everything else succeeds -- exactly the bug pocsag_companion's own history already paid for once), button GPIO0 (active-low, internal pull-up).

**Reused the button UX spec sketched earlier this session** ("Pager brainstorm continued: channel-isolation approach picked, button UX sketched" entry above) -- single-button state machine (idle shows last message; long-hold enters a canned-message menu; short-press cycles options; long-hold in-menu sends and returns to idle; menu times out back to idle after 8s of inactivity; an incoming message during the menu is stored but doesn't yank the display away, "leaning toward wait" as flagged then) -- carries over unchanged from the original ch5-7 LoRa plan since it's about the button/OLED interaction, not the channel/modulation choice that got revised since.

**Real API verification against the ACTUALLY INSTALLED RadioLib 7.7.1 source** (found at `~/Documents/Arduino/libraries/RadioLib`, via `arduino-cli lib list` confirming the exact installed version) rather than guessing from memory/training data -- caught real mismatches before they became compile or runtime failures:
- `SX126x::beginFSK(br, freqDev, rxBw, preambleLength)` (the base class) has NO frequency or power parameter -- but the concrete `SX1262` subclass overrides it with the full convenience signature `beginFSK(freq, br, freqDev, rxBw, power, preambleLength, tcxoVoltage, useRegulatorLDO)`. That positional form is marked `\deprecated` in favor of the newer `beginFSK(const ConfigFSK_t& config)` struct-based API (designated-initializer style) -- used the modern struct form since this is fresh code, not legacy migration.
- **Confirmed against the real SX1302 HAL C source** (`extra/sx1302_hal/libloragw/src/loragw_sx1302.c`), not assumed: `DCFREE_ENC=2` with an explicit `/* Whitening Encoding */` comment (both the RX config path, line 744, and the TX path, line 2704) -- meaning the concentrator whitens its FSK payload bytes, so the Heltec side MUST set `radio.setEncoding(RADIOLIB_ENCODING_WHITENING)` to match, or sync-word detection would fail outright (not just degrade) since a whitened bitstream looks like noise to a non-whitening-aware receiver, and vice versa for what it transmits. Also confirmed `CRC_IBM=0` with an explicit `/* CCITT CRC */` comment -- matches RadioLib's `setCRC()` default polynomial (`0x1021`, the real CCITT polynomial), used `radio.setCRC(2)` (2-byte length, RadioLib's CCITT-matching defaults) rather than guessing a CRC scheme blind.
- **NOT fully confirmed, flagged honestly in the sketch's own header comment**: Gaussian shaping IS enabled concentrator-side (`GAUSSIAN_EN=1`, `GAUSSIAN_SELECT_BT=2`) but the HAL headers never document which real BT value (0.3/0.5/0.7/1.0) index "2" maps to -- picked `RADIOLIB_SHAPING_0_5` as a reasonable middle guess, explicitly called out as unconfirmed and the first thing to revisit if real hardware never receives anything (lower risk than the whitening/CRC findings above -- shaping mismatches degrade spectral cleanliness/edge-case CRC behavior, not whether the link can sync at all).
- `ConfigFSK_t` struct fields confirmed from `PhysicalLayer.h`: `frequency`, `bitRate`, `frequencyDeviation`, `receiverBandwidth`, `power`, `preambleLength` -- used exactly these names.

**Hardcoded radio parameters** (matching `concentrator_source.py`'s `PAGER_FSK_*` constants and `config.py`'s `RadioConfig.pager_*` defaults as currently deployed): 869.4625 MHz, sync word `{0x94, 0x64, 0x37}` (0x946437 MSB-first), 4.8 kbps, 25 kHz deviation, 125 kHz RX bandwidth, 14 dBm TX power (matching `TransmitConfig.tx_power_dbm`'s default, conservative -- well under the sub-band's 27dBm/500mW ceiling, raising it needs a real PA/antenna check not done here). Sketch's own header comment explicitly notes the "get these from local.yaml instead of hardcoding" idea the user floated, as deliberately deferred future work (would need either a provisioning HTTP call or pocsag_companion-style on-device WiFi dashboard, neither built), not forgotten.

**Verified for real, not just written and hoped**: compiled via the actual local `arduino-cli` toolchain (confirmed RadioLib 7.7.1, Adafruit GFX 1.12.6, Adafruit SSD1306 2.5.17, esp32 core 3.3.10/3.3.11 all already installed) against the exact same FQBN `pocsag_companion.ino` uses (`esp32:esp32:heltec_wifi_lora_32_V3`) -- clean compile, 399,742 bytes (11%) flash / 24,316 bytes (7%) RAM, and a second pass with `--warnings all` produced zero warnings at all (not just zero errors) -- genuine confidence the RadioLib API usage is syntactically and semantically correct, not just "looks right."

**Status: compile-verified only, nothing flashed or tested on real hardware yet.** This is the first genuinely new piece of hardware in the whole pager project (the concentrator side has been live-tested via its own TX->RX self-loopback already; this is a second, separate physical radio that has never talked to it). Explicitly flagged in the sketch itself as the next real risk area: whitening/CRC are checked against source and should be right; Gaussian shaping BT is a guess; the button UX and OLED layout have never been tried by human hands. Next step: flash a real Heltec V3 (user already owns several) and see whether it actually receives what the concentrator's TX sends, and vice versa.

**Pager project: capture_source fixed to "concentrator", clear script added, 2026-08-03 (same session, immediately after the firmware card/SF-label/row-click batch).** User spotted a real inconsistency live: the Packet Detail popup showed "Source: pager" for a pager packet where LoRaWAN/Meshtastic packets from the same hardware show "Source: concentrator". Asked me to explain the original reasoning before changing anything (good instinct -- the tag wasn't arbitrary, it was load-bearing for two things), then approved the proper fix once explained.

**Why "pager"/"pager_tx" existed in the first place** (not "because ch9 isn't in the bandplan", as the user first guessed -- that's true background context but not the actual mechanical reason): (1) `coordinator.py`'s `_process_capture()` dispatches by `capture_source` string prefix for meshcore_usb/dapnet/pager, BEFORE falling through to the generic `PacketRouter` -- needed so pager frames don't get trial-decoded as Meshtastic/MeshCore and silently vanish into the non-persisted stray-frame log (the exact DAPNET bug fixed earlier this session); (2) the `packets` table has no `direction` column at all, so `capture_source` was reused as a convenient already-selected column to split Inbox (`"pager"`) from Outbox (`"pager_tx"`) in `emergency_pager_routes.py`'s query.

**The real fix, once agreed**: `capture_source` no longer means anything protocol-specific for pager -- it's `"concentrator"` for every pager packet, sent or received, exactly like Meshtastic/LoRaWAN (ch9 is a different IF chain/channel on the SAME hardware object, not different hardware). Replaced both original jobs with more honest mechanisms: (1) `coordinator.py`'s dispatch now checks `raw.protocol_hint == Protocol.PAGER` instead of the capture_source string (protocol_hint was already being set correctly by `concentrator_source.py`, just wasn't used for THIS branch before); (2) Inbox/Outbox in `emergency_pager_routes.py` now split by `source_id` (a new `_PAGER_SOURCE_ID = "meshpoint"` constant -- outbound rows have `source_id="meshpoint"`, everything else is inbound) rather than the invented capture_source tags -- a real, already-true distinction (who actually sent it) instead of a made-up label.

**Files touched**: `src/coordinator.py` (dispatch condition), `src/capture/concentrator_source.py` (FSK packets now tagged `capture_source="concentrator"`), `src/api/routes/emergency_pager_routes.py` (query rewritten to filter on `source_id` with a dynamic `=`/`!=` operator chosen from the validated `direction` path param -- never from raw user input, only the compared VALUE is parameterized; send route's inserted Packet now also uses `capture_source="concentrator"`).

**Verified for real**: re-ran the same stubbed-import technique as every other `emergency_pager_routes.py` change this session -- confirmed the Inbox query now uses `source_id != ?` with `('meshpoint', limit)`, the Outbox query uses `source_id = ?`, and the send route's inserted Packet has `capture_source='concentrator'`/`source_id='meshpoint'`. Re-ran `PipelineCoordinator._adapt_pager` with a `RawCapture` carrying `capture_source='concentrator'` (instead of the old `'pager'`) to confirm the adapter itself doesn't care what capture_source says (it never did) and the dispatch change is what actually matters.

**Also added, same conversation**: `scripts/clear_pager_packets.py`, mirroring the existing `clear_dapnet_packets.py` exactly (dry-run by default, `--apply` to actually delete, `WHERE protocol = 'pager'` -- this one clause covers BOTH Inbox and Outbox rows in a single wipe, regardless of the source_id-based split above, since both directions share the same `protocol` value). Verified end-to-end against a real temporary SQLite DB built from the actual `SCHEMA_SQL` (not mocked): dry run correctly counts 2 matching rows without deleting anything, `--apply` correctly deletes exactly those 2 (one inbound, one outbound) while leaving an unrelated Meshtastic row untouched, and a second dry-run afterward correctly reports "No pager packet rows found."

**Status: capture_source fix and clear script both done and verified locally, not yet deployed/looked at live.** Next restart should show "Source: concentrator" for pager packets in the Packet Detail popup, matching Meshtastic/LoRaWAN.

**Pager project: real POCSAG-style capcode addressing added, 2026-08-03 (same session, right after the self-echo discussion and the "Source: concentrator" fix).** User's own real DAPNET capcode (2041152) prompted this: "we need a sender and receiptiant from fe 2041152 and to fe 911, then a pager also has one or more id's he listens on fe 911 for emergency and 2041153 as his pager number." Asked first "check how its done with capcodes in the dapnet/pocsag" before designing anything.

**Research finding that reshaped the plan**: DAPNET's own `blacklist_capcodes`/`ignore_capcodes` (`DapnetConfig`) are about filtering *incoming* traffic tiers, not an identity concept -- not the right template. The actual closer analogue is `pocsag_companion.ino`'s operator **callsign**: a user-set value, required before the companion will transmit at all (a real legal-identification requirement), prepended to every outgoing message -- but it lives on the companion's own NVS since THAT board is the actual RF transmitter. For the pager, Meshpoint itself (via the concentrator) is the transmitter, so the better-fitting existing pattern turned out to be Meshtastic's own identity fields (`TransmitConfig.long_name`/`short_name`/`node_id`) -- plain values living directly in `AppConfig`/`local.yaml`, edited through an ordinary dashboard route, no external device involved.

**Wire format decided together, better than my first proposal**: I initially suggested a hand-rolled binary envelope (4 bytes `to` + 4 bytes `from` + raw text). User asked "and put this all in the message? {from... to... text....}?" -- i.e. just reuse JSON, the same convention `pocsag_companion.ino`'s own serial protocol already uses. Correctly better: ArduinoJson is already a firmware dependency (no new library), self-describing/extensible without a byte-layout migration, and the extra verbosity is irrelevant airtime cost at 4.8kbps for occasional pager traffic. Final format: `{"from": <capcode>, "to": <capcode>, "text": "..."}`.

**This also properly solved the self-echo problem from the conversation just before this one** (concentrator's own TX heard by its own RX, discussed as "for now it's fine, but we don't want to see our own messages later, we'll add a real ACK eventually"). Once Meshpoint has its own real capcode, checking "does this received message's `from` match mine?" is a real, correct filter -- not the fragile timing/RSSI heuristic that was the other option on the table. Placed in `coordinator.py`'s `_process_capture()`, same "ignore tier" treatment as DAPNET's own housekeeping-noise filter (neither persisted nor shown), gated on `pager_capcode` being nonzero (unset = check disabled, not falsely matching every message's absent "from").

**Changes across 9 files + 1 firmware sketch:**
- `src/config.py`: new `RadioConfig.pager_capcode: int = 0` -- this device's own capcode. 0 = unset.
- `src/decode/pager_event_adapter.py`: rewritten again (third iteration this session -- raw text -> plain-UTF8 placeholder -> now real JSON envelope). Decodes `{"from","to","text"}`, returns `None` for anything that isn't valid JSON with a `text` key (same "fails to parse -> stray-frame log" reasoning as `dapnet_event_adapter.py`'s own non-JSON-line guard). `source_id`/`destination_id` now hold the real stringified capcodes (matching DAPNET's own `destination_id=str(capcode)` convention), falling back to `"unknown"`/`"broadcast"` only if `from`/`to` are absent.
- `src/coordinator.py`: new self-echo check right after the existing DAPNET tier block, comparing `packet.decoded_payload.get("from")` against `self._config.radio.pager_capcode`.
- `src/api/routes/emergency_pager_routes.py`: rewritten -- removed the `_PAGER_SOURCE_ID = "meshpoint"` placeholder constant entirely (source_id is now a REAL capcode, not an invented tag); `pager_messages()`'s Inbox/Outbox split now compares `source_id` against `str(_config.radio.pager_capcode)` (computed fresh per-request, since it's a real config value now, not a hardcoded string) and returns `from_capcode`/`to_capcode` in each row; `send_pager_message()` gained a required `to_capcode` field on the request model, refuses to send with `400` if `radio.pager_capcode` is unset (mirrors `pocsag_companion.ino`'s callsign requirement), builds the real JSON envelope for `send_fsk_packet()`, and stores the Outbox row with real `source_id`/`destination_id`.
- `src/api/routes/system_config_routes.py`: `RadioPagerUpdate` gained `pager_capcode` (bounded 0-0xFFFFFFFF). Its own `restart_required` computation now only fires for the 4 fields that actually reconfigure the HAL (`pager_enabled`/`pager_frequency_mhz`/`pager_sync_word`/`pager_sync_word_size`) -- `pager_capcode` alone is pure software (read fresh on every send/receive, no HAL call involved), so a capcode-only save correctly reports `restart_required: false` while a frequency/enable change still correctly reports `true`. Verified all three cases (capcode-only, frequency-only, combined) against the real extracted route function.
- `src/api/routes/config_enrichment.py`: `radio_pager` block gained `pager_capcode`.
- `frontend/js/configuration/radio_pager_card.js`: new "My pager capcode" field.
- `frontend/js/pager_dashboard_panel.js`: New Message tab gained a required "To (capcode)" field; Inbox/Outbox tables gained From/To columns; status hint now distinguishes "channel active but no capcode set yet" from "channel active as capcode N".
- `extra/pager_client/pager_client.ino`: added `#include <ArduinoJson.h>` (confirmed v7.4.3 installed, matching `pocsag_companion.ino`'s own version), a hardcoded `MY_CAPCODES[]` listen-list (911 + a personal number, matching the user's own example) plus separate `MY_SEND_CAPCODE`/`SEND_TO_CAPCODE` constants for outgoing canned messages, JSON-encoded `sendCannedMessage()`, and `handleReceivedPacket()` now parses JSON and only surfaces a message whose `to` matches one of `MY_CAPCODES` (silently ignoring anything not addressed to this device, logged to Serial for debugging). `drawIdle()` now shows "From: N" above the message text.

**Verified thoroughly, same discipline as every other step this session**: backend -- re-ran the stubbed-import technique for `emergency_pager_routes.py` covering the full envelope round-trip (JSON built for TX matches exactly, Outbox row stores real capcodes, Inbox query uses the live-configured capcode as the `!=`/`=` comparison value, missing-capcode send correctly 400s); extracted-function tests for the new `restart_required` logic in `system_config_routes.py` (three real scenarios); a from-scratch `PipelineCoordinator._process_capture` exercise (via a minimal fake coordinator exposing only the methods that function touches) proving the self-echo case is dropped entirely (not stored, not notified) while a genuine different-capcode message still stores normally, and confirming `pager_capcode=0` correctly disables the check rather than matching everything. Frontend -- re-rendered the real `pager_dashboard_panel.js` under Node confirming From/To columns render correctly in both tables, all three status-hint variants (no capcode / disabled / active-with-capcode), and that `_handleSend` builds `{to_capcode: <number>, text}` correctly and refuses to fire without a "to" value. Firmware -- **found a second real CI-breaking gap proactively before it happened**: `config_enrichment.py`'s new `pager_capcode` touch would have broken `tests/test_config_transmit_relay.py`'s mocked config the same way the earlier `pager_sync_word` hex-format bug did, just via JSON serialization of an un-set `MagicMock` instead of an f-string -- reproduced the exact `TypeError: Object of type MagicMock is not JSON serializable` standalone before fixing the fixture, rather than waiting for a second CI failure to catch it. Compiled `pager_client.ino` again via the real local arduino-cli toolchain (`esp32:esp32:heltec_wifi_lora_32_V3`, RadioLib 7.7.1, ArduinoJson 7.4.3) -- clean, zero warnings, flash usage grew slightly (399,742 -> 408,098 bytes) as expected from linking in ArduinoJson.

**Real bug caught from that same screenshot**: the Packet Detail popup's Payload section showed only `{"text": "test"}`, missing `from`/`to` -- even though the Mesh section right above it correctly showed "From: 2041152" / "To: 911". User asked directly: "in the payload is no to or from will the receiver still pickup the to and from correctly?" -- a fair question given what the popup displayed. Confirmed and explained: this was purely a client-side display gap, not a real data problem -- the actual over-the-air JSON built by `send_pager_message()` (verified earlier this session) genuinely includes `from`/`to`, and the Mesh section (built from `source_id`/`destination_id`, which the API response always had correctly) proved it. The bug was narrower: `PacketDetailModal._normalize()`'s pager-reshaping branch (added when the API response only had `text`) was never updated when `from_capcode`/`to_capcode` got added to `GET /api/pager/messages`'s response later in this same session -- so the POPUP's own JSON dump was quietly stale, while the real stored/transmitted data was already correct the whole time.

**Fix**: `packet_detail_modal.js`'s `_normalize()` now reconstructs `decoded_payload` as `{from: packet.from_capcode, to: packet.to_capcode, text: packet.text}` instead of just `{text: packet.text}`. Verified with the real `_normalize()` function against a realistic Outbox row shape -- confirms all three fields now present.
