**Pager project: per-unit capcode injection at flash time, 2026-08-03 (same session, right after the live confirmation/display-bug fix).** User's request, in three parts across three messages: (1) "we want a extra input on the companion firmware page pager client firmware where we can iput the capcode of the pager we program... split my capcodes into my capcode and emergency capcodes add 112 to the emergency and of course listen for the my_capcodes and the emergency_capcodes. so we can then tkae the input from the web to use that capcode to flash, then the my_send_capcode is of course the same as my capcode and send to capcode should be out of the yaml the pager_capcode entry"; (2) "my capcodes can be more then one please komma delimited orso"; (3) "so we can make groups, persons, etc etc". Net effect: a single physical Heltec V3 pager can now be flashed with MULTIPLE capcodes at once (a personal number plus one or more group/team addresses), not just one, entered as a comma-separated web field rather than hand-edited into the sketch.

**Design, mirroring the existing POCSAG card's board-select precedent**: `pager_client.ino` keeps `MY_CAPCODES[]` (array, was briefly a singular `MY_CAPCODE` mid-session until the "more than one" correction landed), `EMERGENCY_CAPCODES[] = {911, 112}` (genuinely fixed, NOT per-unit -- stays hand-edited in the sketch, unlike the other two), and `SEND_TO_CAPCODE` (this unit's base station, pulled from the SERVER's own `radio.pager_capcode`, not user-entered on this form at all). `handleReceivedPacket()`'s filter now checks `to` against every entry in `MY_CAPCODES[]` OR `EMERGENCY_CAPCODES[]`. Sending uses `MY_CAPCODES[0]` as "from" (the first/personal entry, by convention -- a group address is never used as a sender identity).

**Backend**: `src/api/routes/pager_firmware_routes.py` gained `_rewrite_my_capcodes()`/`_rewrite_send_to_capcode()` (regex-based, same "rewrite a source-level placeholder right before compiling" idea as `pocsag_firmware_routes.py`'s `_select_board_define()`, just numeric-array/numeric-literal instead of a comment-toggle) plus `init_routes(config)` to access `radio.pager_capcode` for the SEND_TO_CAPCODE side. `CompileRequest` gained `my_capcodes: list[int]` (min length 1, went through the singular->plural correction same as the firmware). Range-validates each capcode against 0-0xFFFFFFFF before touching the file. Wired into `server.py` right next to the existing `emergency_pager_routes.init_routes()` call.

**Frontend**: `pager_firmware_card.js` gained a "Capcodes to program" text field (comma-separated, placeholder "e.g. 123456, 654321") above the existing device picker. `_compileFirmware()` now parses the input client-side (split on comma, trim, `Number()`, reject if empty or any entry isn't a non-negative integer) before sending `{my_capcodes: [...]}` as the POST body to `/api/pager/firmware/compile/stream` -- previously sent an empty `{}` body since no per-unit data existed yet.

**Verified**: extracted the real `_rewrite_my_capcodes()`/`_rewrite_send_to_capcode()` functions straight out of `pager_firmware_routes.py`'s own source (via `ast.parse`+`compile`, not reimplemented/copy-pasted) and ran them against the actual `pager_client.ino` on disk -- confirmed multi-capcode rewrite (`{2041153UL, 555000UL, 555001UL}`), SEND_TO_CAPCODE rewrite, and that `EMERGENCY_CAPCODES[]` is never touched by the MY_CAPCODES regex. Then did the real end-to-end proof: injected those actual multi-capcode values into the real on-disk `pager_client.ino` (not a copy) and ran a genuine `arduino-cli compile --fqbn esp32:esp32:heltec_wifi_lora_32_V3 --warnings all` against it -- clean, zero warnings, 408,134 bytes flash -- proving the regex rewrite produces code that actually compiles, not just a string that looks right. Restored the file to its committed placeholder state (123456/654321) afterward via a pre-edit backup, confirmed via diff that only the two intended lines had ever changed. Pydantic/FastAPI aren't installed in the Mac dev environment at all (confirmed via direct `ModuleNotFoundError`, consistent with the project's documented Mac/Pi split) so the `CompileRequest` model itself couldn't be exercised through real Pydantic locally -- the novel regex logic (the actual risk in this feature) was verified directly against the real route source instead, which is the part that mattered.

**Status: fully built and verified locally (real compile with real injected values, not just unit tests), not yet deployed or flashed to real hardware.** Next real-world test is flashing an actual Heltec V3 with a real multi-capcode combination from the dashboard field and confirming it only answers to those addresses plus 911/112.

**Follow-up gap caught by the user's own reasoning, same day**: user asked, essentially, "if I do nothing, does a flashed pager just end up as 123456, and does an empty radio capcode just end up sending to 654321 -- shouldn't the defaults match so it works out of the box?" Two different answers for the two halves: MY_CAPCODES' "123456" was never a real default -- it's placeholder-only text (gray `placeholder=` attribute, not a submitted `value`), and the frontend already refuses to compile at all with an empty field, so that half of the worry didn't apply. But SEND_TO_CAPCODE genuinely had no matching guard -- `compile_firmware_stream()` pulled `_config.radio.pager_capcode` straight from config with no check, so a box with the (real) default `pager_capcode: 0` would have silently baked `SEND_TO_CAPCODE = 0UL` into a flashed unit -- a base station address nothing listens on, with no warning at compile time. Fixed by adding the same 400 guard `send_pager_message()` already has (refuse if `radio.pager_capcode` is unset) to the compile route too, so a fresh, un-configured box now blocks compiling with a clear error instead of shipping a broken pager. Verified the guard is present in the real route source (via `ast.get_source_segment`) and both branches (0 -> blocked, real capcode -> proceeds) behave as expected.

**Same conversation, user then asked two more things looking at the actual Radio (Pager) card screenshot**: (1) "should we guard the input here too?" (the "My pager capcode" field itself had zero client-side validation, unlike the sync-word field right below it which already rejects invalid hex before save) -- (2) "if you enable a capcode needs to be inserted?" (should turning on the pager channel itself require a capcode). Answered (2) first: recommended keeping them independent -- enabling ch9 only turns on reception, which is a legitimate standalone state (it's literally how this whole feature started, raw listening before any protocol/firmware existed), and the two places that actually need a real capcode (sending, and now compiling) already refuse without one, so coupling enable+capcode would block a harmless "just listen" state for no real safety gain. User didn't push back, so left as-is. For (1), added a client-side guard to `radio_pager_card.js`'s capcode field matching the sync-word field's existing pattern -- rejects non-integer/negative/>0xFFFFFFFF values with a clear message before ever hitting `PUT /api/config/radio/pager`, instead of relying solely on the backend's `Field(ge=0, le=0xFFFFFFFF)` for feedback.

**Pager project: is the EU868-only restriction fixable? Multi-region expansion researched (idea only, nothing implemented), 2026-08-03.** User read the Radio (Pager) card's hint text ("must stay inside the ETSI EU868 sub-band P... 869.40-869.65 MHz") and asked why it's EU868-specific, since they recalled the frequency being "guarded against the bandplan" -- wondering if that meant it already worked for any region. Checked the real code (`system_config_routes.py:129`, `RadioPagerUpdate.pager_frequency_mhz: Field(None, ge=869.40, le=869.65)`): this is a HARD, unconditional Pydantic bound, applied regardless of `radio.region` -- it isn't validating against "whichever region's bandplan is configured," it's a fixed EU868-only regulatory window. The separate RF1-anchor-offset check (`_PAGER_MAX_IF_OFFSET_HZ`) is a hardware-tuning-range check, not a multi-region feature -- for any of this project's five OTHER regions (`US`, `ANZ`, `IN`, `KR`, `SG_923`, none of which anchor RF1 anywhere near 869MHz), the request would already 422 at the Pydantic layer before that anchor check ever runs. So: confirmed the hint text is accurate, not a bug -- the pager channel really is EU868-only today, by explicit design (869.40-869.65 MHz is the ETSI "sub-band P" carve-out, the only reason ch9 gets 500mW/10%-duty instead of the standard 25mW/1%).

User then asked me to investigate whether it's worth expanding to the other regions, floating "though they just can change the freq, not?" as their own guess at the fix. **Answer: no, it's not just a frequency swap** -- researched each region's actual unlicensed-band power/duty-cycle rules via live web search (this session's knowledge cutoff predates verifying current regs, and RF transmit-power compliance is exactly the kind of claim that needs a real source, not a guess) to see whether an EU868-sub-band-P equivalent (a narrow high-power carve-out) exists elsewhere, or whether the whole regional ISM allocation already permits similar power:

- **US (902-928MHz, FCC Part 15.247)**: the WHOLE band already allows up to 1W for frequency-hopping systems using >=50 channels -- no narrow "sub-band" needed at all, unlike EU868. BUT ch9 is a single fixed-frequency FSK channel, not a real >=50-channel hopper, so it almost certainly does NOT qualify for that 1W FHSS allowance -- a genuinely different (and much lower) power class would likely apply to a non-hopping narrowband signal here. Probably the hardest region to get real headroom in, not the easiest, despite the band nominally allowing high power.
- **ANZ (915-928MHz, ACMA LIPD class licence)**: up to 1W EIRP for BOTH frequency-hopping AND "digital modulation" transmitters -- promising, since a single-frequency FSK signal might already qualify as "digital modulation" without needing hopping, and 1W is actually MORE than EU868's own 500mW. Needs the actual LIPD class licence text (not just search snippets) to confirm the exact conditions/bandwidth requirements of that "digital modulation" category before relying on it.
- **IN (865-868MHz, WPC de-licensed SRD rules)**: up to 1W power / 4W ERP, with no explicit duty-cycle ceiling found (unlike EU868's harsh 1%/10% split) -- also promising, arguably more permissive than EU868 for continuous transmission, though bandwidth is capped at 200kHz per channel (specific RFID sub-channels get an even higher 2W ERP allowance).
- **KR (920-923MHz, KCC)**: search results suggest a much lower ceiling, around +14dBm/25mW EIRP for standard channels -- similar to or more restrictive than EU868's BASE (non-sub-band-P) tier, with no obvious special high-power carve-out found. Likely the region least able to support a pager-style high-power channel.
- **SG_923 / AS923 (920-925MHz, Singapore IMDA)**: up to 500mW/27dBm EIRP across the WHOLE band, not a narrow carve-out -- the SAME power ceiling as EU868's sub-band P, but without needing any special narrow window at all, since the whole allocation already permits it. Looks like the easiest region to add next if this gets pursued, since it needs no new "special window" concept, just a wider valid frequency range reusing the existing anchor-offset check.

**What real expansion would require** (this is the concrete answer to "just change the freq"): a per-region power/duty-cycle table instead of one hardcoded EU868 constant, confirming the concentrator's TX gain/LUT config on this hardware actually supports whatever higher power level a given region allows, and -- since this affects real RF transmit legality -- reading the ACTUAL primary regulatory text per region (FCC 47 CFR 15.247, the real ACMA LIPD class licence PDF, the WPC exemption rules PDF, the real KCC notice, the real IMDA TS SRD document) rather than trusting search-engine summaries, before any code ships that lets a real device transmit under a new assumption. If pursued, SG_923 (no special window needed, same power as EU868) or IN (permissive, no duty-cycle ceiling) look like the sane starting points; US and KR look like the two to deprioritize or skip.

**Status: research only, nothing implemented, no code changed.** User framed this explicitly as "maybe an idea", not a firm feature request. Findings sourced from live web search on 2026-08-03 (not primary legal text): [47 CFR 15.247, eCFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-47/chapter-I/subchapter-A/part-15/subpart-C/subject-group-ECFR2f2e5828339709e/section-15.247), [ACMA LIPD class licence page](https://www.acma.gov.au/licences/low-interference-potential-devices-lipd-class-licence), [India WPC 865-868MHz SRD exemption rules PDF](https://thc.nic.in/Central%20Governmental%20Rules/use%20of%20low%20power%20Equipment%20in%20the%20frequency%20band%20865%20to%20868%20MHz%20for%20Short%20Range%20Devices%20Exemption%20from%20Licence%20Rules,2021.pdf), [LoRaWAN KR920 regulatory summary, rfwireless-world.com](https://www.rfwireless-world.com/terminology/lorawan-frequency-bands-korea-kr), [Singapore AS923 frequency band forum thread, thethingsnetwork.org](https://www.thethingsnetwork.org/forum/t/singapore-frequency-band/4662) -- treat these as a starting point for further reading, not a citable compliance source, before actually building or shipping this.

**Branding/trademark check on the sidebar's Meshtastic and MeshCore icons, 2026-08-03 -- not pager-related, but same session.** User asked, apropos of nothing pager, whether meshpoint is "allowed" to use the Meshtastic and MeshCore icons the way it does in `frontend/index.html`'s sidebar. Investigated both properly rather than assuming:

- **Meshtastic (sidebar `#/meshtastic` icon)**: already the official "M-Powered"/"M-PWRD" mark (`meshtastic/design` repo, per the code's own comment) -- confirmed via web search against Meshtastic's real trademark docs ([meshtastic.org/docs/legal/licensing-and-trademark](https://meshtastic.org/docs/legal/licensing-and-trademark/)) that this specific mark was purpose-built by the Meshtastic project for third parties to self-apply WITHOUT needing an individual trademark grant, conditioned only on not being banned from their community. Solid, no action needed -- someone already got this right in an earlier, unsummarized part of this session.
- **MeshCore (sidebar `#/meshcore` icon)**: NOT the same situation. Checked the real local checkout (`/Users/einstein/Software/MeshCore`): MIT-licensed at the repo root, but `logo/` has both a plain `meshcore.svg` (the one meshpoint's icon is cropped from, per the code's own comment) and a separate `meshcore_tm.svg` ("_tm" = trademark) with no brand-usage grant anywhere in the README. Web search surfaced something more serious than a licensing gap: MeshCore is in the middle of a real, ongoing, contested trademark dispute -- a core developer filed trademark applications for the name/logo in multiple countries (AU/NZ/US/China, later CA/CH/EU/UK) without informing the rest of the team, which caused the project to actually split ([blog.meshcore.io/2026/07/04/help-us-save-meshcore](https://blog.meshcore.io/2026/07/04/help-us-save-meshcore), [github.com/meshcore-dev/MeshCore/discussions/2523](https://github.com/meshcore-dev/MeshCore/discussions/2523)). No formal fair-use policy exists -- their own post says they'll write one only if they win the opposition. It's currently unclear who even has authority to grant permission.

**User's decision, informed**: offered to swap the MeshCore icon for a generic mesh/network glyph (this file already has that exact fallback pattern nearby, for other icons with unconfirmed provenance) vs. leaving it as-is. User chose **leave it as-is**, accepting the low practical risk for a small open-source dashboard rather than the current cropped-wordmark icon's rest on MeshCore's now-uncertain "historically liberal" attitude. No code changed. Worth re-raising if MeshCore's trademark dispute resolves (they may publish a real fair-use policy) or if the icon's usage ever expands beyond a small sidebar glyph (e.g. marketing material, a larger/more prominent placement) -- the risk calculus is different for a bigger footprint than a 20x14 sidebar SVG.

**Pager project: dashboard Inbox filtering confirmed (no code change), and a "select recipient from a preset list" idea noted for later (recovered content, originally written 2026-08-03).** User asked whether the dashboard's own Pager Inbox filters by `to` (only showing pages addressed to this device) or grabs everything except our own echo. Confirmed against the real code (`src/coordinator.py:416-429`): there is NO `to`-based filter server-side at all -- the only check is the existing self-echo guard (`heard_from == our_capcode` -> dropped). Every other valid pager frame gets stored and shown in Inbox regardless of its `to` address. The `to`-based filtering (`MY_CAPCODES`/`EMERGENCY_CAPCODES`) only exists on the physical Heltec firmware, which is intentional -- the concentrator/dashboard behaves like a full monitor/logger of ch9 traffic, while individual handheld units are selective about what they surface. No code changed, this was already built the way the user expected.

**Idea floated for later** (explicitly deferred, not being built now): let the Heltec pager firmware's PRG-button flow also select a RECIPIENT from a short preset list (e.g. dispatch/base capcode, a squad/group capcode, 911) per outgoing message, instead of always sending to the one fixed `SEND_TO_CAPCODE` baked in at flash time. Noted that the dashboard side needs no changes to support this at all -- it already renders whatever real `from`/`to` comes through generically (Inbox/Outbox columns, packet detail popup), so "meshpoint can see that" is essentially free once the firmware actually varies `to` per send. The only real work is firmware UI: with one button and no keyboard, adding a second selectable dimension (message x recipient) needs either a two-step "pick message, then pick recipient" flow or folding recipient into each preset entry, to avoid a combinatorial menu explosion.

**Blocked on hardware, not decisions**: user is receiving a new Heltec V3 board in the mail on 2026-08-04 -- this (and any further real pager firmware testing/iteration in general) waits until that arrives.

**Another practical use case floated for later: gate/actuator control over the pager channel, not just human paging.** User's idea: a gate (or similar actuator) could have its own capcode and listen on ch9 like any other pager, but instead of displaying `text` it treats it as a command (e.g. "OPEN") and triggers a relay -- opened from another physical pager, a dedicated one-button sender, or straight from the web dashboard. Worth noting the send side needs no new code at all: the existing New Message tab/send route already sends arbitrary free-form `text` to any capcode, so "trigger via web" already works today with zero changes. A dedicated physical trigger button would want a much simpler stripped-down firmware variant (one hardcoded command, one hardcoded destination capcode) rather than the full `pager_client.ino` menu system. The real caveat: there's still no ACK/delivery confirmation (already a known gap from earlier this session) -- acceptable for a human-readable pager where a person notices a non-delivery, less acceptable for something like an unattended gate where you'd want confirmation the command actually landed. Idea only, nothing built -- also waiting on the same 2026-08-04 hardware arrival as everything else pager-related right now.

**Pager project: Inbox/Outbox Time column truncation fixed, 2026-08-04.** User compared the Pager Outbox screenshot ("Aug 3, 1…", truncated) against DAPNET's own packets table (full "Aug 3, 23:20", untruncated) and asked to fix it, plus check the whole Pager page. `_fmtTime()` in `pager_dashboard_panel.js` is byte-for-byte identical to `dapnet_panel.js`'s own copy -- not a formatting-logic bug. Root cause was CSS: both Inbox and Outbox tables reuse DAPNET's `.lw-table--dapnet-packets` class (good, consistent styling) but their new From/To capcode columns use `col-id`, and `frontend/css/lorawan.css` had no `.lw-table--dapnet-packets col.col-id` width rule at all -- only `.lw-table--dapnet-capcodes col.col-id` (a DIFFERENT table) had one. Under `table-layout: fixed`, two undefined-width columns in the same row threw off the whole column-width algorithm and squeezed the fixed-width Time column down far enough to truncate. Fixed by adding `.lw-table--dapnet-packets col.col-id { width: 90px; }`, matching the pattern already used for every other column in that same table class. Since Inbox and Outbox share the identical table class and column structure, this one CSS rule fixes both, not just what showed in the Outbox screenshot. Reviewed the rest of `pager_dashboard_panel.js` while in there per the user's "check the hole page" request -- status hint logic, tabs, New Message form, RSSI/SNR columns, and row-click-to-detail-popup wiring all looked correct, no other issues found.

**Pager project: WiFi/mDNS/OTA/web dashboard ported into pager_client.ino from pocsag_companion.ino, 2026-08-04.** User's request: "can you also put mdns ota async webserver etc a webpage have a look at pocsag_companion :)". Read the full ~2350-line `pocsag_companion.ino` (WiFi/NTP/OTA section, the whole web dashboard section including `INDEX_HTML`/`setupWebServer()`/the mutex-guarded log ring buffer/web-send handoff, `secrets.h` format) to port the pattern faithfully rather than reinventing it, then adapted -- NOT a blind copy -- for what's actually different about this device:

- **No callsign/licensing gate.** POCSAG's TX is real amateur radio (439.9875 MHz, DAPNET's real frequency) and enforces a configured callsign before it'll transmit at all. ch9 is ISM-band FSK, not amateur spectrum -- there's nothing to license-gate here, so that whole mechanism (callsign validation, TX prefix, the file header's licensing warning) was correctly left out entirely.
- **No NTP.** POCSAG syncs wall-clock time for potential future timestamp fields; this device has no current use for it, left out to keep scope to what was actually asked ("mdns ota async webserver etc a webpage").
- **No serial protocol.** POCSAG is a USB companion with its own JSON-over-serial command set (`{"cmd":"status"}`, `set_wifi`, etc.) that Meshpoint drives; pager_client is a standalone RF device with no USB link to anything, so none of that applies -- WiFi credentials are only settable from the web UI itself here (`/api/wifi`), not over serial.
- **Per-unit mDNS hostname.** POCSAG's hostname is a fixed `pocsag-companion` constant (only one exists per deployment). Pager units are multi-unit by design (per-unit capcodes, comma-list groups) -- computed `pager-<MY_CAPCODES[0]>` at runtime in `setup()` instead, so multiple physical pagers on the same WiFi network get distinct hostnames automatically, no per-unit `secrets.h` hostname edit needed.
- **Free-text send, not callsign-prefixed.** POCSAG's `/api/send` prefixes every message with the operator callsign (identification requirement). Pager's `/api/send` sends whatever text is given, unprefixed -- ties back to the earlier "gate/actuator" and "select recipient from a preset list" ideas noted in this file: a browser can now trigger an arbitrary send without touching the physical button, which is exactly the kind of automation those ideas assumed would be possible.

**Same cross-thread discipline as POCSAG, verified by direct comparison while porting**: AsyncWebServer callbacks run on AsyncTCP's own FreeRTOS task, not `loop()`'s thread, and `loop()` is the only thread allowed to touch `radio` -- so `/api/send` only ever calls `queueWebSend()` (stages a request) and `loop()`'s `checkWebSendPending()` actually calls `sendMessage()`. Refactored the existing button-triggered `sendCannedMessage(idx)` into a shared `sendMessage(text)` (radio TX + logging) + a thin `sendCannedMessage(idx)` wrapper, so the button path and the new web path share one code path rather than diverging. `webLog[]`/`webPassword`/WiFi-credential Strings all go through `stateMutex`, identical reasoning to POCSAG's own (String mutation across FreeRTOS tasks is a real heap-corruption risk on ESP32, not just a stale-read risk).

**Real bug caught by the compile, not by review**: `/api/status` referenced `rxBatchCount`, copied straight from POCSAG's own status handler -- but pager_client never had an RX counter at all (only `hasReceivedMessage`/`lastMessage*`), so this failed to compile (`'rxBatchCount' was not declared in this scope`). Added a real `int rxCount` global, incremented in `handleReceivedPacket()` only when a message is actually addressed to this unit (same `forMe` gate the OLED path already uses, not every frame heard on the channel), and fixed `/api/status` to reference it. A copy-paste-across-files bug that a careful read wouldn't necessarily have caught (both names read as plausible) -- exactly what the real compile is for.

**New files**: `extra/pager_client/secrets.h.example` (placeholder template, mirrors POCSAG's own exactly, minus the callsign-specific comment) added and tracked in git. `extra/pager_client/secrets.h` created locally with placeholder (non-functional) values purely so the sketch would compile for verification -- gitignored (`.gitignore` gained `extra/pager_client/secrets.h`, mirroring the existing POCSAG entry) -- user needs to fill in real WiFi/OTA/web-password values themselves (or copy their existing `pocsag_companion/secrets.h` WiFi credentials over if reusing the same network) before this device will actually connect to anything.

**Verified**: real `arduino-cli compile --fqbn esp32:esp32:heltec_wifi_lora_32_V3 --warnings all` against the actual sketch (not a syntax-only check) -- clean, zero warnings, after fixing the `rxBatchCount` bug above. Flash usage grew from ~408KB (12%) to ~1.17MB (34%) as expected from linking in WiFi/AsyncWebServer/ArduinoOTA/mDNS; RAM usage 54,992 bytes (16%), well within budget. Also re-ran the multi-capcode compile-time injection (`_rewrite_my_capcodes()`/`_rewrite_send_to_capcode()` from the earlier per-unit-capcode session) against this larger file specifically to close the gap rather than just assume it still worked -- injected `{2041153UL, 555000UL, 555001UL}`/`2041152UL` into the real on-disk file, confirmed exactly one regex match each (the declarations themselves weren't touched by this change, so no surprise, but confirmed rather than assumed), then restored the placeholder values afterward via a pre-edit backup and diffed to confirm only those two lines had changed.

**Status: compile-verified only, like the rest of this firmware.** Real-hardware test of the WiFi/mDNS/OTA/web dashboard section is new territory beyond the RX/TX-only real-hardware test still pending from earlier (per-unit capcode flashing) -- both are still waiting on the same Heltec V3 board arriving 2026-08-04.

**Pager project: FIRST REAL HARDWARE FLASH, BOTH DIRECTIONS confirmed working end-to-end, 2026-08-0[4/5].** User flashed a physical Heltec V3 with `pager_client.ino` and confirmed **bidirectional** communication -- messages genuinely go both ways (concentrator -> pager and pager -> concentrator), not just receive. First screenshot showed the dashboard's own Pager Inbox with two real received-at-the-concentrator messages (capcode 2041153 -> 2041152, "Emergency - need help" and "OK", RSSI -16.5/-17.5 dBm); user separately confirmed the pager itself receiving concentrator-sent messages too. This is the first real over-the-air confirmation of the WHOLE stack built this session: RF link (frequency/sync word/whitening/CRC match), JSON envelope parsing both directions, capcode addressing + self-echo filtering (concentrator correctly did NOT show its own TX in Inbox), and RSSI reporting -- all working correctly on real, physically separate hardware for the first time (previously only the concentrator's own TX->RX loopback had been self-tested). User's own assessment: "the client is not yet the best gui but messages go back an forth" -- i.e. the physical pager's on-device UX (OLED layout, button flow) has room to improve, but the actual RF/protocol layer is proven solid.

**User then noticed SNR showing exactly -128.0 on both real rows and asked to check it.** Traced through the real vendored HAL (not guessed): `extra/sx1302_hal/libloragw/src/loragw_sx1302.c:2130-2132`, inside the `IF_FSK_STD` branch of the packet-parsing function, explicit comment "Undefined for FSK": `p->snr = -128.0;` is unconditionally hardcoded for every FSK packet, always -- SNR is a LoRa-only metric on this chip (computed from the LoRa correlator's peak/noise-floor ratio), FSK's demod path has no equivalent. NOT a bug anywhere in Meshpoint's code -- this is the real Semtech-derived driver's own documented "not available" sentinel. RSSI, by contrast, gets a real correction formula two lines above (`RSSI_FSK_POLY_*`) and is genuinely meaningful for FSK, which is why -16.5/-17.5 dBm look like sensible real near-field readings. **Real, not-yet-fixed gap found while investigating**: `pager_dashboard_panel.js`'s Inbox/Outbox rendering only checks `snr != null` before printing it -- doesn't know `-128.0` is a meaningless sentinel rather than real data, so it prints the literal misleading number instead of `--`. Offered to fix (map the sentinel to `None` in the pager event adapter, or just drop the SNR column from the Pager page entirely since it can never be meaningful for this protocol) -- user hadn't responded/decided as of this entry, so nothing changed yet.

**Same conversation, separately: real US-region regulatory research for the pager, going deeper than the earlier multi-region survey.** User asked what frequency to use in the US. Researched FCC 47 CFR 15.247/15.249 specifically (not just the earlier surface-level summary): confirmed our current modulation (narrowband FSK, no hopping, ~60kHz occupied bandwidth via Carson's rule) doesn't qualify for either of §15.247's generous tiers (1W "digital modulation" needs >=500kHz occupied bandwidth; 0.25-1W hopping needs real frequency hopping across 25-50+ channels) -- falls back to §15.249's field-strength cap, which works out to roughly **0.75mW EIRP**, dramatically below EU868's 25-500mW tiers. Recommended 915.0 MHz (band center) as the frequency IF pursued, while being clear power is the real constraint, not the frequency choice.

**User then asked how frequency hopping would actually work, explicitly "dont change anything" (informational only).** Explained the real architectural obstacle: ch9's frequency is an IF offset from RF1's anchor (`_PAGER_MAX_IF_OFFSET_HZ = +-1MHz`, from the earlier EU868 validation work) -- RF1 is SHARED with the LoRa/Meshtastic channels, so hopping the real RF1 carrier across the whole 902-928MHz band would drag every other channel on that chain along with it. Hopping would have to stay within the existing +-1MHz IF window, which only fits ~30 channels at our ~60kHz spacing -- enough to clear the 25-channel/0.25W tier, not the 50-channel/1W tier. Plus a genuine sync problem (concentrator and every pager need to land on the same channel at the same moment) on top of that.

**User then asked about the OTHER §15.247 option (>=500kHz bandwidth, no hopping) and explicitly asked to CHECK whether ch9 can actually pass 500kHz-wide FSK, rather than leave it as an open question.** This resolved definitively, and NEGATIVELY, by tracing register writes in the real vendored HAL:
- API layer looks configurable: `IS_FSK_BW(bw)` accepts values 1-7 (`BW_500KHZ`=6 passes), and Meshpoint's own `configure_fsk_channel()` docstring even claims bandwidth "reuses BW_125/250/500KHZ... values available for the bandwidth parameters (LoRa & FSK)" -- a reasonable-looking claim from an earlier session that turned out to be WRONG.
- The real hardware-programming function, `sx1302_fsk_configure()` (`loragw_sx1302.c:736`), never reads the configured bandwidth value at all: `lgw_reg_w(SX1302_REG_RX_TOP_LORA_SERVICE_FSK_FSK_CFG_1_CH_BW_EXPO, 0x03); /* 125KHz */` -- hardcoded, the ONLY write to that register anywhere in the whole HAL. Whatever bandwidth value Python passes in is silently ignored for the real channel filter.
- For contrast, the "LoRa Service" channel (ch8, `IF_LORA_STD` -- shares a register-name PREFIX with FSK, "LORA_SERVICE_FSK", but is a functionally separate modem/config path) DOES have a genuinely register-level-configurable bandwidth up to 500kHz (confirmed via a real `switch(cfg->bandwidth)` at `loragw_sx1302.c:1024-1037` for SF11/SF12 LoRa rates).
- **Conclusion: wideband FSK on ch9 is a dead end without patching/rebuilding the vendored C driver itself** (not just "unverified," as first flagged) -- the channel filter is physically fixed at 125kHz in this exact HAL build. The LoRa/chirp-spread-spectrum path (moving the pager onto ch8 instead of ch9) is the only 500kHz-capable option actually proven on this hardware.
- **Also found and flagged, not yet fixed**: the existing code comment in `src/hal/sx1302_wrapper.py` (lines 86-89) claiming FSK bandwidth is tunable ("reuses the same BW_125/250/500KHZ... may need tuning") is now known to be actively misleading given this finding -- left untouched per the user's explicit "dont change anything" for that whole sub-thread, but should be corrected if anyone revisits US-region work.
- Also clarified real Heltec board TX power specs the user asked about mid-thread (verified via web search, not assumed): V3 ~21dBm/125mW (bare SX1262, no PA) vs. V4's high-power variant ~28dBm/~630mW (has a real external PA) -- V4 headroom is irrelevant to the current narrowband-FSK US ceiling either way, since that's a regulatory cap on radiated power, not a hardware capability limit.

**Pager project: screen auto-blank + wake-on-short-press added to pager_client.ino, ported from pocsag_companion.ino, 2026-08-0[4/5].** User's request: "we need a timeout for the screen to turn it off, look at pocsag companion they have that, activate sceen on short button presse." Ported pocsag_companion.ino's own display-power section (bool `displayOn`, `lastDisplayActivity`, runtime `displayTimeoutMs` defaulting to the same 10s POCSAG uses, `wakeDisplay()` helper) directly, adapted for one real difference: **no physical manual on/off toggle** -- POCSAG has a dedicated BOOT button free for exactly that; pager_client's single button is already fully committed to the idle/menu/send state machine, so display power here is timeout-plus-wake-on-activity only, no manual override button.

**Wiring**: `drawIdle()`/`drawMenu()` both now call `wakeDisplay()` first (so any real content update wakes the panel if off and resets the idle timer, same as POCSAG), `loop()` gained the auto-blank check (real `SSD1306_DISPLAYOFF` command, not just cleared pixels, so it actually saves power on this battery device), and `onShortPress()`'s previously-dead IDLE branch ("no action defined") now calls `drawIdle()` unconditionally -- which cleanly handles both cases (wakes if off, just resets the timer if already on) via the shared `wakeDisplay()` call, without needing to special-case display state in the button handler itself. `displayTimeoutMs` is persisted via the same NVS `prefs` mechanism already used for `webPassword`/WiFi credentials, and settable live from a new "Screen Timeout" card in the web dashboard (`POST /api/timeout`, same request/response shape as POCSAG's own route) -- a plain `uint32_t`, no mutex needed for it specifically, same reasoning POCSAG's own comment gives (String mutation across FreeRTOS tasks is the real risk, not a single aligned word read/write).

**Small fix caught while adding the HTML**: the input needed `type="number"` (matching POCSAG's own field) but the existing CSS only styled `input[type=text], input[type=password]` -- added `input[type=number]` to that selector, otherwise the new field would've rendered unstyled/inconsistent with the rest of the dashboard.

**Verified**: real `arduino-cli compile --fqbn esp32:esp32:heltec_wifi_lora_32_V3 --warnings all` -- clean, zero warnings, flash usage barely moved (1,165,459 -> 1,167,735 bytes, +2.3KB, as expected for a small feature). Also used this pass to fix two OTHER already-stale claims found while touching the same paragraphs: CHANGELOG.md's pager bullet and README's pager section both still said "not yet flashed or tested on real hardware" despite the live confirmation two entries above in this file -- updated both to reflect the real flash/live-test status instead of re-stating the stale claim a third time.

**Pager project: idle/menu screen redesign (status bar icons, real word-wrap, boot screen), 2026-08-0[4/5] -- same day as the real hardware flash.** User shared a real photo of the flashed pager showing the existing plain idle screen, and asked to make it "nicer" plus add a topbar with WiFi/new-message icons, and separately asked to show the unit's own capcode and add a branded boot screen ("LoRaPager"). Explicitly asked to be ADVISED first ("just advise me please") before any code changed -- gave a text mockup of both screens and flagged one real scope question (a wall clock would need NTP, deliberately excluded from this firmware; recommended relative "Xm ago" instead, which needs no network) before implementing, user approved as described ("no go for it please").

**Implementation, entirely new vector-icon/word-wrap code, no bitmap assets**:
- `drawWifiIcon()`/`drawEnvelopeIcon()`: small 8x8px glyphs built from `Adafruit_GFX` primitives (`drawCircleHelper()`, `drawRect()`, `drawLine()`) rather than a bitmap font -- no extra tooling/flash footprint for two small icons. **Verified the `drawCircleHelper()` quadrant bitmask against the REAL installed library source** rather than guessing (`/Users/einstein/Documents/Arduino/libraries/Adafruit_GFX_Library/Adafruit_GFX.cpp`) -- cross-checked against `drawRoundRect()`'s own four calls (each corner at a known screen position with a known mask value), confirmed `0x1`=upper-left, `0x2`=upper-right; combined `0x3` draws just the top arc, the classic "wifi bars" look anchored on a bottom dot. This was worth verifying properly since there's no way to visually iterate quickly without the real hardware in hand -- guessing wrong would only surface as a wrong-looking icon after a real flash+photo round trip.
- `hasUnseenMessage` (new global): set true in `handleReceivedPacket()`, cleared at the top of `drawIdle()`. Reasoned through when this flag actually matters: `handleReceivedPacket()` already redraws idle immediately if a message arrives while `STATE_IDLE`, so the flag is realistically only ever true for more than an instant in ONE case -- a message arriving while `STATE_MENU`, which deliberately does NOT interrupt the menu (an earlier, already-implemented design decision) -- so the envelope icon's real job is signaling "something arrived while you were in the menu," not a general unread-count badge.
- `printWrapped()`: real space-aware word wrap (breaks at the last space within each line, hard-breaks only if a single word alone exceeds the line width, truncates with "..." past `maxLines`) -- replaces reliance on `Adafruit_GFX`'s own auto-wrap, which breaks at the screen edge character-by-character. Directly fixes a real defect the user's own photo showed: "test emergency paging" wrapped as "test emergenc" / "y paging", splitting "emergency" mid-word.
- `relativeTimeAgo()`: "Xs/Xm/Xh/Xd ago" from a stored `lastMessageMs`, deliberately not a wall clock (would need NTP, which this firmware's own WiFi/mDNS/OTA section header comment already documents as intentionally excluded since the device otherwise has no use for wall-clock time).
- `drawTopBar()`: shared by `drawIdle()`/`drawMenu()` for visual consistency -- title text left, icons fixed at the right edge (x=108 WiFi, x=118 envelope) regardless of title length, divider line below.
- `drawBootScreen()`: new, shown once in `setup()` right after `display.begin()` succeeds, replacing the old bare "Pager starting..." line -- "LoRaPager" in large (size-2) text, centered, plus the unit's own capcode and configured frequency below it in smaller text, also centered (width computed from character count * fixed glyph width per text size, no font-measurement API needed for this simple monospace case).

**Verified**: real `arduino-cli compile --fqbn esp32:esp32:heltec_wifi_lora_32_V3 --warnings all` -- clean, zero warnings, flash usage grew ~3KB (1,167,735 -> 1,170,707 bytes) as expected for the new icon/wrap/boot-screen code. **NOT verified visually** -- there's no OLED simulator in this toolchain, so the pixel-position math (icon box placement, centered boot-screen text, bottom-row RSSI/"ago" spacing worked out by hand to confirm no overlap in the worst realistic case) is reasoned through carefully but genuinely unconfirmed until the user flashes and looks at the real screen. Said this explicitly rather than claiming more confidence than the verification actually supports.

**Status: compile-verified only, like the rest of this session's UI-facing pager work.** This is the first UI/OLED-layout change made AFTER the real hardware flash existed -- unlike everything before it (which was flying blind on a device that didn't exist yet), the user can now genuinely test this quickly and report back what it actually looks like.

**Pager project: real ACK delivery confirmation implemented, replacing the long-deferred placeholder, 2026-08-0[4/5] -- same day as the screen redesign.** User asked "do you remember?" about the ACK feature discussed way back when the Outbox schema was first designed -- confirmed via a memory grep (not fuzzy recall) that yes: the user's own words then were "we can say send, and then when a ack comes back we can even ack it in the display... thats for later," and THAT is specifically why the Outbox `status` field was built as a string (not a boolean) from the start -- exactly so a future ACK could be a new status value with no schema migration. Explained this precisely to the user before proceeding, then designed the mechanism together via several short exchanges (per this session's established pattern for design-stage work) rather than just building it unilaterally.

**Design evolution, real user input at each step**: user's own opening idea was to reuse the packet_id already shown in the packet detail popup ("maybe we can also send a message id with the pageing, we can maybe map it to the packetid?"). Checked the actual code first rather than assuming it'd just work: `pager_event_adapter.py`'s `packet_id=uuid.uuid4().hex[:16]` is invented AFTER THE FACT, server-side, purely for internal bookkeeping -- never transmitted over the air, so the pager device has no way to know or echo it back as literally proposed. Fixed version, which the user then confirmed ("we can send it with the message in json and reply with the same id ack orso"): generate the id at SEND time instead, embed it in the wire JSON payload, let the pager echo that same id back in its ACK -- reusing the SAME field/column, just generated at a different point for a different reason.

**ID length went back and forth, real numbers driving each turn**: proposed keeping the existing 16-hex-char format (consistency with every other packet_id in the app, zero collision risk, negligible airtime cost either way). User asked for actual possibility counts per length (computed: 4 hex=65,536; 5 hex=~1.05M; 6 hex=~16.8M; 16 hex=~1.8x10^19) and initially wanted 5 hex ("5 hex is enough dont you think?"), reacted to the "1mln message ids" number with amusement. Started implementing 5-hex-char ids on that basis -- then the user reconsidered mid-implementation ("should we keep that 16 rather") and asked to confirm the airtime-cost reasoning again ("since you said it doesnt matter airrtime wise?"), landing back on 16 for consistency ("so its all uniform"). **Caught and fixed a real bug from the back-and-forth**: had already changed the code's fallback to `uuid.uuid4().hex[:5]` before the revert decision landed, and updating the DOCSTRING back to say 16 without checking the actual line meant the code and its own comment briefly disagreed -- caught via a targeted grep for `hex[:` before moving on, not assumed fixed just because the docstring looked right.

**Implementation, five files, backend through firmware**:
- `src/storage/packet_repository.py`: new `update_pager_status(packet_id, status) -> bool` -- there's no dedicated status column, so this reads `decoded_payload`, patches the `status` key in Python, writes the whole JSON blob back. Returns False (not an exception) if the packet_id doesn't exist, e.g. the ACK arrived for a message `cleanup_old()` already pruned.
- `src/decode/pager_event_adapter.py`: rewritten to handle two frame shapes -- a real message (`{"from","to","text","id"}`, packet_id = the id if present, else a fresh fallback uuid) and an ACK (`{"from","to","ack_id"}`, no "text", packet_id = the ack_id verbatim so it round-trips straight back to the original Outbox row via a plain lookup, no separate id-to-packet_id mapping table needed).
- `src/coordinator.py`: new branch in `_process_capture()`'s existing pager-handling block, right after the self-echo check -- if `decoded_payload` has `ack_id`, call `update_pager_status()` and return (same "protocol control frame, not a message" treatment as self-echo, no new row created, no notify).
- `src/api/routes/emergency_pager_routes.py`: `send_pager_message()` now generates the id, embeds it in the transmitted envelope, and uses it as the Outbox row's own packet_id (was a separately-generated uuid before). `pager_messages()` now includes `status` in every row's response. Fixed two now-stale docstrings caught while in the file (module-level "there is no real Heltec V3 firmware running the matching protocol yet" -- long since untrue -- and the send route's own "there is no ACK scheme yet" placeholder comment).
- `frontend/js/pager_dashboard_panel.js`: Outbox rows now render a real status-based badge -- green "Acked" (reusing LoRaWAN's own `.lw-badge--join` styling, semantically fitting: confirmed/join = success color) once acked, neutral "Sent" otherwise.
- `frontend/js/packet_detail_modal.js`: proactively updated the pager reshaping branch to also include `id`/`status` -- this exact class of bug (API response gains a field, this modal's reshaping branch silently doesn't) already happened once before this session with `from`/`to`, so fixed it preemptively this time instead of waiting for it to happen again.
- `extra/pager_client/pager_client.ino`: `handleReceivedPacket()` now recognizes an incoming `ack_id` (a reply to something WE sent -- logged and dropped, this device doesn't yet track/expect acks for its OWN outgoing sends, only the dashboard's Outbox does) and extracts a real message's `id` field; after successfully accepting a message (passed the forMe filter), calls new `sendAck(from, msgId)` if an id was present -- builds and transmits a `{"from","to","ack_id"}` envelope, no "text". Acks every capcode match uniformly (personal or shared/emergency, e.g. a 911 broadcast gets acked by every pager that heard it) -- no per-pager "who acked" tracking exists, just one status string, so redundant acks from multiple pagers on a broadcast are harmless/idempotent.

**Verified with real logic tests throughout, not just syntax checks** (same discipline as every other backend change this session): re-ran `adapt_event()` directly against real JSON bytes covering all four cases (message with id, message without id falling back correctly, ACK frame, malformed/non-JSON both correctly returning None). Built a real temporary SQLite DB from the actual schema (same technique as `clear_pager_packets.py`'s own test) and ran `update_pager_status()`'s exact SQL logic against a real inserted Outbox row, confirming status updates correctly while every other field is preserved, and confirming a lookup for a nonexistent packet_id returns False without crashing. Extracted `coordinator.py`'s real pager-handling code (not reimplemented -- pulled directly from the method's own AST via `ast.get_source_segment`, dedented/reindented into a standalone testable function) and exercised it with a fake coordinator exposing only the touched methods, confirming: a real ACK updates status and does NOT create a new stored/notified packet; the pre-existing self-echo filter still works completely unaffected by the new branch; a genuine different-capcode message still stores/notifies normally; ack-matching still works even with `pager_capcode` unset. Firmware: real `arduino-cli compile --fqbn esp32:esp32:heltec_wifi_lora_32_V3 --warnings all` -- clean, zero warnings, flash grew ~650 bytes (1,170,707 -> 1,171,355) for the small ack-send/ack-recognize addition.

**Status: LIVE-CONFIRMED on real hardware the same day, both the positive and negative case.** User flashed this build and tested deliberately, then showed the real Outbox: a message to `2041153` (the pager's own real capcode) and a message to `911` (emergency broadcast) both correctly flipped to a green "Acked" badge; messages to `9111` and `2041154` (addresses the flashed unit doesn't listen on -- typo'd/deliberately-wrong capcodes) correctly stayed at "Sent" with no false ack, since nothing was there to receive and reply to them. User explicitly said the wrong-number cases were deliberate negative tests ("i did on purpose a 9111 to not get a ack"), not confusion -- this is a genuinely thorough validation of the whole round trip (dashboard embeds id -> pager receives, passes forMe filter, sends ack_id back -> coordinator matches packet_id -> Outbox status flips), not just "it compiled." First feature this session confirmed working end-to-end on real hardware on the very same day it was built.

**Pager project: pager_client.ino's on-device menu rebuilt into a real Inbox/Outbox/Send/Settings tree, replacing the old single-destination design, 2026-08-0[5/6].** User linked a third-party Arduino OLED menu example (github.com/upiir/arduino_oled_menu) and asked to reuse it for a proper menu -- "button hold like now open the menu from there we have inbos outbox send settings etc send we already build whta the button hold does now works perfect" -- explicitly wanting the EXISTING working long-press/short-press gestures preserved unchanged, just pointed at a bigger menu instead of straight into the canned-message picker.

**Investigated the actual linked code before reusing anything** (a plain WebFetch on the raw GitHub URL got summarized/truncated by the fetch tool before reaching the real logic -- had to `curl` the raw file directly into the scratchpad and grep past ~1250 lines of PROGMEM bitmap data to find the real `setup()`/`loop()`). Two real incompatibilities found: (1) it assumes **3 physical buttons** (UP/DOWN/SELECT, separate GPIO pins) -- pager_client.ino has exactly one (GPIO0/PRG); (2) it uses **U8glib**, not `Adafruit_GFX`/`Adafruit_SSD1306` this file already depends on -- different API entirely (page-buffered `firstPage()`/`nextPage()` loop vs. single-buffer `clearDisplay()`/`display()`), pulling it in would mean a second, redundant OLED library. Concluded: the button-handling code isn't portable at all, but the VISUAL pattern (previous item dim, current item highlighted, next item dim, plus a thin scrollbar showing position in a longer list) is a genuinely good compact design for 128x64 and simple enough to reimplement natively in Adafruit_GFX -- reused the idea, not the code. Presented this finding plus a concrete menu-structure mockup for confirmation before writing any code (matching this session's established practice for UI work with no live preview) -- user confirmed with "yes build it please" after a couple of unrelated tangents (recapping the earlier US-bandplan FCC research, and drafting Discord replies about project scope -- neither touched code, not written up here).

**Design**: kept the exact same two gestures (short press = cycle, long-hold = select/act) and extended the existing `PagerUiState` enum from two states (`STATE_IDLE`, `STATE_MENU`) to seven: `STATE_IDLE`, `STATE_TOP_MENU` (Inbox/Outbox/Send/Settings), `STATE_SEND_MENU` (renamed from the old `STATE_MENU` -- the existing canned-message picker, internal logic completely unchanged, just relocated behind the top menu instead of being the only long-hold destination from idle), `STATE_INBOX_LIST`/`STATE_OUTBOX_LIST` (new scrollable lists), `STATE_MSG_DETAIL` (full word-wrapped text of one selected list entry), `STATE_SETTINGS` (read-only status). Long-hold dispatch: idle->top menu->(whichever item)->its own screen; from a dead-end screen (detail/settings), long-hold returns straight to idle since there's nothing further to select. `MENU_TIMEOUT_MS`'s existing auto-return-to-idle mechanism (previously only checked `uiState == STATE_MENU`) now applies to ANY non-idle state uniformly -- doubles as the only "back" gesture in the whole tree, since there's no dedicated back button and none was invented.

**Real, free data reuse worth noting**: Inbox/Outbox don't need any new on-device message history storage -- they're just the EXISTING `webLog[]` ring buffer (built for the web dashboard's own `/api/log` endpoint, already logging both rx/tx with capcode/text/dir/timestamp) filtered by `dir`. A snapshot of matching indices is taken once when entering the list (`buildListSnapshot()`, mutex-guarded the same way `pushWebLog()`/the `/api/log` handler already are) rather than re-filtering on every redraw.

**Small things fixed while in the same area**, matching this session's habit of not leaving stale comments behind when found: two leftover comments referencing the old `drawMenu()`/`STATE_MENU` names (in the "Display power" and `hasUnseenMessage` sections, both written during the earlier screen-redesign session) updated to reflect the real function/state names now in use; the header's "Button UX" and "Screen design" sections rewritten to actually describe the new multi-screen tree instead of the old two-state design.

**Verified**: real `arduino-cli compile --fqbn esp32:esp32:heltec_wifi_lora_32_V3 --warnings all` -- clean, zero warnings, flash grew ~2.4KB (1,171,355 -> 1,173,723 bytes) for the new menu/list/detail/settings screens and snapshot logic. Grepped afterward for any remaining `STATE_MENU`/`drawMenu(` references to confirm the rename was complete, not just assumed. Pixel-position math (row spacing, scrollbar track/handle sizing, text-truncation budget accounting for variable-length capcode prefixes) was worked through by hand the same way the earlier screen redesign was -- genuinely reasoned through, not guessed, but **NOT verified visually** -- no OLED simulator exists in this toolchain. Said this explicitly in both the code's own header comment and to the user, rather than overclaiming confidence the compile alone can't provide.

**Status: compile-verified only.** Real-hardware confirmation (does the 3-row scroll list actually look right, does the scrollbar track correctly, does anything clip) is the next real test once the user flashes this build -- same "flying blind until it's actually on the device" caveat as the earlier screen redesign, except this time there's a real flashed unit to test on quickly, unlike that first round.

**0.8.0 kicked off, 2026-08-05: version bump, new CHANGELOG section, and first three UX fixes.** User said "we want to move on and start with 0.8.0" -- last addition under v0.7.9 was the pager work. Bumped `src/version.py` to 0.8.0, opened a `### v0.8.0 (August 2026)` section in `docs/CHANGELOG.md` right after Unreleased/before v0.7.9.

**Learned live, worth remembering**: a plain prose paragraph under a `### v0.x.y` header is invisible on the dashboard's own "What's New" preview -- `ChangelogParser`'s `ChangelogSection` dataclass has no field for it at all (only `header`/`bullets`), so intro prose is silently dropped by the parser, not just visually de-emphasized. User caught this by screenshotting the actual Settings -> Updates "What's New" panel showing "No bullets in this section" despite the intro sentence being right there in the raw file. Fixed by converting the intro into a real `- **Headline.** detail` bullet instead. **Takeaway for future changelog entries: only bullets are ever visible to an operator in the running app; prose paragraphs under a version header are maintainer-only (GitHub/raw file readers), never assume they reach the dashboard.**

**Three small topbar UX fixes, screenshot-confirmed working**:
- **Uneven gap between Meshtastic and MeshCore pills**: root cause was `.topbar__group`'s own `display: inline-flex` beating the browser's built-in `[hidden] { display: none }` UA rule (same "author CSS always wins" gotcha already fixed in `configuration.css`/`rf.css`/etc. elsewhere in this codebase) -- the empty Meshtastic-serial-companion group stayed a zero-content flex item still eating a `gap` slot. Added `.topbar__group[hidden] { display: none; }` to `topbar.css`.
- **DAPNET pill no longer shows board/hardware** ("| Heltec V3") -- removed `boardEl`/`_formatBoard()` from `topbar_dapnet_chip.js`.
- **Pager pill now shows this unit's own capcode** (`p.pager_capcode`, already plumbed to the frontend via `config_enrichment.py`'s `radio_pager.pager_capcode`), mirroring DAPNET's callsign segment -- added a `_sep()` helper (didn't exist on `TopbarPagerChip` before) and a capcode span in `topbar_pager_chip.js`.

**User's next question: why does a new pager message take a few seconds to appear?** Confirmed via grep across every protocol panel (`meshtastic_panel.js`, `meshcore_panel.js`, `lorawan_panel.js`, `dapnet_panel.js`, `pager_dashboard_panel.js`) that **15-second polling (`setInterval(() => this._load(), 15_000)`) is the universal pattern app-wide**, not a pager-specific issue -- every protocol page works this way, none of them push live updates to these table views (there IS a `coordinator.py` `_notify_callbacks`/`on_packet` hook used elsewhere, e.g. `public_radar_routes`, but no protocol dashboard page subscribes to it for its own table). Answered directly rather than guessing; did not change the interval since only asked "is that why," not asked to fix it.

**Pager page gained DAPNET-style stat tiles + CSV export, same session.** User asked for real per-message counters like DAPNET's (Total Pages/Unique Capcodes/Alpha/Tone) and CSV export next to Refresh. Design choices, reasoned through rather than copied blindly:
- **Tiles chosen: Total Messages, Unique Capcodes, Acked, Pending** -- not a literal DAPNET copy, since Alpha/Tone are POCSAG message-type categories that don't exist for pager (every pager message is free text). Acked/Pending reuses the real ACK `status` field from the delivery-confirmation feature built earlier this project, and is arguably more useful here than DAPNET's tiles since it surfaces delivery health app-wide instead of only per-row.
- **New `GET /api/pager/stats`** in `emergency_pager_routes.py`, mirroring `dapnet_routes.py`'s own `/stats` shape (real DB aggregate query, not computed client-side from the already-fetched, capped-at-100 Inbox/Outbox arrays -- matches how DAPNET's own tiles reflect the true full-history total, not just what's on screen). Acked/pending counts are computed in Python after fetching Outbox rows' `decoded_payload`, not via SQL `json_extract` -- checked first that no route anywhere in this codebase uses SQL-level JSON functions (grepped, zero hits), so stayed consistent with the app's existing "decode JSON in Python" convention (`_decode_payload()`, already used by `pager_messages` in the same file) rather than introducing a one-off pattern.
- **New `GET /api/pager/export/inbox.csv`** and **`/export/outbox.csv`**, same `stream_query`/`streaming_csv`/`export_filename` helpers DAPNET's own export routes use (`src/api/csv_export.py`) -- BOM-prefixed, streamed in batches, not buffered. Frontend's Export CSV button exports whichever tab (Inbox/Outbox) is currently active, same `ds = ... ? ... : ...` pattern as `dapnet_panel.js`'s own export button (falls back to Inbox when on the New Message tab, mirroring DAPNET's fallback to `packets` when on its own Send tab).
- **Verified with a real temporary in-memory SQLite DB** built from the actual `packets` table schema (`database.py`'s own `CREATE TABLE` statement, copied verbatim) -- inserted real outbox (acked + pending) and inbox rows, ran the exact SQL/Python logic copy-pasted from the new route code, asserted correct totals/unique-capcode-count/acked/pending and correct CSV-flatten output for both directions. Full route-level test wasn't possible since this Mac has no `fastapi`/`pydantic`/`aiosqlite`/`websockets` installed (confirmed by import failures) -- per this file's own standing instruction, tested the underlying logic with a real DB via plain `sqlite3` instead of skipping verification.

**Status: syntax/logic-verified only, not yet seen live.** No `node --check` failures, no Python `ast.parse` failures, real SQL logic tests pass -- but the stat-tile row and Export CSV button haven't been seen in the actual browser yet (same caveat as every other frontend change made without a live dashboard to test against).

**Real live incident on the deployed RAK V2, 2026-08-05: `sx1261_spi_path` crashed the whole service, not just spectral scan.** User asked why the RF Environment page's Channel histogram said "not available on this carrier. Expected on RAK V2 and SenseCap M1" despite genuinely having a RAK V2 (RAK2287) with `/dev/spidev0.0` and `/dev/spidev0.1` both present. Investigated properly rather than taking the static message at face value: `radio.sx1261_spi_path` defaults to `""` for every board (not a probed capability check), and this fork's own history already proved the SenseCap M1 -- which upstream also marks "unavailable" -- genuinely works once that path is set, so the RAK V2 message wasn't necessarily accurate for this specific unit either. Recommended trying `sx1261_spi_path: "/dev/spidev0.1"` per `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`'s own documented procedure, with the caveat that some RAK2287 revisions route the SX1261 behind the SX1302's internal SPI router rather than a Pi-visible CE line.

**User tried it and the service crashed on startup** -- `ERROR: sx1261_check_status: SX1261 status is not as expected: got:0x00 expected:0x22` followed by `RuntimeError: lgw_start() failed`, buried under ~80 lines of recursive FastAPI lifespan traceback. Traced into the real vendored HAL (`extra/sx1302_hal/libloragw/src/loragw_hal.c:1148-1159`) to confirm this is unmodified Semtech behavior, not a bug introduced by this fork: when `CONTEXT_SX1261.enable == true` and the SX1261 patch/connect fails, `lgw_start()` returns `LGW_HAL_ERROR` and refuses to bring up the concentrator **at all** -- RX, TX, and native relay included, not just spectral scan. This directly contradicts `_configure_sx1261_for_spectral_scan()`'s own docstring promise ("every other concentrator path must keep working even if spectral scan is unavailable") -- that promise only covers the earlier `lgw_sx1261_setconf()` staging call in Python; the real chip-patch attempt only happens later, inside `lgw_start()` itself, where a failure is unconditionally fatal to the whole HAL bring-up.

**Gave immediate recovery steps** (`sed` one-liner to blank `sx1261_spi_path` in `local.yaml` + `systemctl restart meshpoint`) since the box was down. **Deliberately did NOT attempt an automatic Python-side retry-without-SX1261 recovery path** -- reasoned through it but concluded the risk/value tradeoff was wrong: it would mean writing new low-level HAL retry sequencing (`lgw_stop()` + re-`lgw_sx1261_setconf(enable=False)` + retry `lgw_start()`) that can't be verified against real hardware from this Mac, and getting the sequencing subtly wrong on the exact startup path that just broke risks making the *next* failure mode harder to diagnose, not easier. Chose the safer fix instead: (1) `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`'s warning rewritten from soft ("may then refuse to bring up the concentrator") to explicit about real blast radius, with the exact recovery command inline; (2) `SX1302Wrapper.start()` (`src/hal/sx1302_wrapper.py`) now raises a `RuntimeError` that names `sx1261_spi_path` as the likely cause and states the fix directly, instead of a bare `lgw_start() failed` -- purely a clearer error message, no new HAL call sequencing, so no new hardware risk introduced.

**Status: fix is docs + diagnostics only, deliberately not a live-recovery code path.** Not yet verified against a second real failure on this box (the user reverted before I made this change) -- next time `sx1261_spi_path` is misconfigured on real hardware, the clearer error message should be the first live confirmation this actually helps.

**Pager RX/TX totally silent on the RAK V2 unit (both directions), 2026-08-05 -- root-caused as another SPI-latch variant, not a pager bug.** User reported: web UI says pager TX "sent" but the physical pager hears nothing, and nothing appears in the Inbox when the pager sends either -- while the SenseCap M1 unit's pager (same code) works fine both ways. Spawned an Explore agent to check for any RAK-vs-SenseCap board branching in the pager path (frequency, sync word, RF-chain assignment, TX gain) -- confirmed **none exists anywhere**: `concentrator_source.py`/`sx1302_wrapper.py`/`server.py`'s `RAK2287_TX_GAIN_LUT` injection all run identically regardless of board, so this couldn't be a missing "if RAK do X" branch. Also confirmed from `emergency_pager_routes.py:290-296` that "sent" in the UI only ever means `lgw_send()` accepted the packet into the HAL's TX FIFO, never that it was actually radiated.

**Diagnostic path that isolated it**: had the user `journalctl -u meshpoint -f | grep "if=9\|lgw_receive returned\|CRC_BAD\|NO_CRC"` while pressing the pager's send button -- nothing at all, not even a CRC-garbage line, meaning zero RF energy was reaching the FSK demod. Broadened the grep to include `if=8` (Meshtastic, also RF1-anchored at 869.525 MHz) to test whether this was RF1-chain-wide rather than pager-specific -- still silent. This matches a known, already-documented RAK2287 hardware quirk (`docs/ONBOARDING.md`'s existing note: the RAK2287's SPI bus can latch after certain power interruptions, requiring a full power removal, not just `reboot`/`systemctl restart` -- SenseCap M1 doesn't have this issue, which is exactly why it kept working the whole time). **User did a full power cycle and it fixed it** -- confirmed live with a screenshot: pager Inbox showing a real received message (204112 "OK", RSSI -72.4) and Outbox showing the "test" page Acked, both directions working.

**This is a milder, partial variant of an already-documented failure mode** (`docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md`'s existing "Concentrator starts but receives no packets" section, which described total silence across all channels and ended in "module needs replacement"). The new variant is narrower -- only one RF chain (RF1: Meshtastic + Pager) goes deaf while the other (RF0: LoRaWAN) keeps working, and the dashboard still shows every channel "ON" the whole time since that's just the software-side channel plan, not a live RF confirmation. Added a paragraph to that same TROUBLESHOOTING.md section calling out the single-chain variant explicitly and pointing at the power-cycle fix (no module replacement needed for this narrower case) -- did NOT touch the "full silence -> maybe hardware damage" guidance, which still stands for the total-silence case. CHANGELOG bullet added under v0.8.0.

**Separately found and fixed a real, unrelated bug while investigating: the login/setup page showed a stale app version ("v0.7.7") even on units confirmed running v0.8.0.** User caught this by comparing the authenticated dashboard sidebar ("online . v0.8.0", correct) against the same box's own `/login` page ("v0.7.7", wrong) -- and confirmed it wasn't per-device staleness (my first, wrong guess) by showing BOTH the RAK V2 and SenseCap M1 units showing the same wrong "v0.7.7" on `/login` despite both genuinely running 0.8.0. Traced the two display paths: dashboard sidebar reads `GET /api/device/status` -> `src/api/routes/device.py:48`, which already used `__version__` directly (always correct, live). Login page reads `GET /api/identity` -> `identity_routes.py` -> `DeviceIdentity.firmware_version`, fed from `server.py:192`'s `config.device.firmware_version` -- a **config-file value**, not the live running version. Root cause: `DeviceConfig.firmware_version` (`config.py:363`) was designed to *default* to `__version__` but is also a real YAML-overridable field, documented in `CONFIGURATION.md` as "mostly wizard-managed" -- and the shipped `config/default.yaml` template itself had a hardcoded literal snapshot (`firmware_version: "0.7.7"`) baked in, which silently overrides the correct live default on every single install, forever, since nothing ever rewrites it on `git pull`/upgrade. `coordinator.py:355` had the exact same bug feeding the MQTT map-report's advertised firmware version to the public Meshtastic map -- a second, less visible consequence of the same root cause (any public map listing would show this node broadcasting a stale version too).

**Fix**: `server.py:192` and `coordinator.py:355` now both read `__version__` directly (imported from `src.version`, same pattern `device.py` already used) instead of `config.device.firmware_version`. Removed the `firmware_version` field from `DeviceConfig` entirely (`config.py:363`, plus the now-unused `__version__` import there) since nothing legitimately needs it as configurable state -- a device's own running version was never meaningfully "configuration." Removed the stale `firmware_version: "0.7.7"` line from `config/default.yaml` (the shipped template -- this alone stops every future fresh install from baking in a wrong value from day one) and from this Mac's own gitignored `config/local.yaml` dev copy. Updated `CONFIGURATION.md`'s example config block to drop the now-nonexistent field. **The already-deployed Pi units' own `local.yaml` files still have the stale key** -- harmless once this code lands (just triggers the existing "ignoring unknown config key" warning on startup, doesn't affect the now-correct display), user can clean it up whenever convenient but doesn't need to for the fix to take effect.

**Verified**: `ast.parse` clean on all three edited files; `pytest tests/test_identity_route.py tests/test_config_loader.py` (26 tests) pass; `ChangelogParser.parse_file` still parses (28 sections); `load_config()` run for real (not just `_merge_dataclass` in isolation, learning this file already flagged once before with the fan-control section_map bug) confirms `cfg.device` has no `firmware_version` attribute and loads with no warning now that the local.yaml copy on this Mac is also cleaned up. Not yet live-verified on either Pi (both still on whatever they're running until next `git pull` + restart) -- next deploy to either box should show the login page's version matching the dashboard sidebar's.

**RAK2287 spectral scan question settled definitively via RAK's own datasheet, 2026-08-05 (same day as the sx1261_spi_path crash above).** User asked "is there really no way to get this going on RAK2287?" after the crash+revert earlier, and found RAK's own datasheet page themselves (https://docs.rakwireless.com/product-categories/wislink/rak2287/datasheet/). Fetched it: confirms the module is **"one SX1302 chip and two SX1250 chips"** -- no SX1261 anywhere in the document -- and the SPI section documents a single `HOST_CSN` pin, i.e. only one chip-select is wired to the Pi at all. This settles what was previously only a hedge ("some RAK2287 revisions route the SX1261 behind the SX1302's internal SPI router") into a confirmed fact for this exact module: **the SX1261 simply isn't populated on RAK2287, period** -- not a routing/reachability issue, a components-not-on-the-board issue. `/dev/spidev0.1` existing as a device node on the Pi is just the BCM SoC's normal SPI0 CE0/CE1 pair at the OS level; RAK2287 only wires CE0 to anything, which is exactly consistent with the earlier crash's `got:0x00 expected:0x22` (nothing real answering on that line).

**Docs updated with this now-sourced fact**: `CONFIGURATION.md`'s hardware capability matrix splits RAK2287 into its own row (bold, definitive "no — confirmed absent, not just unreachable", datasheet linked, explicit "don't set sx1261_spi_path on this board"), separate from the remaining genuinely-uncertain "RAK5146 / some off-the-shelf concentrators" row (left as "unverified"). Also re-fixed the RF Environment page's "hardware histogram not available" message (both `rf_routes.py`'s `_FLEET_SPECTRAL_SCAN_NOTE` and `rf_tab.js`'s `_histogramEmptyText`, edited earlier the same session after the user called the original wording "misleading" for implying it should just work on RAK V2) -- caught my own mistake in that edit too: it pointed at `TROUBLESHOOTING.md`, which doesn't actually document this at all; the real writeup has always lived in `CONFIGURATION.md`. Fixed the pointer in both places.

**Interesting side-fact surfaced, not acted on**: RAK2287 has **two** SX1250 chips (one per RF chain), not one -- meaning the existing `_configure_rf_chains()`/`sx1302_wrapper.py` assumption that only `rf_chain 0` is TX-capable (`tx_enable = (rf_chain == 0)`, hardcoded for every board including this one) may be a software design choice carried over from whatever board this was first proven on, not a hardware necessity on genuine RAK2287 -- RF chain 1 might well support real TX on this specific module too. Flagged here for later, not investigated or changed this session -- current pager/Meshtastic TX already works via the existing RF0-retune approach, so there's no open problem motivating a deeper look at this yet.

**Status: fully resolved as a documentation/messaging fix, no code behavior change** -- the underlying `sx1261_spi_path` gating and crash-on-unreachable behavior are unchanged (still real, unmodified Semtech HAL behavior); only the in-app copy and CONFIGURATION.md's guidance changed, now correctly discouraging anyone from trying this on RAK2287 instead of vaguely hedging.
