**RF Environment companion built end-to-end: Heltec V3 real-RSSI histogram for boards with no SX1261, 2026-08-06.** Direct follow-on from the RAK2287-has-no-SX1261 datasheet finding above (2026-08-05) -- user asked to actually close the gap with a real device: "can we program a heltec v3 to do exactly that? and then we bind in the companion into the rf enviroment to give the data?" Used `EnterPlanMode` for this (multi-file, firmware+backend+config+docs) rather than building unplanned; two design decisions confirmed via `AskUserQuestion` before planning: **Meshpoint polls the companion** (pull, not push) **over USB serial** (not WiFi) -- matching the existing POCSAG/DAPNET companion's transport (`src/capture/dapnet_source.py`), not the pager's WiFi dashboard.

**Key architectural insight, found during planning (two parallel Explore agents traced the real wiring rather than guessing)**: `rf_routes.py`'s `_spectral_status()` only ever duck-types against `_scan_service` (`.hardware_supported`, `.is_running`, `.scans_run`, `.scans_failed`, `.histogram_payload()`) -- it doesn't care whether that's the real HAL or a companion. So the companion slots in as a **drop-in replacement for `_scan_service` only when the real one is `None`** (i.e. exactly the condition that already triggers `_FLEET_SPECTRAL_SCAN_NOTE`), with **zero frontend changes** (`rf_tab.js` already renders whatever `levels_dbm`/`counts` arrays it's given) and one small addition to `rf_routes.py`: a `getattr(_scan_service, "is_companion", False)` check that swaps in a "via companion, not the concentrator's own hardware" message so the operator isn't misled into thinking the RAK grew a working SX1261.

**Implementation, six real files, firmware through docs**:
- `extra/rfenv_companion/rfenv_companion.ino` (new) -- Heltec V3, RadioLib 7.7.1, same pins/VEXT-before-Wire.begin() gotcha already proven in `extra/pager_client/pager_client.ino`. USB serial only, no WiFi -- polled directly, unlike the WiFi-based pager/POCSAG companions. Newline-delimited JSON request/response (`{"cmd":"status"}`/`{"cmd":"scan","frequency_hz":...,"nb_scan":...}` -> `{"type":"scan_result",...}`), same idiom as `pocsag_companion.ino`. Retunes via RadioLib's `setFrequency()`, samples with `getRSSI(false)` (instantaneous AGC-level reading, valid without packet sync -- verified the real method signature against the actual installed RadioLib source at `~/Documents/Arduino/libraries/RadioLib/src/modules/SX126x/SX126x.h` rather than assuming), buckets on-device into a 35-level fixed-bin histogram (`-140` to `-38` dBm, 3 dBm steps) -- bucketing happens in firmware, not Python, deliberately mirroring the real HAL's own division of labour (scan operation vs. value derivation) so the histogram math (percentiles) stays reusable Python-side.
- **User asked mid-build, twice, for more on-device value**: (1) "show something on the display please" -> added a status/live-band-scan OLED UI; (2) "maybe even show the spectral scan on the display... use it when not connected" -> the live band-scan view (continuous BAND_STEPS=32-point sweep across BAND_START_MHZ..BAND_END_MHZ, default EU868 863-870, bar chart) that works with zero USB/Meshpoint connection; (3) "on button press do a scan and show it, so a user can use it standalone" -> added long-press (>=700ms) triggering the *exact same* 35-bin histogram scan Meshpoint itself requests (extracted the sampling loop into a shared `runHistogramScan()` used by both the serial handler and the button path), rendered with an on-device `percentileDbm()` mirroring `SpectralScanResult.percentile()` so the floor/median readout matches what the RF Environment page would show for the same scan. Three-screen button UX: short-press cycles STATUS<->LIVE_SCAN, long-press (from either) runs a local scan and shows it, short-press from there returns to STATUS.
- `src/hal/sx1302_spectral_scan.py` -- extracted `SpectralScanService.histogram_payload()`'s dict-building body into a standalone `spectral_scan_result_payload()` function next to `SpectralScanResult`, so both the real service and the new companion service share one serialization path instead of duplicating it. One-line, behavior-preserving change to the existing method.
- `src/api/telemetry/rfenv_companion_scan_service.py` (new) -- `RfEnvCompanionScanService`. Self-contained serial transport (reader thread + `Future`-based request/response via `asyncio.Lock`-guarded `send_command()`) modeled on `DapnetSerialSource`'s proven pattern but NOT sharing code with it or subclassing it -- deliberately not touching that already-live, field-verified path for a brand-new feature; also not a `CaptureSource` at all (no packets into the pipeline, this is a telemetry poller closer in spirit to `SpectralScanService`). Polls on the *same* `radio.spectral_scan_interval_seconds` cadence the real service uses (no new interval config), builds a real `SpectralScanResult` from the companion's reply (direct reuse, zero reimplemented percentile math), and also feeds `NoiseFloorTracker.update_from_spectral()` (skipped when `floor_dbm`/`median_dbm` are `None`, i.e. an all-empty histogram) so the Noise Floor card benefits too, not just the histogram.
- `src/config.py` -- new `RfEnvCompanionDeviceConfig` + `_coerce_rfenv_companion_devices()`, exact mirror of the existing `PocsagSerialDeviceConfig`/`_coerce_pocsag_serial_devices()` shape; new `CaptureConfig.rfenv_companion` list field; new opt-in `capture.sources` value `"rfenv_companion"`.
- `src/api/server.py` -- new `_build_rfenv_companion_service()` (mirrors `_build_spectral_scan_service()`'s shape), constructed in `lifespan` **only when** `_spectral_scan_service is None` (fallback, never competes with real hardware), started/stopped alongside it; `rf_routes.init_routes(...)` now receives `_spectral_scan_service or _rfenv_companion_service`. Confirmed `src/main.py` (headless CLI path) never mounts `rf_routes` at all, so nothing needed there -- RF Environment is web-dashboard-only.

**RF Environment companion: Band Spectrum sweep support added, same session (2026-08-06).** After the histogram feature was live-confirmed on the real RAK V2 (above), user saw a screenshot of the Band Spectrum card on another Meshpoint (the SenseCap M1, real SX1261) and asked "what about bandspectrum? like on another meshpoint?" -- correctly spotting that Band Spectrum (`SpectralScanService`'s `sweep_frequencies_hz`/`latest_sweep`, served via `/api/device/spectrum`) is a genuinely separate feature from the single-frequency histogram, one I'd explicitly flagged as deferred scope during the original companion plan. User said "just build it :)" -- built directly (no separate EnterPlanMode this time, given how closely it follows the already-proven pattern).

**Design, reusing the same "Meshpoint decides what to scan, firmware just samples" split as the histogram feature**: new `{"cmd":"sweep","frequencies_hz":[...],"nb_scan":<uint16>}` serial command -- `RfEnvCompanionScanService` sends the *exact same* frequency list `server.py`'s existing `_sweep_frequencies_hz(config)` already computes for the real HAL sweep (single source of truth stays Python-side, same reasoning as the histogram scan not hardcoding a region in firmware). Firmware sweeps each frequency with a small per-point sample count (16, clamped to [16,32] -- deliberately far below the histogram scan's up-to-1500, since a 71-point EU868 sweep needs to finish in a few seconds total, not per point) and replies with only floor/median/p95 per point (not a full histogram -- keeps a 71-point JSON reply small), computed via the same `percentileDbm()` helper the button-triggered local scan already used. Firmware caps a sweep at `SWEEP_MAX_POINTS=128` for time/memory safety -- flagged honestly in both the firmware header comment and `CONFIGURATION.md` that wide-band regions (US915, ~260 points at the default step) get a truncated sweep, EU868 (~71) is unaffected.

**Backend**: `RfEnvCompanionScanService` gained `sweep_supported`/`latest_sweep`/`request_sweep()` -- the exact same duck-typed surface `spectrum_routes.py` already expects from `SpectralScanService`, plus a `_run_sweep()`/`_sweep_due()`/`_sleep_until_next()` trio deliberately mirroring `SpectralScanService`'s own sweep-loop shape line-for-line (same `sweep_interval_seconds`-driven due-check, same event-based early-wake for on-demand `request_sweep()`), so `latest_sweep`'s dict shape (`generated_at`/`duration_seconds`/`point_count`/`points` with `frequency_mhz`/`floor_dbm`/`median_dbm`/`p95_dbm`) is byte-for-byte what the real service produces -- `spectrum_routes.py`'s GET response is identical regardless of which backs it. `server.py`: `spectrum_routes.init_routes(...)` call moved to AFTER the companion-service construction (was previously called too early, right after the real service, before the companion fallback even existed in that code path) and now passes `_spectral_scan_service or _rfenv_companion_service`, exact same fallback precedence as the histogram wiring -- real hardware always wins when it exists.

**Verified**: `arduino-cli compile` clean, zero warnings (364120 bytes, 10% flash -- barely moved from the histogram-only build). 19 tests in `test_rfenv_companion_scan_service.py` now (8 new sweep-specific: supported/unsupported, request_sweep gating on poll-task state, successful sweep envelope shape, timeout/malformed/empty-points all correctly leaving `latest_sweep` unset rather than corrupting it) -- all pass locally via `python3 -m unittest`. New `tests/test_spectrum_routes.py` (3 tests, needs fastapi so can't run on this Mac, will run in CI) confirms a fake companion-shaped object surfaces through `GET /api/device/spectrum` identically to the real service. Full local-runnable suite (83 tests across noise floor/spectral scan/config/rfenv companion) still green after all edits. `ChangelogParser` re-parse: still 28 sections, v0.8.0 bullet count unchanged (15 -- edited the existing rfenv_companion bullet in place to add the sweep + live-verification info, rather than duplicating a second bullet for the same feature area).

**RF Environment companion OLED: fourth screen (on-device Band Spectrum), consistent headers, auto-blank, same session (2026-08-06).** After the sweep backend was live-confirmed, user asked for the OLED itself to also show a band-spectrum-style view ("channel histogram but also a screen with bandspectrum?"), confirmed "maybe have a new page for the rf spectrum" (a dedicated screen, not folded into the existing live-scan view), and separately asked for a consistent header on every screen ("on everypage make a header with what this is") and screen auto-blank after 5s idle for burn-in protection (explicitly citing the already-known pager_client/pocsag_companion pattern by name in spirit, though not by name).

**New SCREEN_BAND_SPECTRUM**: short-press-triggered (not continuous like LIVE_SCAN) -- `runBandSpectrumSweep()` sweeps the same `BAND_STEPS`/`BAND_START_MHZ`/`BAND_END_MHZ` frequency plan LIVE_SCAN already uses, but with a small per-point histogram (`BAND_SPECTRUM_NB_SCAN_PER_POINT=8`, via the existing shared `runHistogramScan()`) instead of one raw sample, giving real median/p95 statistics per point (`percentileDbm()`, same helper the channel-histogram screen already used) rather than a single noisy reading. Takes ~0.6s, run synchronously on screen entry (same accepted blocking tradeoff as the existing local histogram scan). Rendered as two series on a 1-bit display: median as a solid connected `drawLine()` polyline, p95/peak as sparse dots every other point (deliberately not a second solid line -- would be visually indistinguishable from median on monochrome 128x64) -- the on-device equivalent of the dashboard's actual Band Spectrum card (median + Peak(p95) lines).

**Button cycle restructured**: short-press now cycles all three "browsable" screens (STATUS -> LIVE_SCAN -> BAND_SPECTRUM -> STATUS, triggering a fresh sweep each time BAND_SPECTRUM is entered) instead of the previous two-screen toggle; long-press (channel histogram scan) still works from any of the three and always returns to STATUS on the next short press, unchanged from before.

**Consistent headers**: new `drawHeader(const char *title)` helper (title line + divider, called first thing in every draw*Screen()) using the literal dashboard card names -- "STATUS", "LIVE SCAN", "BAND SPECTRUM", "CHANNEL HISTOGRAM" -- so the on-device screen name matches the RF Environment page's own card titles 1:1, recognizable at a glance. Replaced each screen's previous ad hoc title line (e.g. LIVE_SCAN's "Live scan 863-870 MHz", LOCAL_HIST's "Scan @ X MHz") -- LOCAL_HIST's scanned frequency moved to its own content line below the new header rather than being dropped.

**Auto-blank, ported from the same pattern already proven in `extra/pager_client.ino`/`extra/pocsag_companion.ino`** (`displayOn`/`lastDisplayActivity`/`wakeDisplay()`/`SSD1306_DISPLAYOFF` via `ssd1306_command()`), but 5s here (vs. 10s there) per the user's explicit ask, and with one deliberate difference reasoned through rather than copied blindly: `wakeDisplay()` is called from `drawCurrentScreen()` (covers every button-triggered and serial-triggered redraw), but NOT from `stepLiveScan()`'s own direct `drawLiveScanScreen()` call (which bypasses `drawCurrentScreen()` on purpose) -- otherwise LIVE_SCAN's own continuous ~150ms-interval background redraw would perpetually reset the idle timer and the panel would never blank while sitting on that screen, defeating the whole point of "blank when nobody's actually there." User separately confirmed the base "press wakes the display" requirement was already satisfied by this design (every button path already funnels through `drawCurrentScreen()` -> `wakeDisplay()`) without needing a special first-press-just-wakes gesture.

**New files**: `src/api/routes/rfenv_companion_firmware_routes.py` (compile/flash streaming via the same `arduino-cli` NDJSON-streaming mechanism every other firmware route uses -- `_stream_subprocess()`/`_ndjson()` duplicated per this codebase's own established convention of each firmware-route file keeping its own copy rather than sharing one) and `frontend/js/configuration/rfenv_companion_firmware_card.js` (device picker + Compile/Flash/Show-output, no extra compile-time fields since none are deferred-in-scope yet). Wired into `server.py` (import, `app.include_router(...)`, `init_routes(config=config, service=_rfenv_companion_service)` -- reads the same module-level global the RF Environment companion's other wiring already populates) and the frontend (`configuration_panel.js`'s firmware-section dispatcher, `index.html` script include).

**Real bug caught before it shipped**: first draft checked `service.hardware_supported` right after `await service.start()` to report "reconnected" -- but `hardware_supported` only flips True after the poll loop's first successful status/scan round-trip completes (several seconds later, asynchronously), so it would have falsely reported "did NOT reconnect" on every single successful flash. Fixed to check `service.is_running` instead (true immediately once `start()` opens the port and spawns the poll task) -- the correct analog to `DapnetSerialSource.connected`, which is what `pocsag_firmware_routes.py`'s own equivalent check uses.

Actually did rename-then-revert once mid-conversation since the user's second message read as a firmer instruction before their third message walked it back -- ended at the original name, `configuration_panel.js`/`index.html` never needed touching since they always referenced the original name throughout.

No capcode analog exists here, so kept title/"Companion"/anchor-frequency (`DEFAULT_FREQ_MHZ`) as the three lines -- same spirit (title plus two lines of real device info), still centered via `getTextBounds()` (already the technique this file used, more robust than pager's manual "N chars * fixed glyph width" math). `arduino-cli compile` clean, zero warnings, +236 bytes flash. Also clarified for the user, mid-conversation, that the earlier header/BAND-SPECTRUM/auto-blank OLED work they weren't seeing on the real device was a stale-firmware issue, not a code issue -- confirmed by grepping the current .ino for `drawHeader(` call sites (all four present) -- the board simply hadn't been reflashed since those changes landed.

**Real bug found and fixed: rfenv_companion.ino's OLED never showed ANY text, from the very first flash -- root-caused, not guessed, 2026-08-06.** User reported (after several rounds of me wrongly chasing a stale-firmware theory) that after a genuinely fresh, hash-verified flash via the new Configuration -> Firmware card, the OLED showed "no text, no header, no waiting for meshpoint... only a stripe line, a scan line and an empty page" -- i.e. lines/bars rendered but ALL text was invisible, and this had been true since the first version, not a new regression (they'd never actually visually confirmed the OLED at any point this session -- every earlier "verified" moment was the Meshpoint dashboard or Serial Monitor JSON, never a photo of the physical screen's own text rendering).

**Root cause, confirmed against the real installed library source rather than pattern-matched from pager_client.ino's own working code**: `Adafruit_SSD1306::drawPixel()` (`~/Documents/Arduino/libraries/Adafruit_SSD1306/Adafruit_SSD1306.cpp:659-687`) is a plain `switch(color)` with exactly three cases -- `SSD1306_WHITE=1`, `SSD1306_BLACK=0`, `SSD1306_INVERSE=2` -- and NO default case. `Adafruit_GFX`'s own constructor (`Adafruit_GFX.cpp:116`) defaults `textcolor = textbgcolor = 0xFFFF` (a generic RGB565-style default, meaningless for this monochrome driver's tiny enum) UNLESS `setTextColor()` is explicitly called to override it. `rfenv_companion.ino` never called `setTextColor()` anywhere, so every `print()`/`println()` glyph pixel silently hit the switch's no-op fallthrough -- literally nothing written to the buffer, not garbage, just untouched. Meanwhile every `drawFastHLine()`/`fillRect()` call in the same file always passes `SSD1306_WHITE` explicitly as an argument (never relies on the ambient text-color state), so lines/bars rendered fine the whole time -- exactly matching the user's own description ("stripe line, scan line, empty page" = graphics visible, text invisible).

**Fix**: one line, `display.setTextColor(SSD1306_WHITE);`, added once in `setup()` right after `display.begin()` succeeds (before `drawBootScreen()`) -- persists for the rest of the program since it's object state, so it fixes the boot screen, all four screen headers, and every other text draw in one shot. `pager_client.ino`'s own boot screen already does call this (confirmed via grep) -- explains why THAT device's text has always worked while this one never did, since the two firmwares otherwise share the same OLED init sequence. `arduino-cli compile` clean, zero warnings, +12 bytes.

**Process note for future sessions**: this whole detour (several rounds of "did you reflash / stale build / IDE buffer" questions) happened because I never actually confirmed the OLED text rendering myself and kept assuming compile-success + prior dashboard-side verification meant the physical screen was fine too -- it wasn't, and no one had actually looked at real rendered text on this device before this exchange. Lesson: "compiles clean" and "the backend/dashboard shows real data" are NOT evidence that on-device UI text actually renders -- don't claim OLED work is done without an explicit user confirmation of what's physically on the screen, and when a user reports something not showing, verify against real library source before re-asking the same "did you flash it right" question multiple times.

**Status: fix compile-verified only, not yet re-flashed/confirmed on real hardware.** Next step is the user's own reflash (now proven easy via the new Configuration -> Firmware card) and an actual look at the physical screen -- first real visual confirmation of the OLED work this whole session.

**RF Environment companion: 70cm/EU868 band selector added to the firmware card, same session (2026-08-06).** User asked if a 433/868 band selector would be "overkill" for a second, standalone 430 MHz amateur-band handheld scanner (spare Heltec V3 hardware, ham radio interest in "what's in the 430 band"). Gave a brief recommendation first per this session's own exploratory-question convention (not overkill, small well-scoped addition following an already-proven pattern) and flagged the key scoping point before building: a 70cm-flashed board is a SEPARATE physical device for standalone scanning only -- it can never feed a Meshpoint box's own RF Environment page, since that page always reflects the concentrator's own operating band (868/915/etc), not whatever the companion happens to be tuned for. User confirmed that's exactly the intent.

**Implementation mirrors POCSAG's existing board-select mechanism exactly, just for band instead of board** (user asked mid-build what "extend rfenv_companion_firmware_routes.py with band discovery/select" actually meant -- explained the two-step discovery/rewrite-before-compile idea in plain terms before continuing):

New `BAND_NAME_STR` ("eu868"/"70cm") added to the `{"cmd":"status"}` reply.
- Backend (`rfenv_companion_firmware_routes.py`): added `_KNOWN_BANDS`, `_BAND_DEFINE_RE`, `_discover_band_targets()`, `_select_band_define()` -- line-for-line the same shape as `pocsag_firmware_routes.py`'s own `_KNOWN_BOARDS`/`_BOARD_DEFINE_RE`/`_discover_board_targets()`/`_select_board_define()`, just `BAND_` prefix instead of `BOARD_`. `/targets` now also returns `bands`; `/compile/stream` gained a required `band_macro` body field, rewrites the sketch's toggle before compiling.

**Implementation, closely mirroring pocsag_companion.ino's proven mechanism, adapted for this device's data**:
- `secrets.h.example`/`secrets.h` (both already existed, header comments still said "for pocsag_companion.ino" -- fixed to reference this sketch; 4-key format already matched POCSAG's exact template, no structural change needed).
- New `==== WiFi / mDNS / OTA / Preferences / web dashboard ====` section: `setupWifiOta()` ported verbatim from POCSAG's `setupWifiNtpOta()` minus NTP (this device has no wall-clock need, same reasoning `pager_client.ino`'s own header comment already gives for its own NTP exclusion) -- non-blocking on no-credentials/failed-connect, exactly like POCSAG. `MDNS_HOSTNAME "rfenv-companion"` (fixed, not per-unit like pager_client's capcode-based hostname -- no per-unit identity concept here). `PREFS_NAMESPACE "rfenv"`, keys `web_password`/`wifi_ssid`/`wifi_pass` (no callsign key, confirmed not applicable). Same `SemaphoreHandle_t stateMutex` + `xSemaphoreTake/Give` bracket pattern POCSAG/pager_client both use.
- **New pattern this device needed that POCSAG's own reference didn't have**: web-triggered Scan/Sweep buttons. POCSAG's only web-triggered radio action is TX send (`queueWebSend()`/`checkWebSendPending()`); added the identical staging pattern twice more -- `queueWebScan()`/`checkWebScanPending()` (calls the existing `runLocalHistScan()`) and `queueWebSweep()`/`checkWebSweepPending()` (calls the existing `runBandSpectrumSweep()`) -- both mutex-guarded, both called every `loop()` pass, so a web handler never touches `radio` directly, same discipline as everything else in this file.
- `INDEX_HTML`: single-page password-gated dashboard (Status / Channel Histogram / Band Spectrum / WiFi Credentials cards), hand-rolled `<canvas>` bar chart (histogram) and line chart (median + p95 sweep, mirroring the OLED's own BAND SPECTRUM screen's two-series idea) -- no Chart.js/CDN, matching POCSAG's own "LAN-only device" rationale. Same `X-Auth-Password` header + `sessionStorage` auth pattern as POCSAG's real JS, copied structurally then adapted for this device's own `/api/status` shape (histogram + sweep arrays, WiFi info, uptime, last-Meshpoint-poll).
- Routes: `/`, `/api/whoami` (unauth), `/api/status`, `/api/scan`, `/api/sweep`, `/api/wifi` (mirrors pager_client's own addition -- POCSAG deliberately omits this to avoid self-lockout, but this device's portable-scanner use case makes it worth the tradeoff, same call pager_client already made), `/api/reboot`. POST-with-body routes use the exact same request/body-callback split AsyncWebServer requires, copied from POCSAG's own `/api/send`/`/api/timeout` handlers rather than guessed (this API shape is notoriously version-finicky).
- Wired into `setup()` (mutex created first thing, `prefs.begin()` + NVS-override loading right after radio init, `setupWifiOta()` last so a slow/failed WiFi connect never blocks core RF function) and `loop()` (`ArduinoOTA.handle()` gated on `wifiConnected`, the two new pending-action checks, reboot-delay check) -- same ordering POCSAG's own `setup()`/`loop()` use.

**Real bug found from the frequency-axis screenshot, same session (2026-08-06): "Scan now"/"Sweep now" left "Scanning…"/"Sweeping…" stuck on screen forever.** User noticed it said "Sweeping..." despite the sweep clearly having completed (fresh chart data, real "30s ago" timestamp visible). Root cause: `scanNow()`/`sweepNow()` set the status text then scheduled exactly ONE re-poll via a bare `setTimeout(pollStatus, 1500/2000)` -- `pollStatus()` itself never touched `#scanResult`/`#sweepResult`, so nothing ever cleared the "in progress" text regardless of whether the action actually finished. Fixed by extracting a shared `runAndAwaitFresh()` helper that polls every 1s (up to 12 tries) checking whether the relevant result's own `age_s` has come back small enough to mean "just landed" (`<=2s`), only then declaring "Done." (or "Still running?" after giving up) -- same poll-until-the-real-thing-changed idea the actual Meshpoint dashboard's own Band Spectrum card already uses for its own "Sweep now" button (`radio_spectrum_card.js`'s `_sweepNow()`, tracks `generated_at` across polls). Also made `pollStatus()` return the parsed status object so the polling loop can inspect it directly instead of re-fetching or scraping rendered DOM text.

Verified both ways again: real `arduino-cli compile` (clean, zero warnings) AND extracted+`node --check`'d the actual embedded `<script>` JS text (clean) -- same double-verification discipline as the frequency-axis fix just before it, since the C++ compiler genuinely cannot see inside the raw string to catch a JS mistake.

**Feature A -- frequency-targeted web scan**: `runLocalHistScan()` split into a parameterized `runLocalHistScanAt(freqHz)` (does the actual scan+store) plus a thin wrapper preserving the OLED button's existing last-requested-or-default behavior. `queueWebScan()` gained a `freqHz` param (0 = default logic, non-zero = explicit target), stored in a new mutex-guarded `webScanFrequencyHz` global, read by `checkWebScanPending()`. `/api/scan` route upgraded from a bare POST to the request/body-callback split (optional `{"frequency_mhz":...}` body). New per-band `WEB_SCAN_DEFAULT_MHZ` constant to pre-fill the web input sensibly -- user specifically asked for "meshcore freq for 868, pocsag for 433": used `DEFAULT_FREQ_MHZ` (869.525, the existing shared Meshtastic/MeshCore-area anchor -- this firmware has no live knowledge of a deployment's own actual MeshCore frequency, which is region/config-resolved by Meshpoint itself at runtime, not a fixed constant anywhere in this codebase) for EU868, and DAPNET's real 439.9875 MHz (same constant `pocsag_companion.ino` already uses, a genuine real-world standard not a guess) for 70cm. `/api/status` gained `web_scan_default_mhz`; frontend pre-fills a new `#scanFreq` input once on first poll (only if still empty, tracked via a `scanFreqPrefilled` flag so it never fights a value the user's actively typing), `scanNow()` reads and parses it into the POST body.

Closes the real gap the WiFi/web-dashboard build left open: a board flashed with placeholder `secrets.h` had no way to get real credentials without a recompile+reflash, since the web UI's own `/api/wifi` route obviously can't be reached before WiFi is even connected -- USB serial (already the primary Meshpoint-polling channel) works regardless of WiFi state, so it doubles as the provisioning path, exactly the same reasoning POCSAG's own header comment gives for its identical commands.

**RF Environment companion: fixed "Save failed" on the Live Device Commands panel, and reworked it to target the picked port directly, same session (2026-08-06).** User's first live use of the Live Device Commands panel (WiFi/web-password Save) failed with a toast "Save failed: No reply from companion (timed out)" -- screenshot confirmed. Root cause: the panel and its backend gate (`_require_connected()`) both relayed exclusively through the one already-configured, already-connected `RfEnvCompanionScanService` (`capture.rfenv_companion`) -- so any board that wasn't already that exact configured/connected device (e.g. a freshly-flashed board not yet registered as a companion, or connected on a different port) had nothing to relay to, and the request deterministically timed out waiting for a reply from a device that was never asked. User's own fix direction: "but just use the coosen port and send the command" -- i.e. target whatever port is already selected in the same card's "Device to flash" picker, not the configured companion.

**Reworked accordingly**: `src/api/routes/rfenv_companion_config_routes.py` rewritten -- every route (`PUT .../wifi`, `PUT .../web-password`, `POST .../reboot`) now takes an explicit `port` in the request body and opens its own short-lived one-off `pyserial` connection (`_blocking_send()`, run via `asyncio.to_thread` since pyserial blocks) to write the command and read for a matching `type`-tagged JSON reply, then closes -- same wire parsing `RfEnvCompanionScanService`'s own reader thread does, deliberately not shared code (one-shot vs. long-lived-with-pending-future). If the selected port happens to be the currently-configured companion's own port (checked via a new public `RfEnvCompanionScanService.port` property), the live service is briefly `stop()`ped first so the one-off connection doesn't collide with it, then `start()`ed again after -- same release/reconnect pattern `rfenv_companion_firmware_routes.py`'s own flash route already established for the identical reason. Port is validated against `list_serial_ports_with_stable_paths()` (mirrors the flash route's own validation) before anything is attempted.

**Fixed: Hardware/Radio page's Thermals chart (CPU temp) hidden entirely on boards with no fan, same session (2026-08-06).** User noticed RAK V2's Radio page shows no CPU temp readout at all (unlike SenseCap M1, which has both temp + fan duty), correctly guessing it was wrongly gated behind fan config. Root cause confirmed: `GET /api/device/thermals` returned `{"available": False}` whenever `_fan_controller is None`, because temperature *history* sampling only ever happened inside `FanController._poll_once()`'s own loop -- which only runs when `config.fan.enabled` (there's no fan on RAK V2/Chameleon/DIY, only SenseCap M1) -- even though `read_cpu_temp_c()` itself just reads `/sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone0/temp`, a plain Linux thermal-zone file with zero connection to GPIO/PWM/fan hardware. (Note: the instantaneous `cpu_temp_c` on `GET /api/device/metrics` was NOT affected -- it already read temperature independently on every call; only the *history* chart backing the Thermals card was gated.)

**Fix**: new `CpuTempSampler` class (`src/hardware/fan_control.py`) -- same poll-loop/deque-history shape as `FanController`, minus GPIO/PWM/duty entirely, just `(ts, temp_c)` per sample. `server.py`'s startup now always samples temperature: `FanController` (as before) when `config.fan.enabled`, else a `CpuTempSampler` -- both handed to `system_metrics.init_routes()`, which now tracks two separate globals (`_fan_controller` for duty-related fields, `_temp_sampler` for whatever's actually producing history, falling back to `_fan_controller` when that's the one running). `GET /api/device/thermals` gained a `fan_available` bool (`available` now means "temp is being sampled at all", true on every board type; `fan_available` means "and there's a real fan to also report duty for") -- points include a `duty` key only when `fan_available`. `radio_thermals_card.js` updated to match: the whole card hides only when `available` is false; the fan-duty panel independently hides when `!fan_available`, temp panel's own x-axis ticks show whenever it's the only panel (no more assuming a duty panel is always below it).

**Verified**: `ast.parse`/`node --check` clean on all four touched files. Since `system_metrics.py` imports `fastapi` at module level (uninstalled on this Mac), wrote a proper CLAUDE.md-style stub (`sys.modules['fastapi'] = <minimal APIRouter/Depends stub>`) to actually import and exercise the real `thermals()` function end-to-end for all three states (nothing sampling / fan+history / temp-only-no-fan) -- confirmed the exact expected dict shape for each, not just syntax-checked. Updated `tests/test_system_metrics_fan.py` to match the new response shape (`fan_available` key) and added a new `test_temp_only_sampler_reports_available_without_fan` case covering the exact RAK V2 scenario this fixes -- can't run it locally (needs real fastapi) but it's structured identically to the existing passing-on-CI sibling tests in that file. `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`'s Fan Control section and `docs/CHANGELOG.md` (24 bullets in v0.8.0, `ChangelogParser` re-parse clean at 28 sections) updated to document the decoupling.

**Status: logic/syntax-verified only (via stub, not a real FastAPI app), not live-tested.** Next real check is the user's own RAK V2 dashboard after deploying: Radio → Hardware should now show a CPU temp chart with no fan-duty panel beneath it, updating over time same cadence as before.

Gave a brief recommendation first (one combined prompt covering all six, not six separate ones, since they're only ever used together on the Radio tab) before building; user confirmed with the exact section numbers ("6 7 8 9 10 11 all that is rtl-sdr related").

**Implementation**: same `INSTALL_RTLSDR`/`--skip-rtlsdr` pattern as `INSTALL_ARDUINO`/`--skip-arduino` -- prompt placed right after the arduino-cli one (both optional-toolchain questions asked together, upfront, before the long unattended run), default-no when prompted (`[y/N]`, matching the arduino-cli convention the user themselves established), non-interactive runs still default to installing (preserves old always-install behavior for scripted/piped invocations). The whole body of sections 6-11 (everything from `RTLSDR_BUILD_DIR=` through section 11's closing `fi`) wrapped in `if [ "$INSTALL_RTLSDR" = "1" ]; then ... else info "Skipping..." fi`, section header comments kept inside (unlike the arduino-cli wrap, where the section-13 header stayed outside the guard -- no strong reason for the inconsistency, just how each edit happened to land; both read fine).

**Real bug hit and fixed during this edit**: a bulk Python script (read lines, blindly indent every non-blank line by 4 spaces, wrap in if/fi) broke the DVB-blacklist heredoc (`cat > "$DVB_BLACKLIST_FILE" <<'_DVB_BLACKLIST' ... _DVB_BLACKLIST`) -- indenting the closing `_DVB_BLACKLIST` delimiter meant bash could no longer recognize it as the heredoc terminator (a quoted `<<'DELIM'` heredoc requires the terminator at column 0 unless `<<-` with tabs is used), which `bash -n` caught immediately ("unexpected end of file"). Fixed by hand: un-indented the heredoc's body and terminator back to column 0 (verified via `git diff` that the restored body is byte-identical to the pre-edit original), left the surrounding `cat >`/`fi` lines at their correct nested indentation. **Lesson for any future bulk-indent edit on this file**: heredocs are indentation-sensitive and a blind per-line indent will silently produce a script that only `bash -n` (not a visual read) reliably catches -- grep for `<<'` / `<<"` / bare `<<` before doing this again, and always follow with `bash -n`.

**Verified**: `bash -n scripts/install.sh` clean after the fix. Manually confirmed the wrapped block's `if`/`fi` count balances (8 pairs) via `awk`+`grep` over just that line range, and `git diff` confirmed the heredoc body/terminator are back to their original unindented form. `docs/CHANGELOG.md` gained a bullet (28 in v0.8.0 now, `ChangelogParser` re-parse clean at 28 sections) and the top-of-file usage comment gained the `--skip-rtlsdr` line, matching `--skip-arduino`'s existing style.

**Status: syntax-verified only, not run for real** (no Pi/root access from this Mac). Next real check is the user's own next install/upgrade run -- confirm both prompts appear together, `n`/`n` skips all of sections 6-11 and 13 cleanly with the rest of the install completing normally, and the DVB-blacklist heredoc still writes the exact same `/etc/modprobe.d/blacklist-rtlsdr-dvb.conf` content it always has when RTL-SDR IS installed.

**Fixed: rtl-sdr rebuilt from source on every install.sh run, same session (2026-08-06).** User's real install run (the RTL-SDR-support change just landed) showed rtl-sdr cloning+rebuilding from scratch while every other RTL-SDR section (redsea, multimon-ng, rtl_433, dump1090, welle.io) and unrelated tools (meshtastic-cli, esptool) all correctly logged "already installed, skipping". Root cause, spotted directly from the pasted build log: section 6's idempotency check was the one outlier in the whole script -- `ldconfig -p | grep -q librtlsdr` (tests the shared-library CACHE) instead of `command -v <binary>` (tests the actual installed binary on disk), the pattern every other section in this file already uses. The build log's own cmake install output proved the library files were already correctly present ("-- Up-to-date: /usr/local/lib/librtlsdr.so.0" / ".so") even while the ldconfig-cache check falsely reported it missing -- exactly the kind of staleness a cache-based check is vulnerable to (e.g. surviving an SD card image restore/clone taken before the cache was ever refreshed, even though the files themselves came along fine) that a direct binary check isn't. Fixed by switching to `command -v rtl_sdr &>/dev/null` (rtl_sdr is one of the binaries this exact step installs to /usr/local/bin), removing the ldconfig-cache dependency entirely rather than trying to explain/preserve it.

**Verified**: `bash -n scripts/install.sh` clean. Root cause and fix both derived directly from the user's own real build log (not simulated) -- this is a live-diagnosed bug, though the FIX itself is not yet re-run to confirm it actually skips next time. `docs/CHANGELOG.md` gained a bullet (29 in v0.8.0 now, `ChangelogParser` re-parse clean at 28 sections).

**Status: fix is syntax-verified only, not yet re-run.** Next real check is the user's own next install.sh run -- confirm rtl-sdr now correctly logs "already installed, skipping" instead of rebuilding.

**Reticulum (RNS) investigation + ch7 frequency reservation on the concentrator, same session (2026-08-09).** User asked whether their remaining 3 free LoRa channels could run Reticulum (linked reticulumnet.nl/lora/), first as a separate companion node question, then specifically about doing it directly on the meshpoint concentrator with no separate hardware.

**Findings (from reticulumnet.nl + local `~/Software/heltec_v4_reticulum_bron/`)**:
- Mandated LoRa params for that network: **869.463 MHz / BW125 / SF8 / CR5**, chosen specifically to sit clear of Meshtastic/MeshCore -- but that rationale assumes the generic Meshtastic default of 868.0 MHz. This deployment's own actual MT/ME traffic sits at 869.5-869.6 MHz (confirmed via local_meshradar's own packet feed all session), only 40-140 kHz from 869.463 MHz -- worth re-checking for adjacent-channel risk against this specific band plan rather than trusting the generic claim.
- Two viable architectures exist upstream: (1) RNode-as-dumb-modem + a host computer running the real `rns` Python stack talking KISS over USB/serial -- reticulumnet.nl's own default recommendation; (2) a Heltec V4 running `microReticulum_Firmware` standalone (full RNS stack on-device, LoRa on one side + WiFi->TCP bridge to `node.reticulumnet.nl:4242` on the other -- still needs WiFi to reach the wider network, just not a host *computer*). Already have a **pre-built, ready-to-flash** binary for option 2 sitting locally: `heltec_v4_reticulum_TechInc_merged.bin` (pinned to `microReticulum_Firmware @ 1926f15`), pre-configured for the "TechInc" WiFi network, one `esptool write_flash 0x0 ...` away from working -- see that folder's own `BUILD-INSTRUCTIES.md` for the exact command and rebuild-with-different-WiFi steps.
- **Running it directly on meshpoint's own SX1302 concentrator (no companion device) is NOT possible today, but is a real, scoped, buildable feature**, not blocked by hardware:
  - `src/decode/packet_router.py` only dispatches `Protocol.LORAWAN`/`MESHTASTIC`/`MESHCORE` -- no Reticulum decoder or `Protocol.RETICULUM` exists. Retuning a channel alone just makes the SX1302 hear frames it can't classify.
  - The hard part -- real bidirectional SX1302 TX/RX -- already exists and is proven: `src/transmit/tx_service.py`'s `_build_hal_packet()` already drives the concentrator HAL (`extra/sx1302_hal/`) for real Meshtastic/MeshCore sends. This is architecturally the same job RNode/microReticulum firmware does on separate hardware.
  - Correct build approach if/when pursued: add the official `rns` pip package as a dependency (don't reimplement RNS's own crypto/routing/packet framing), write a custom Reticulum `Interface` subclass that calls meshpoint's existing HAL send/receive instead of a serial port, register a new `Protocol.RETICULUM` in the router. Not started -- `rns`/`reticulum` doesn't appear anywhere in requirements or `src/` currently.

**Channel plan change made this session**: `src/hal/concentrator_config.py`'s `eu868_lorawan()` -- ch7 (previously one of three disabled 869.525 MHz placeholders, "nothing LoRaWAN-useful within ±490kHz of RF1") is now enabled at **869.463 MHz**, reserved for Reticulum. Chose ch7 over retuning the active Pager channel (ch9, currently 869.462 MHz FSK -- would have worked frequency-wise too, near-identical to Reticulum's target, but sacrifices working Pager decode for no reason when ch5/ch6/ch7 sit unused). ch5/ch6 remain disabled/spare for later. A multi-SF channel's *default* bandwidth (125 kHz) and SF scan range (SF5-12, auto-detect) already match Reticulum's BW125/SF8 requirement exactly -- no override needed beyond frequency + `enabled=True`, and the IF offset (-62 kHz from RF1's 869.525 MHz anchor) is comfortably within the ±490 kHz hardware limit documented in this same function.

**Known gap, explicitly NOT fixed this session (deferred, per user's own "we'll make the receiving part later")**: even with ch7 enabled at the right frequency, it will not actually receive Reticulum frames yet. `src/hal/sx1302_wrapper.py`'s `set_syncword()` docstring confirms it "overrides ONLY the service channel [ch8] registers... leaving ch0-ch7" on the LoRaWAN public sync word (0x34) set globally via `lorawan_public=True`. ch7 needs an equivalent per-multi-SF-channel sync word override (nothing like that exists today; ch8/Meshtastic's 0x2B override via direct register writes is the only precedent) before it demodulates anything on that channel. So: frequency is reserved and correct; sync word is still wrong (0x34); no decoder exists either. Dashboard's Concentrator Channels table now labels ch7 "Reticulum" correctly (`ChannelConfig.protocol` field added to `concentrator_config.py`, read through instead of the old hardcoded "lorawan" string in `config_routes.py`'s `_concentrator_status()`, plus a matching branch in `radio_concentrator_card.js`) -- user confirmed on a live screenshot.

**Confirmed target sync word value, verified directly from `~/Software/heltec_v4_reticulum_bron/microReticulum_Firmware/` source (not assumed)**: Reticulum's real on-air sync word is the standard "private LoRa network" convention -- **0x12** in the classic single-byte form `sx1302_wrapper.py`'s PEAK1/PEAK2 scheme is built around (same numbering convention as Meshtastic's 0x2B and LoRaWAN's 0x34). `sx127x.cpp:73` (`#define SYNC_WORD_7X 0x12`) confirms this directly for SX127x-class radios. The Heltec V4 itself uses an SX1262 (`sx126x.cpp`), which expresses that same private-network sync word through a different chip-specific 16-bit register pair -- `writeRegister(REG_SYNC_WORD_MSB_6X, 0x14); writeRegister(REG_SYNC_WORD_LSB_6X, 0x24)` (0x1424), a known SX126x-vs-SX127x register-encoding quirk, not a different network convention. (That function even has its own `// TODO: Why was this hardcoded instead of using the config value?` comment from the firmware's own maintainers -- the hardcoding is deliberate/known, not a bug to route around.) **Conclusion: when the ch7 sync-word override gets built, the target value to program on the SX1302 is 0x12** (not the 0x34 it inherits today) -- this replaces the earlier "probably 0x12" guess with a source-verified answer.

**CORRECTION, same session, right after writing the above -- the "just needs a per-channel override like ch8 got" framing is wrong.** Checked the actual SX1302 register map (`extra/sx1302_hal/libloragw/inc/loragw_reg.h`) instead of assuming ch7 could get its own independent sync-word register the way ch8 (the service channel) does. It can't:

```
SX1302_REG_RX_TOP_FRAME_SYNCH0_SF7TO12_PEAK1_POS_SF7TO12   578
SX1302_REG_RX_TOP_FRAME_SYNCH1_SF7TO12_PEAK2_POS_SF7TO12   579
SX1302_REG_RX_TOP_FRAME_SYNCH2_DROP_ON_SYNCH               582
```

These are prefixed `RX_TOP` (the multi-SF demodulator **front-end block shared by all 8 multi-SF channels**) and grouped by spreading-factor range (SF5 / SF6 / SF7-12), not indexed per channel -- there is no ch0..ch7 variant. All 8 multi-SF channels (ch0-ch7) differ only in their own IF/frequency offset; sync-word peak detection for SF7-12 traffic is one shared register pair across all of them. Contrast with ch8 (`SX1302_REG_RX_TOP_LORA_SERVICE_FSK_FRAME_SYNCH0/1_PEAK*`, registers 932/933) -- genuinely separate hardware, which is *why* Meshtastic's 0x2B override on ch8 was even possible.

**Consequence: writing 0x12 to that shared register to "fix" ch7 would apply to ch0-ch6 too**, breaking live LoRaWAN reception on all five active LoRaWAN channels (real TTN traffic uses 0x34, not 0x12). This is a hardware-sharing constraint, not a missing software function -- there is currently no way to give one multi-SF channel its own distinct sync word while the others keep 0x34, unlike what the earlier "add an override, like ch8's" framing implied.

**`DROP_ON_SYNCH` investigated same session, resolved as a dead end.** Register 582 (`SX1302_REG_RX_TOP_FRAME_SYNCH2_DROP_ON_SYNCH`) is defined in `loragw_reg.c`'s register table (1 bit, default 0) but is **never written anywhere in the vendor's own reference driver** outside that table -- it just sits at hardware power-on default, untouched, always. Separately, it's almost certainly not even the right mechanism to look at: LoRa preamble detection works by correlating incoming symbols against a pattern derived from the sync word (that's what `PEAK1`/`PEAK2` -- registers 578/579, shared across ch0-7 -- actually program); a sync-word mismatch generally means the correlator never locks onto/detects the frame at all, rather than "detects it, then a flag decides whether to drop it." So even fully understanding this register's semantics wouldn't route around the real shared-register constraint above. No register was written on any live hardware to reach this conclusion -- pure source reading.

**Channel 9 (the Pager FSK channel) investigated same session as an alternative -- also a dead end, but confirmed for a completely different reason, and it turns out this exact idea already has a prior answer sitting in the code as a comment.** `sx1302_wrapper.py:73-82` (predates this session -- someone already worked this out before, evidently during whatever built ch9's pager support) confirms ch9 genuinely IS independent hardware with its own sync word and config context, unlike ch0-7 -- so the "only one protocol can run there at a time" tradeoff the user proposed would have been architecturally sound from a register-sharing standpoint. It fails for an unrelated, harder reason: that same comment cites the vendor HAL source directly -- *"the hardware capability table in `loragw_sx1302.c` lists `IF_LORA_STD` and `IF_FSK_STD` as two of ten independent, simultaneously-active modems -- not a mode switch."* ch9's modem is physically FSK silicon, permanently, not a reconfigurable LoRa/FSK toggle. Reticulum needs real LoRa chirp modulation (SF8/BW125/CR5); an FSK demodulator cannot decode that at any sync word setting. Confirmed from source, not guessed.

**Conclusion: both realistic leads on the SX1302 concentrator itself are now closed with source-level evidence, not just deferred.** Running Reticulum receive on this concentrator, on any channel, without sacrificing either LoRaWAN (ch0-6, shared sync-word register) or Meshtastic (ch8, the only channel that genuinely has its own swappable sync word) is not possible with the current hardware/HAL. The standalone Heltec V4 route (independent SX1262 radio, zero interaction with any of the above) is no longer just "the safer near-term path" -- it's the only path that doesn't require giving up an existing working protocol on this concentrator.

**Given the above, the standalone Heltec V4 route (already built, sitting in `~/Software/heltec_v4_reticulum_bron/`, independent SX1262 radio, zero interaction with the SX1302's shared multi-SF sync-word constraint) is the safer near-term path if Reticulum needs to actually work before the DROP_ON_SYNCH question gets resolved.**

**Key findings that shaped the design**:
- `microReticulum_Firmware`'s own `platformio.ini` needs **PlatformIO**, not arduino-cli (`custom_variant`/littlefs/symlinked `lib_deps` -- arduino-cli's `boards.txt` can't express any of that) -- ruled out reusing the existing arduino-cli toolchain.

- `platformio.ini` defines **32 environments** (28 espressif32 + 4 nordicnrf52) -- user initially considered "all ESP32 boards", talked down to **just the one owned/used environment** (`heltec_wifi_lora_32_V4-local-udp`) after establishing this project's own companions (Pager/POCSAG/RF-Env) are all single-fixed-board, unlike Meshtastic/MeshCore's legitimate multi-board pickers (which wrap an actual third-party release matrix, a different situation).

User: "no let's stick with the one we have no new stuff."
- `Remote.h` also revealed both SSID and password truncate at a **32-byte fixed buffer** (`strncpy(wr_ssid, NODE_WIFI_SSID, 32)`) -- tighter than WPA2's real 63-char allowance, and silently truncates rather than erroring. Enforced explicitly in both the route (Pydantic validator) and the card (client-side + `maxlength`) rather than letting it fail mysteriously on the device.
- Found and fixed a **real gitignore gap**: `node_config.h` (real WiFi credentials, whatever they are at build time) was tracked in git, unlike every other companion's `secrets.h`. Turned out to be a non-issue this time (TechInc hackerspace's own intentionally-shared guest password, not a real leak) but the gitignore/`.example` fix was still made since the new route now owns writing this file every provision.

Confirmed both ways live: `meshchat.py` run alone (rnsd killed first) happily became its own master and received real announces fine; then a throwaway 40-line test script (`RNS.Reticulum()` + `LXMF.LXMRouter()` + `register_delivery_identity()` + delivery callback, no meshpoint code) run *after* `rnsd -vv` was already up attached cleanly (no "Opening serial port" in its log) and a message sent from meshchat's web UI to the script's printed LXMF address was received and printed -- full round-trip proof the client-attach mechanism works end to end on this exact deployment. **Decision: `rnsd` should always be the master (started first), meshchat/meshpoint's own service always attach as clients** -- decouples the physical RNode from any one app's lifecycle; matches the user's own existing plan to make `rnsd` a systemd service via `install.sh` later (not done yet, started by hand today).

**First live run on the Pi, same session, immediately after the backend build above: caught and fixed a real startup crash.** `reticulum.enabled: true` in `local.yaml` (correctly nested as its own top-level section, sibling to `meshtastic:`, not inside it -- one round of back-and-forth on YAML indentation/colon syntax first, `reticulum:enabled: true` on one line is NOT valid nesting) triggered `PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/home/meshpoint'` on every startup, reproduced twice (once past an unrelated pre-existing `radio.band_plan` unknown-config-key warning the user fixed separately). Root cause: `lxmf_service.py`'s `start()` called `RNS.Reticulum()` with no `configdir`, so it fell back to RNS's own default `~/.reticulum` -- resolved against `$HOME` for the `meshpoint` systemd user, which is `--no-create-home` (same fact that made PlatformIO need `/opt/platformio` instead of a home-relative install, two sessions ago) and has no real home directory for RNS to create its local client-side storage in. Fix: new `config.reticulum.reticulum_config_dir` (default `data/reticulum/rns_config`, under meshpoint's own already-`chown`ed-by-systemd `data/` tree -- confirmed via `scripts/meshpoint.service`'s `WorkingDirectory=/opt/meshpoint` + its `chown -R meshpoint:meshpoint /opt/meshpoint` ExecStartPre, so relative `data/...` paths are guaranteed writable, same as `storage.database_path` already relies on) passed explicitly to `RNS.Reticulum(configdir=...)`. Confirmed this does NOT need to match `rnsd`'s own configdir (the `pi` user's `~/.reticulum`) -- shared-instance discovery is a fixed-local-port check independent of the attaching client's own configdir, which is purely local cache, same pattern `reticulum-meshchat` itself supports via its own `--reticulum-config-dir` flag. `docs/CHANGELOG.md` gained a second bullet for this fix (v0.8.0); stub test's `LxmfService(...)` call signature and fake `RNS.Reticulum` updated to match and re-passed.

**Restarted, permission fix confirmed working -- progressed further, hit a second real bug immediately after.** The log showed the config-dir fix took: `[Notice] Could not load config file, creating default configuration file... Default config file created... data/reticulum/rns_config/config` (i.e. no more PermissionError, and a live real Meshtastic packet even decoded successfully in between), then crashed with `ValueError: signal only works in main thread of the main interpreter`. Root cause: `RNS.Reticulum()`'s own `__init__` calls `signal.signal(SIGINT, ...)` unconditionally, and the code called it via `self._loop.run_in_executor(None, ...)` specifically to keep it off the event loop -- but `run_in_executor`'s default pool runs on a worker thread, and Python only allows `signal.signal()` from the main thread of the main interpreter. The executor wrapping was actively wrong here, not just unnecessary caution. Fix: call `RNS.Reticulum(configdir=...)` directly/synchronously in `start()` instead -- a one-time startup cost during `lifespan()` before the server accepts requests, same as the SX1302 HAL's own synchronous init two lines earlier in the same boot log. `docs/CHANGELOG.md` gained a third bullet; stub test re-passed (the fake `RNS.Reticulum` doesn't care whether it's called via executor or directly, so this didn't need a stub-side change, just re-running to confirm nothing else broke). **Re-restarted, second fix confirmed working -- clean startup, first real live confirmation of the whole backend.** Log showed `lxmf_service: Reticulum instance ready`, `Reticulum: generated new identity`, `Reticulum LXMF service started -- address <8e81e5eb694e923d306f48bff4c6a4ad>`, then `Application startup complete` with no crash -- stayed up through a WebSocket client connecting/disconnecting and a periodic update check. `GET /api/reticulum/status` hit directly by the user, confirmed real (not stubbed) response: `{"enabled": true, "running": true, "available": true, "own_address": "<8e81e5eb694e923d306f48bff4c6a4ad>"}`. `GET /api/reticulum/peers` also hit live, returned real announces from the public network (`lxmf.delivery`/`lxmf.propagation` aspects, one with a real display name "Ratspeak Tunnel", two propagation nodes falling back to their hash -- confirmed expected, propagation-node announces don't carry a display name the way delivery destinations do). **The real FastAPI route registration/pydantic validation in `reticulum_routes.py`, previously only stubbed, is now live-confirmed working.**

**One residual non-fatal issue, not yet root-caused or fixed**: meshpoint's own log recurringly shows `[Error] Could not decode display name in included announce data. The contained exception was: 'bool' object has no attribute 'decode'` (RNS's own bracketed logger format, roughly every 10-40s, tracking ambient network announce traffic). Confirmed this is NOT from `lxmf_service.py`'s own `_on_announce` (which only calls the plain `LXMF.display_name_from_app_data()` helper, wrapped in a silent try/except, and would never produce this exact wording) -- "included announce data" points at a different code path, almost certainly `lxmf`'s own internal propagation-node peer-sync logic (which embeds a nested copy of another destination's announce inside a propagation-node announce), hitting a version-mismatch bug against some real peer's announce shape on the public network. Non-fatal (service keeps running fine through it) -- user explicitly deprioritized chasing this in favor of moving forward on the frontend panel, revisit only if desired later.

**Separately, same session: fixed a real `scripts/install.sh` idempotency bug the user spotted live in its own output** (`'meshcore-cli' already seems to be installed... Not modifying existing installation` from pipx, right after install.sh's own `[INFO] Installing MeshCore CLI...` line -- a giveaway that install.sh's own check had failed even though the tool was already present). Root cause: unlike the Meshtastic CLI/esptool checks in the same section (`pip3 --break-system-packages`, lands on system Python's site-packages, immediately on PATH), MeshCore CLI installs via `pipx`, which symlinks into `~/.local/bin` -- `pipx ensurepath` only adds that to *future* login shells' rc files, not this script's own current PATH, and not guaranteed on the next run's PATH either. So `command -v meshcore-cli` always failed and silently re-ran `pipx install meshcore-cli` on every single install.sh run, harmlessly caught by pipx's own message but still wasted work -- same "idempotency check tests a proxy instead of the real installed thing" shape as the earlier rtl-sdr/`ldconfig` fix, different underlying cause (PATH timing, not a stale cache). Fix: also check pipx's own install record directly, `[ -d "$HOME/.local/share/pipx/venvs/meshcore-cli" ]` (exact path confirmed from the user's own pasted pipx output, not guessed). `bash -n` clean. `docs/CHANGELOG.md` gained a bullet, same v0.8.0 section; `ChangelogParser.parse_file()` re-verified clean, 35 bullets total, all four new ones this session (Reticulum backend, the two Reticulum startup-crash fixes, the meshcore-cli fix) parsed correctly.

**Fixed a real bug (user caught it, not found proactively): a peer's known display name could get blanked out by a later, nameless announce.** `ReticulumPeerRepository.record_announce()` unconditionally `UPDATE`d `display_name` on every announce from an already-known peer, including with an empty string whenever *that particular* announce had no decodable name (no `app_data`, or a decode failure) -- silently losing a name learned from an earlier announce. Fix: only overwrite `display_name` when the new announce actually carries a non-empty one; a nameless re-announce now just bumps `last_seen`/`aspect`, name left untouched. Stub-tested directly (fake DB, not the full `LxmfService` harness): confirmed a nameless re-announce preserves the existing name, and a later named announce still updates it correctly.

**Diagnosed and fixed a real, previously-unknown architectural bug, same session, immediately after: script-to-meshpoint sends silently never arrived, ever -- confirmed by the user across repeated attempts.** `rnsd`'s own log showed repeated `[Error] An error occurred while handling RPC call from local client: digest received was wrong`, growing in burst size (2-3 -> 5-6 per burst) roughly tracking known-destination count (376 -> 973 over the session). Ruled out version mismatch first (`RNS 1.4.2`/`LXMF 1.1.1` confirmed identical across the test script's python3, meshpoint's own venv, and `rnsd` itself -- user ran the comparison, all three matched exactly). `WebSearch`/`WebFetch` against a real markqvist/Reticulum GitHub discussion (#533) confirmed this exact error string is a documented symptom of a shared-instance **RPC client using a different configdir than the master** -- the RPC channel authenticates per-configdir, not just over a fixed local port as this session's own earlier `ReticulumConfig` docstring incorrectly assumed (written several turns before this was caught -- corrected in the docstring itself, see below). Root cause, confirmed by elimination: `lxmf_service.py` uses `config.reticulum.reticulum_config_dir` (`data/reticulum/rns_config`, meshpoint's own self-contained dir, chosen earlier this session specifically to dodge the `/home/meshpoint` `PermissionError`) -- a **different** directory than `rnsd`'s own (a user's `~/.reticulum`), unlike both throwaway test scripts (which used RNS's bare default, landing on the same dir `rnsd` uses since both run as the same `pi` user). This explains the full asymmetry cleanly: dashboard-to-script sends worked (meshpoint's outbound RPC apparently tolerated the mismatch enough to queue/send), script-to-meshpoint never did (inbound delivery notification over that same broken channel never reached meshpoint) -- confirmed conclusively via a live screenshot showing all 3 "conversations" in the Messages tab were actually meshpoint's own *outbound* sends to 3 different past ephemeral script identities, zero real inbound messages ever recorded, across the entire session.

**User explicitly rejected the interim fix (granting `meshpoint` cross-user group access into a `pi`-owned directory)** as non-general -- "later on the user wont have it in /pi but only meshpoint" -- correctly identifying that real deployments won't have a `pi` user manually running `rnsd` by hand at all. Agreed this session's original "later, make rnsd a systemd service" plan (mentioned as far back as the very first `rnsd -vv` discovery) should happen now, done properly, rather than patched around with a permission hack. **Also explicitly corrected a real design mistake in the first draft of this plan**: initially proposed a hard `Wants=`+`After=rnsd.service` on `meshpoint.service` itself -- user caught that meshpoint's core function (concentrator/mesh capture/dashboard) has nothing to do with Reticulum and must never depend on it, since `config.reticulum.enabled` is opt-in/false by default. Fixed to a **soft `After=rnsd.service` alone** (ordering only, no `Wants=`/`Requires=` -- systemd starts meshpoint fine regardless of whether rnsd exists, is enabled, or fails); same opt-in philosophy extended to `install.sh`'s own new section (prompted, `--skip-rnsd`, not automatic).

**Also caught and fixed a real, silent bug in `ChangelogParser` usage while re-verifying this session's own new bullet**: `_BULLET_RE` (`src/api/update/release_notes.py`) requires the bold headline to contain **zero** `*` characters (`[^*]+?` -- not even a nested single-asterisk italic span), and the first draft of the rnsd-service bullet used `*to*` (italic) inside its headline. This didn't raise an error or a parse exception -- the line just silently failed to match and was dropped from the parsed output entirely, with the overall bullet count staying unchanged (37 before and immediately after adding it), which is exactly the kind of silent-failure shape that's easy to miss without an explicit re-count check. Caught only because this session has been re-verifying bullet counts after every changelog edit as standing practice -- fixed by removing the italic markup from the headline (kept it in the detail text, which has no such restriction: `detail` group is unrestricted `.*`). Scanned the rest of the changelog file afterward for the same failure mode (every other `- **` line individually matches `_BULLET_RE` fine); a separate ~10-bullet raw-vs-parsed discrepancy exists file-wide but predates this session's edits entirely (likely older sections with a header format `_VERSION_RE`/`_UNRELEASED_RE` doesn't recognize) -- out of scope, not investigated further. **Worth remembering for any future changelog edit in this repo: never put italic (`*word*`) markup inside a bullet's bold headline** -- it silently vanishes from the parsed release notes (the dashboard's own "What's New" preview) with no error anywhere.

**Live-tested the same session, immediately after -- confirmed the core fix works, surfaced one more real bug in the process.** User deployed manually (not via install.sh yet): `pkill -f "rnsd -vv"` (killed the old hours-long-running manual instance), copied `rnsd.service` in, `systemctl enable --now rnsd`, confirmed clean startup via `journalctl` (backbone-only, since `rnode_serial_port` wasn't set in `local.yaml` yet -- expected, not a bug), then `systemctl restart meshpoint`. meshpoint's own restart log showed **zero digest/RPC errors** attaching to the fresh shared instance -- first clean attach of the whole session.

**Immediate side-effect, correctly self-diagnosed by the user before I even explained it**: the throwaway test script (still pointed at its old default `/home/pi/.reticulum`, never updated) was now talking to a *different, no-longer-running* Reticulum instance than the one meshpoint had just moved to (`/opt/meshpoint/data/reticulum/rns_config`) -- a fresh, different-shaped digest mismatch than before, but a direct and predictable consequence of the very fix just deployed, not leftover mess. Rewrote the test script to point at the shared configdir explicitly and run as the `meshpoint` user (`sudo -u meshpoint /opt/meshpoint/venv/bin/python3 ...`, storage moved to `/tmp/` to dodge a further three-way permission cascade: `pi` can't write meshpoint's dir, root's bare `python3` has no `RNS` installed, `meshpoint` can't read a script sitting in `pi`'s home -- resolved by staging the script in `/tmp` and using meshpoint's own venv explicitly).

**Once that was sorted: web-to-script delivery confirmed clean, zero digest errors** -- real, repeatable proof the shared-configdir fix is the actual root cause fix, not a coincidence. **Script-to-meshpoint hit a different, unrelated failure**: `Unknown destination -- no announce received from it yet`, even for a peer the script had *just* received a real message from seconds earlier. Root-caused correctly without needing another external search: `RNS.Identity.recall()` only searches the announce-based known-destinations table, and receiving a message over a Link doesn't necessarily populate that same table -- meshpoint's LXMF service had announced once at its own startup (13:56), before this fresh script instance ever attached (14:02), so the script's local cache was genuinely cold for meshpoint specifically despite having just talked to it.

**Fixed properly in the real product code, not just the test script** (`src/reticulum/lxmf_service.py`'s `send_message()`): now calls `RNS.Transport.request_path(dest_hash)` and retries `Identity.recall()` for up to 5s (`_PATH_REQUEST_RETRIES=5` x `_PATH_REQUEST_POLL_INTERVAL_S=1.0`) before raising, instead of failing on the very first empty cache check -- same pattern `reticulum-meshchat` and other real RNS apps use, explicitly framed as correct production behavior (a peer whose announce is momentarily stale should still be reachable), not a testing-only workaround. New `LxmfService.announce()` + admin-only `POST /api/reticulum/announce` + an "Announce now" button on the dashboard's Reticulum page header (reuses the shared `#r-toast` pill `app.js`'s own `_toastAdminRequired()` already established, rather than inventing a second notification mechanism) -- lets a stale announce be refreshed on demand, directly addressing the same underlying cold-cache problem from the other side (the user's own "maybe an announce button?" suggestion).

**Verified on the Mac**: `node --check`/`py_compile` clean on all touched files. Stub test extended with two new scenarios -- a cold-cache destination that resolves after exactly 2 failed `recall()`s (confirms `request_path()` gets called exactly once and the retry loop exits as soon as `recall()` succeeds, not after exhausting all 5 tries) and a destination that never resolves (confirms `ValueError` is still raised cleanly, doesn't hang or silently drop the send) -- both passing, plus a direct check that `announce()` calls through to the underlying source's own `announce()`. `docs/CHANGELOG.md` gained one more bullet describing both the request_path fix and the announce button together; `ChangelogParser.parse_file()` re-verified clean, 39 bullets under v0.8.0. **Live-tested immediately after, confirmed working -- this closes out the entire session's Reticulum arc.** User clicked the new "Announce now" button, then retried the script's send -- the script's own one-shot `recall()` check still failed on the very first attempt ("Unknown destination") since the test script was never updated with the same request_path/retry logic, but succeeded immediately after the manual announce refreshed meshpoint's presence ("Sent to 5771b31be2e41bdfed57ad65aeb03ee5: \"hice works\""). **Real CI failure, caught by the user pasting the GitHub Actions log (PR #583): `ruff check` failed with `E402` (x3) on `lxmf_service.py`**, introduced by this session's own earlier `try`/`except ImportError` wrapping of `RNS`/`LXMF`. Root cause: the conditional import block sat between `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` and the module's other `from src....` imports -- ruff tolerates a top-level conditional-import `try`/`except` itself (standard optional-dependency idiom), but not plain imports appearing after one. Fixed by reordering: all real imports contiguous at the top, `logger = ...` next, the `RNS`/`LXMF` try/except last (nothing follows it, so nothing can be "after" it). Verified two ways: installed the exact CI-pinned `ruff==0.15.1` in a throwaway venv (not a newer local ruff -- CI's own workflow comment explains 0.16.0+ broadened the default ruleset with new rules like `UP045`, so a newer version would show unrelated noise) and got a clean pass on the whole `src/ tests/` tree, plus re-ran the full existing stub test suite (all 8 assertions) to confirm the reorder changed nothing functionally. Also caught (by the same real ruff run, not proactively) a genuine unused-import `F401` in the brand-new `rnode_firmware_routes.py` (a leftover `from pathlib import Path` from an earlier draft that no longer needed it) -- fixed before it could become a second CI failure. `docs/CHANGELOG.md` gained a bullet; `ChangelogParser` re-verified clean, 40 bullets under v0.8.0.

**Built:**

**Documentation catch-up, same session**: realized mid-stream that the entire native-Reticulum feature (built much earlier this session) had never made it into `README.md`'s "What's Different in This Fork" or `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`, despite `CLAUDE.md`'s own standing rule that larger features need both.
